I'd have to learn more about the practical, economic side, manage production if I'm selling products, etc. The good news is that the more you integrate your personal skills and interests into your business, the more likely you’ll be to enjoy the process and stick with it.

So, Alan's beard looks more like a wild animal these days.      Indeed. It's got quite a bit of character. Reminds me of the wild look I had when I was writing some of my novels.      I think you two of you have quite the... impressive beards.      Yeah, well, let's not make it a competition, but I think Alan takes the prize.      Baw! So, big!      You know, I had this wild writer’s look even when I was a publisher. Women thought I was quite dashing with my beards and glasses. But when it came to engaging with family, it was a different story.      Now that was before the years of youth. Family engagement is about being present, not the length of your beard.      Exactly. It’s all about balance. I used to work, you know, but now I’m home with little Timmy. It’s amazing how his world centers around food deliveries and computing games.      And food and compy!      I remember how that was different for us. When our children were young, it was more about... engagement through storytelling, playing outside together, and a focus on school.      Ah, yes. Schools. There's a bit of a shortage of places in Cambridge and it's been quite a challenge for some families. You know, it's especially tough on families like... ...ours, that are trying but also navigating other complex issues.      Absolutely. And it seems even harder when you’re unemployed or retired like us. The system can be very unforgiving. I heard there’s this new Polish family in the neighbourhood. They're getting settled but I bet they’ve got their own struggles finding a school for their children too.      Indeed. It's all interlinked: housing shortages, school shortages, finding work or engaging in the community. Speaking of 40s, we should plan a little party for you all at some point. A celebration for being functional successful adults living through these times, despite everything.      A 40s party? With all the stress and chaos, I wouldn't mind some cake and family cheer for a change.      Cake! Fold cake!      And if we can manage that, I might just write a short story about it.      And I'll try to remember recipes from my days as a teacher.

Ah, I'm so glad we could catch up without the kids this time. It's been ages since we've had an adult conversation about anything other than what they need for school or whether the tea is ready. You look well though, Alison! How's your job going? Thanks, Sue – I am doing all right, just trying to keep on top of everything. Does your son still get the car park passes for the school run from that same place? Yes, he does. He even volunteers there now sometimes. Speaking of which, I had to go back to Birmingham for a sales meeting last week and it was a nightmare with the traffic and parking. And you won’t believe it, but I saw Mr. Jenkins from our sixth form at the station! He’s not changed a bit. We talked for ages. It was like no time had passed at all. That is weird! The sixth form still feels like yesterday for me. I remember the politics project we did together. I wonder if we also voted the same way in the referendum. Ah, the referendum – I was all for staying in. I never thought it would actually happen. But, I guess it's all part of life, innit? I'm just relieved we're still working and can afford the basics. Same here. Well, I guess the real worries come when you're not well or need to rely on others, which reminds me – how's your health? You mentioned something about the drive last time we spoke. Yes, I've had a bit of trouble with my back again. Just one of those things that comes with age, I suppose. But it's manageable, just means I have to be a bit more careful with exercise and sit-ups. You need to be careful, but also don't let it get you down too much – it can be debilitating if you let it. I've been trying to do more light exercises myself, got a bit of a routine going and it’s been really uplifting.

Ah, I'm losing my mind with Twitter. Just saw someone online who was whining about their job and social media. It's like, can't people just enjoy their day off rather than everyone else's misery? Are we all that bored with our own lives? [laughs] You know, questions like this kind of make me wonder if social media is just a way for us to broadcast our discontent or seek validation rather than genuine connections. I'm right there with you, though. I found myself doing the same thing for my work — sharing interesting articles and discussing them alongside my peers. It became routine, almost therapeutic in its predictability, but sometimes you can't help but question the value of all this. Therapeutic? You're not just any Communications Manager, you're a Director of Studies. Tell me, in your position, do you find that social media has helped or hindered your organization's mission? On one hand, Twitter has been incredible for spreading important research studies and news within our academic circles. It's allowed us to engage with a wider audience than ever before. But at the same time, it's a constant battle to maintain what you'd call 'brand voice' and not get sucked into the rabbit hole of endless online debates. I understand the need to stay relevant and communicate with wider audiences, but it feels like a double-edged sword. For my work, I try to use social media strategically — like sharing key projects or sentiments that tie into our community engagement efforts. But for personal use... I'd love to take a break sometimes. Doesn't it seem we're all really good at maintaining our online personas, but when it comes to real-life relationships and face-to-face conversations, we struggle? Agreed. I've talked to colleagues who literally feel anxious about logging off social media for fear of missing out or the potential career impact of not being constantly 'on'. As someone who just tried to relax over the weekend without checking my phone every ten minutes, I can say it was... liberating. Yet, as soon as Monday hit, it's back to tweeting about the latest findings for the department. It's almost unconscious at this point. I've noticed that too. The influence of habits. But for me, I've started just using Twitter for work-related stuff

Hey, I'm starving. I need something to eat. We have anything easy today? Oh, yes! I made a giant portion of pasta chicken the other day. I can heat that up for you. Or if you're in the mood, we could even cook something together – do you have any preferred kind of dish today? Actually, the pasta sounds amazing. But honestly, I just want something quick and easy – and of course, delicious! [laughs] Me too! I've heard loads about this new vegan recipe. You game for it? Or, if you want a hybrid lazy-day kind of dinner, we could just add some roasted veggies to the pasta. What do you think? I'm game for anything that ends in "delicious" and doesn't involve making me do too much. [laughs] Fair enough. Okay, so pasta with roasted veggies it is then. Perfect! Can I grab a glass of wine while you rustle that up? Of course. Which wine would you like? I have a new bottle of Sauvignon Blanc that is really nice. Or is the red still your go-to? You know me too well. The red is the way to go tonight. Do we also have cheese? Maybe some crackers? Yes, I think there's some cheese in the fridge and some crackers too. There's also a new kind of hummus I picked up that is supposed to be quite tasty. Sound good? Sounds heavenly. Just throw everything on the table and let it be a feast. Deal. While we wait for the food, can you tell me how your weekend was? More specifically, how are your patients? Oh it was a tough weekend. One of my patients had a bit of a breakdown but we managed to get through it okay and she's stable now. But it's always a reminder of just how tough our job can be. Definitely. I've had friends in similar situations and it’s always so hard to see. But, it truly sounds like such an important job you’re doing. Thanks. It's definitely challenging. Did you have a good weekend? Actually, I've had a bit of a disagreement with a friend. We were supposed to go to a concert but they backed out. Totally fine if they didn't feel up to it but they texted me a whole novel on why they couldn't make it.

Ah, I'm so glad we could all come together like this. It feels like ages since we've done something together. How are you all doing? I'm good, thanks for asking. It's lovely to catch up with everyone. Especially now, after what’s been a pretty chaotic month. Exactly! We could all use a break and a good meal. I’ve been thinking, with David's visit coming up, we should discuss the arrangements. Has there been any progress? Ah, keeps coming up. To be honest, not much. We'll need to book a room, figure out the dates. I’ve been meaning to look into that. I’ve done a bit of research, just to help out. There’s a fairly decent B&B just on the outskirts of town. It’s not luxury, but it’s clean and they have decent rooms. That sounds good. It’s important that David feels welcome, after all. What about the dates? Did you guys discuss that? Let me check. I think between the 15th and the 25th is the general time frame. But it would be good to finalize. I’ve looked at the calendars and it seems like we can confirm the 20th. It’s peak holiday time, but I found a few options available online. Twenty first, then. Should work out fine. Can you make the booking? I’m a bit out of practice with this sort of thing these days. Sure thing. I’d be glad to. And we’ll need to figure out the meals. I was thinking we could do a big family dinner here on the 20th? Just to make sure we get everyone together before David leaves. That sounds wonderful. And who’s handling the festivities? Our culinary guru, I presume? Speaking of food, your new car is still a topic of discussion, isn’t it? How’s it been treating you? Oh, the car. It’s been fantastic. It’s done all right for its first trip out – I borrowed it for a small trip down to Plymouth. Just what I needed – it’s so much more comfortable than the old one. And it has that nice, versatile space for when family comes over. Yeah, plus you won’t have to worry about getting parking in town anymore. I’ll make sure to send a reminder to book a spot by then.

Ah, I'm losing patience. I swear, it's almost as though these gods of Spanish don't want us to master their language at all! I've been trying to tackle these verb conjugations for what feels like an eternity. Oh, you're not alone, dear. I'm with you all the way on this. It's like those verbs refuse to stick. I spent three hours on just the past tense of regular verbs and right now, I'm wading through irregular verbs. All very well for Cervantes or whoever, but keeps changing backwards and forwards! I know, right? Like they thought up new rules for fun at some stage! And what's with this 'vosotros' stuff? We only just got down to proper 'yo, tu, el, ella' and then bam, 'vosotros' making life complicated again. And to think we were chuffed at getting the simple 'I love you' right—'Te amo'. Oh, 'Te amo', that's good progress. But yes, it gets so tangled between Spain, Latin America, and even Portugal throwing in variations. For me, it's the accents too. Spanish from Spain, then there's their 'th' in the south, and the 'z' that sounds like 's' in certain regions. It's like the language has its own identity crisis! Absolutely. And don't get me started on the pronunciation. I mean, I know 'c' sounds 'k', 'z' and sometimes 's', but 'll' is still a mystery to me. Sometimes it sounds 'y' and other times like 's' followed by a palatal click. It's like the lisping kind of 's' but then, not really. Seems like the Morecambe accent couldn’t help us there, could it? The 'll' in 'Bill' is never going to prepare us for 'll' in 'llamar', for instance. But you know, it's all part of the fun. Learning any language is like getting to know a new person—there are quirks, sometimes it takes time before you're sure of what they mean or what they'll say next. And that's what keeps me going. Besides, the little successes along the way make the frustration worth it. Remember when we managed to hold a short conversation without realising we used the subjunctive correctly once or twice? Not often, but occasionally. Oh, yes! I remember when you suddenly quoted something in Spanish from memory and I thought, "Wait, that's her?

Dad, I'm going to scan all these papers first, so we have digital copies. It’s easier to save and organize that way. Also, I don't know much about old banking documents, but I've studied a bit of corpus linguistics at uni. Maybe I can help? That’s a good idea, son. I've had these papers for years, and never really looked through them. It's about time we sort it all out. As for language, I've never been much of a word-whiz like you. But I always admired how Kelly Brook could get a certain message across with hardly any words. Haha! Well, while we're on the subject of language, today I used this really cool online tool to compile all the flying-related expressions in English. So, for example, we can pin down places from 'at the eleventh hour' to 'on standby'. And funnily enough, 'on a wing and a prayer' is still being used—even though that sounds like it comes straight out of a 90s movie. You're so into language, it's amazing! I've always admired people like you who really understand the nuances. So, can this scanner do PDF and image files? And how do we start making different files to organize everything? It should handle PDFs without a problem. In fact, I recommend exporting documents to PDF to make them searchable and keep the formatting. As for organizing, how about we make a couple of folders based on what type of document it is—like 'bank', 'insurance', 'utility bills'. Then within those, we can make subfolders based on year or month. That sounds good. Okay, where's the scanner and the papers that need to be scanned? Right here. I just need to make sure everything is tidied up and flat, so it doesn’t get creased in the scanner. One of the papers looks like it's from your old job. Is that right? Yeah, that's from when I worked at customer services. I guess changing the business model and restructuring meant I was let go after a decade… Not that I regret it, but it’s nice to look back sometimes. It’s important to keep these kind of records, though. Might be for insurance or tax purposes later on. Indeed. You could even say it’s like saving boarding pass scans after a trip.

Did you catch what I was saying about the petrol station on Milton Street? Milton Street? Right, yes, I think so. You were saying something about the staff being friendly but the questions they asked kind of seemed over the top? Yeah, exactly right. They asked me to show ID, fill out this very long form for some kind of promo, and wanted to know if I would let them text me my receipts to my phone, which to be honest seemed quite invasive. Not like the old days, is it? Everyone seems to want some kind of digital following now. Exactly. I just want to fill up my car and get outta there! Yeah, spot on. Although it is good for deals and discounts. You never know, you could end up saving next time. True, true. But it just feels quite... Big Brother-y at times. Modesty, while the system observes. You’re quite the one for bringing up oddly placed references. Well, technology is certainly changing the way we interact with companies, isn’t it? Evolution of service. Efficiency and convenience, really. But you never know, maybe the benefits outweigh the invasion of privacy for some people? It's a trade-off, isn't it? I kind of see it as this unspoken agreement where I give up a little privacy in exchange for the potential chance to save money or get exclusive offers. But it’s just the fact that they're collecting all this data without necessarily asking our consent in a way we fully understand... or can opt out of easily if we want to. While you’re on that note, any particular thoughts about bikers on the motorway? Or maybe it's a bit more of a 'petrol station saga' for you? Ah! Bikers. Well, I’ve always found them a bit... daunting to be around when I’m driving, especially if it’s one those big groups. You find bikers intimidating? I thought you'd be one of those people who’d be all for freedom on the road. Oh, I totally get the appeal and freedom they have, but when you're sitting in a car and suddenly any of the five lanes can become a bit impromptu "bike lane" because they're moving like they have the right of way everywhere... it gets a bit frustrating, sometimes. I know what you mean.

We've got Andy Murray today. He's quite possibly the most decorated British tennis player of all time, right? Yeah, his game skill isn’t matched by many. Who's Andy Murray again, right? He's a very successful tennis player. One of the best from the UK alongside Fred Perry. Oh, right, okay. I used to play tennis in school. Sentiments of envy and accomplishment when he won Wimbledon. Did you? Well, well. And what made you enjoy it? The tactical aspect mainly. That's interesting. I used to play too, casually. But Andy's dedication and strategic play - that's really something to admire, especially he's from our general vicinity. So, why do you say he's the most decorated? One of the most decorated in modern times, at least. Three Wimbledon titles, Olympic Gold, and a US Open among others. Exactly. And dedication right, Alex? There's no shortcuts in tennis or anything really if you want to excel. Yeah, I get it. But it's not just about the titles. He's known for his work ethic, mental resilience. During his time off from playing due to the hip surgery, he was just as dedicated to his recovery and returning to the sport. Which is another valuable lesson, Alex. There's more to life than just winning or losing. Persistence and dedication to goals, no matter the setbacks. Makes sense, I guess. I'm not in a rush to become a pro, but it's cool to take notes from the best. It does give some perspective, doesn't it? And for what it's worth, even the best players still have ups and downs. Oh, we could definitely tell you about that! From watching the matches, you don't see all the hard work. Spot on. I think that's often what young players or aspiring players miss - the unseen sacrifices and the effort. So, tennis is about the journey, not just reaching the top? Precisely. And it's not just about tennis. You apply those lessons to anything you're interested in. Mmm. Being passionate and dedicated, learning from each failure or setback as much as from each win. So, this might apply to school too then? Absolutely. Just taking it one step at a time, aiming high but understanding you’ll face challenges. And knowing that even with challenges, you have the strength to push through if you're genuinely interested.

Who took all the napkins yesterday? Did anyone else notice they look like underpants? [laughs] Omg, talked about that with the tea towels last week but I didn't see the napkins! I'm sure they must have been a gag gift from whoever did the shopping. You two and your sense of humor! [Speaker_1, giggles] I wish I could have seen you using them, would've been quite the sight! [laughs] Can you imagine? Dinner with napkins that look like... well, you know! Well, it's all in good fun, dear. I'm more worried about the turkey. Is that the one I marinated for you, [Uncle/Partner]? Was it enough? Yeah, [Uncle/Partner], your turkey always tastes amazing. I remember when [Speaker_1] was younger, you used to get creative with how you cooked it. What was that crazy recipe you used last year? Mm, yeah, that was the "Stockport Secret Sauce" turkey. I'm a bit too old for that now, but it was good, right? [laughs] I assumed we'd grown out of such things. Although, if anyone’s still into it, I'm game! Maybe [Speaker_2] can make it for us next year? I'd take that over some of the fancy things they do today. Back in my day, it was all about simplicity and love. That's true, [Speaker_5]. We don't need anything fancy to have a good time. How the family spends Christmas always reminds me of how our priorities should be. Speaking of simplicity, the Queen’s speech is one of my favorite things about Christmas. I just love the tradition of it, even if it can drag on a bit at times. For me, it's the music. Last year, my uni friends had a party and we danced so much that my legs felt like jelly on Boxing Day. Yeah, that sounds like fun! Though, after [Speaker_4] just mentioned the Queen, I've so much respect for her dancing! Can we see a clip of her and Prince Philip's waltz again after dinner? Haha, only if you two promise to show me those new dance moves [Speaker_3] was talking about. [laughs] You two would make a fine pair on the dance floor. Though, I'm more for staying on my feet long enough to hear the wishbone-breaking ceremony. We always have our own little traditions. I still can't believe [Speaker_1] never won the wishbone break.

Hey everyone, welcome back to the nest! How was your day? I've been working on that new project all morning. Ah, I'm so glad we could catch up without the children this evening. They're still out at that swimming class. How was your day? It was okay. Don't you just hate the fact that sometimes it's just a bunch of boxes to tick and nothing actually gets improved? Exactly! Right, so I'm planning on going to Primark after uni today. I've got so many essentials to pick up and it'll be such a buzz seeing what they've got in the summer range. Have you two been there yet? You thinking of pairing them with something light and breezy or a bit more... statement? I'm thinking statement this time round. A nice summer party dress might finally get some use. You know, something that makes you feel 'you' but still comfortable in the heat. [smiling] Well, I’ve got just the thing then. Turquoise doesn’t come in that many summer hells though, does it? I might struggle finding a pair that'd match. Maybe that’s the point? Something different that stands out, you know? Speaking of which, are we doing anything special tonight? Like, I mean after shopping that is. I wasn’t planning anything, but maybe we could suggest grabbing drinks? Like at that new zero-waste bar on the corner of 5th and Bridge? I heard it’s got a great vibe and almost entirely plastic free. Sounds amazing! I love supporting places that care about the planet plus, the vibes are usually better in those places.

Ah, I'm so glad we could take a break from everything this morning. It's so chaotic these days isn't it? Agreed. There's always something. I don't remember life ever being quite this...never-ending. You're kind of young to be feeling that way, though, aren't you? I wish I could roll back the clock a bit sometimes, you never know what's around the bend. You know what's odd? We talk about historical periods and technologies all the time, but if we had to pick anything – any time to visit for just a day - I think we'd choose the late 1920s. Really? What about the places we've always wanted to go? True, but the 20s were such a fascinating time. The music, the art, the fashion – everything was very alive. And the social changes underway. It's a time when so much was in flux. Plus, I think it would be interesting to experience a time without this...this immediacy we have now. Absolutely. Where anything can happen at any moment, while the rest of the world watches. It's overwhelming sometimes. And the people. The characters from that era - Churchill, Wilde, Picasso – imagine bumping into them at a masquerade ball. Can you imagine walking into a party and seeing Charles and Diana there, but when they were still just a couple? But it's not just about the people we'd meet. The food, the drinks, the whole atmosphere... The jazz, the cocktails, the whole glamour of it! I'd love that. And maybe getting a newspaper or hearing a radio broadcast by someone like Orson Welles for the first time. It's really fun to sit here and imagine all this. Like, what if – on that day – we also managed to attend an imaginary party hosted by a certain American writer? Ernest Hemingway! Can you see us there, sipping on mojitos and hearing him and Fitzgerald debate about life and literature? It's like... having our own little retreat from reality. I wonder, if we came back now, would anything be different? Probably not. But I think we'd come back feeling more...grounded. I guess our versions of escapism are purely historical. I wonder what the soul mates of the past would make of our own journey. Though we mostly keep our spiritual journeys, and such, to ourselves, don't we?

Ah, I'm so glad we could catch up without any distractions. I've been meaning to reach out for ages. How are you, sweetie? Honestly, I'm just tired of work! The civil service never seems to stop, and this year's staff shortage – ugh, it's been overwhelming. Between the pandemic and now the holidays, people are taking more time off than usual! Oh, I know the feeling. Sales won’t stop just because it’s Christmas. But even with all that, I still managed to sneak in some knitting time this week! You always seem to find time for your knitting, don’t you? I wish I could. Between admin and HR, even lunch seems to be scheduled. Ah, but that’s another project on the way. I started a little side business doing bespoke knitted items – its more relaxing than actual work. Ooh, knitting? That sounds similar to my mum’s hobby. But I never got into it. Honestly, it started because I kept bringing knitted items to work – scarves, hats, mittens – and everyone would want one. A friend suggested turning it into a little sideline. It’s been a fun way to unwind and earn a bit extra, and all those knitting patterns and clips online help a lot. That’s brilliant! I’ve always wondered how people manage to do two jobs or work while having hobbies. During exams time or just regular work periods, it feels like there’s just enough time for work, sleep, and mealtime. I totally understand that stress. Speaking of skills, did either of you know that some people are actually making money from podcasting or YouTube channels now? I’ve seen a few where Brits are sharing cultural tidbits or language differences… Like, I was listening to one where they talked about stereotypes in everyday conversation. Funny and enlightening at the same time. Oh, yes! I’ve listened to some of those. It’s fascinating, isn’t it? How one aspect of language can lead to so many cultural misunderstandings. I mean, I swear my relatives are complete masters at this. Do you remember that time at the pub when my uncle kept saying "gutted" to mean really disappointed?

Hey guys, did you hear about James and Emily?? They's moving out of our uni halls; they just realized they can't afford it no more. Yeah, I did. They've been struggling. Especially James. He's from a working class family and this is his first year away from home. It's rough. I saw Emily yesterday. She was pretty bummed about it all. And to think they were just discussing renting a house actually, before the bill came in. Oh wow. That's a real shock for them, especially at this time of year. I mean, we've all noticed the price of everything. I heard about the tax rise for graduates, too. I'm terrified. Yeah, just like the Sports Direct news. I bet they thought we were in for a good year, but now - oh boy. What's that gonna do for our budget? It's unfair, isn't it? We pay our taxes, we study hard, and then this. And the worst bit is, people barely discuss it. It's like it’s the elephant in the room at uni. For sure. We all complain about it, but no one seems to do much about it. I mean, I'm sure we’re not the only ones. Exactly. It’s the university and its resources that should be trying to help us more. I mean, we’re their future customers for uni fees, right? Yeah, and then there’s the football silly isn’t it? Like, really? The team is awful, and the tickets are a rip-off. I know, doesn’t help that the team is in the relegation zone too. And then to make matters worse, the prices for just about everything else are going up. Seems like the commerce class we had missed one thing: real-life. Okay, okay, let's ease off on football for a bit. What about our trip to Edinburgh next week? That should cheer us up. Yeah, definitely. That's on my bucket list. Plus, maybe we should all start hunting for that cheaper book for our next reading list. Genius, let’s do that. I’ve found one for half the price on some student platform. Again, it’s about those small wins, isn’t it? Even just the £5 saved can make a difference in weekly budget. Definitely. And speaking of things we don’t want to spend money on, thinking about shopping.

Right, so everyone's seen the photos from Grandma's hospital stay. I just can't believe how quickly they were able to stabilize her. The staff was amazing, talked about her as if she was family. You two remember when mum got her tattoo? Wasn't it just last year? Oh yes! I was so surprised she took the leap. But she’s been talking about getting one for years. It must have felt like a big deal to finally actually do it. Yeah, and it’s so cool! Can we see it sometime? Definitely, but let’s actually wait for her. I heard she’s planning to show it off at the next family gathering. She’s got quite the spirit. Speaking of spirits, have you all tried the house wine here? It’s quite pleasant. It is, isn’t it? Not bad at all. Can we maybe get another bottle when we decide what to have for dessert? Sure, why not? And maybe next time we talk, I’ll ask about that new supermarket that just opened near home. Mum mentioned they have some great deals. Oh, yes. I'll definitely ask her while I'm there. They've got online shopping too, which is a real help sometimes. Speaking of convenience, have you noticed how easily you can get around with a moped here? A bit chaotic, but it’s good for the area. True, it would be quite handy to have one if we were staying longer. Plus, it’s better for the environment… Yeah, and we could do more cycling or even join a local sports club. Did anyone hear about the new exercise classes the school is offering? Actually, I did, and I'm considering joining. It'll be good to get some exercise in. It's great for your mental and physical health, but also great for a social life. You never know who you might meet. Speaking of meeting people – I’ve been trying to convince mum to join FaceBook again. She uses just her phone for messages but I think she’d really enjoy catching up with old friends or family members who aren’t able to visit as often. Ah, she’s almost gone over to the 'I'll never use social media' camp. I’ve tried showing her, but she just doesn’t trust these things. That’s understandable, but it’s just about being cautious.

Ah, I'm so glad we could all meet up after that Cornwall trip. It's been nearly a week now and I've still got such sweet memories buzzing about in my head. You're right, John. It really was a lovely trip. I must say, this is the kind of weekend getaway we need more often. It isn't always easy for us to organize such things considering our... "situations" but it's so worth it, right? Absolutely, Sam. I especially enjoyed the part where we volunteered at that YHA place. It was quite the experience, seeing the lighthouse and all those crabs you spoke of. Oh, the crabs! They were everywhere in Padstow, just like you said. I've never seen so many in my life. And that village, it's like stepping back in time, isn't it? Exactly, and it did me good being out of this old house and talking to people. I've been quite... ensconced, shall we say, since we couldn't work any longer. Volunteering's a good idea, I think. For sure. We could keep it on the list for next year or so, maybe even different parts of the country. There's a river camping trip I've been wanting to do in Yorkshire. It's called the 'Yorkshire in a day' – cycling, followed by a river cruise. Ah, cycling. I used to love that when I was younger. Almost tempted to dust off my old bike, but I fear it would be a bit of an effort now. Still, love the idea. Maybe we can make a smaller version, John. We could do the lighthouse walk again? Just a small group of us. I do miss walking and fresh sea air. Seems like the lighthouse was a highlight for both of you, isn't it? Maybe we can compile some of our photos from the trip into a couple books or something. That's a nice thought, but we should probably first look through them. I'm sure I've got some good shots of the lighthouse, though I was more focused on trying not to trip over those crabs. Ha! Usual John. Mind your step but always with a camera in hand. Speaking of photos, I recall Sam mentioning about those relationships you used to have back in the day. It's often worth asking what we learned from those experiences.

Right, so who's seen any good restaurants recently that we should definitely hit up? Yeah, I was thinking the same after our latest talked about food! I recently bookmarked some high-praised places in the city center for our next gathering. Hmm, speaking of which, have you folks tried that new Thai place that just opened near us? I heard they do a mean Tom Yum soup that makes your toes curl. Oh wow, that does sound tempting! I love a good Tom Yum! But is it affordable? You know, not all of us are exactly in the industry, and after the prices in Soho last time... I can attest, it is a bit on the pricey side. But, you know, for a special occasion, it might be worth it. Alternatively, there's another mid-range place that does amazing Korean BBQ. It's a bit more up my ally financially, and I thought it was really good. Ooh, Korean BBQ, that's a good shout! I love grilling my own stuff. But what about those really local joints or street food places? Doncaster back home, this is where you get the real taste, ya know? Ah, yes! Nothing beats Doncaster for some authentic local grub. Though I must say, we do have some really nice street food in Norwich, and even some good old-fashioned pub grub here in Cambridge. Speaking of food, has anyone tried making anything in quarantine? I really missed cooking and tried baking bread for the first time. It was trial and error, but rewarding when it turned out decent. Oh hell yes! I've been whipping up all sorts of stuff. Except, unfortunately, I don't have one of those fancy bread makers, or any fancy kitchen tools for that matter. But sandwiches! I've become a master of sandwiches. Sandwiches are underrated! I bet if you and I got together we could make a dinner party out of sandwiches. We could even have a little competition. I'm sure we could put together a mean spread. Either way, food always brings people together, doesn't it? It's like the universal way to bond, or to solve world problems... over a good meal. Yeah, speaking of bonding... Did you two, um, ever consider... going on a double date or something? I saw something on TV and thought, why not? It's all fun and games till your love life goes public, but really, what's the worst that could happen?

Hey, I'm so glad you're back! How was your weekend in Barcelona? You wouldn’t believe how amazing it was! Everything from the food to the architecture just blew me away. Was it as great as people make it out to be? Oh, it was definitely better than I expected. The vibe of the city, the beaches, the art museums - it has this unique blend of culture and chill that I really loved. That sounds wonderful! You know, I've been meaning to visit Barcelona for ages but it's just never happened. What was your favorite part of the trip? Honestly, I loved exploring La Rambla. It’s like the heart of the city, so much to see and do. And of course, the food - oh my god, the tapas were incredible! Tapas, I love that. We should try making some at home sometime. That would be great! Maybe we can have a Spain-themed dinner night. I can bring over some recipes I collected during my trip. I’d love that! When are you planning on doing that? Should we set a date for the weekend? Yeah, let’s do it! How about this Saturday? Sounds perfect! I can start making a list of ingredients to pick up tomorrow. Cool, I’ll email you all the recipes. Oh, and in case you were wondering, the food is much cheaper and fresher compared to what you’d pay in England. Plus, the atmosphere... it doesn’t come close to anything here. That’s really food for thought, you know? I’ve been wanting to travel more but things have held me back. Maybe the next trip we do together will be to Paris, what do you think? I’ve always wanted to see the Eiffel Tower. Yes! Paris next! We should definitely plan it. And we should also make sure we'll have time to explore beyond just the tourist spots. Definitely. What’s your take on the people/personality of the city? I’ve heard Barcelona is quite laid back but Paris is always spoken of as being... somewhat snooty? Barcelona is very laid back and welcoming, almost too much at times! But people there care deeply about quality of life. Paris, I think, has that image of elegance and refinement but don’t let that fool you — people are generally friendly too. Hmm, I guess that takes the edge off.

Ah, I'm so glad we could meet up here. We've lived here in North Cyprus for a few years now. It's a lovely place, don't you think? Absolutely. It's got a really nice balance. Still relatively quiet, but with all the modern conveniences you'd want. It certainly does. Speaking of life, have you been back to London much lately? I miss the hustle and bustle, but I don't know how I'd go back to working there. The teaching job keeps me busy, but it's a better pace of life here. No, I've been based here for a few years now. London is still home, of course, but I find I just don't need it to live and work. And what about you? How has your move here been? What's been keeping you busy? I'm actually involved with a small tech startup. It's been a challenging but rewarding move from traditional finance. I never thought I'd find myself juggling technical strategy and sales pitches. That sounds quite different from teaching, but there are some overlaps I’m sure. I mean, you’re still trying to engage people and impart knowledge in some way. Yeah, the 'selling' part of the job was the most surprising for me. As a teacher, you can't help but teach people something, but technology companies rely so heavily on the customer understanding what you're offering. There is that. I sometimes wish my students really grasped the importance of certain concepts the first time I explained them! And with the tech world, you have to stay ahead doesn’t it? Oh, that’s always the case. The market can change in an instant, and if you're not agile, you'll get left behind. More stressful than any marking period I've ever had. I can believe it. I’ve had years of stress around report cards and exam periods. But I must admit, I enjoyed the routine of changing the board and having my lesson plan down pat. You know, that’s something I’ve missed in this new career. I used to just deal with numbers, charts, and spreadsheets. Now, I’m also trying to navigate the human side of things. It’s the human side that usually keeps me going in my job. When the students grasp a concept and light up with understanding.

Right, so I'm thinking we could find someone else to live with. Grace has been so messy these past few months. She never washes up after herself and now the bathroom looks like the whole flat has taken a shower. Yeah, it's getting beyond a joke. I kind of regret agreeing to have her move in with us in the first place. But then again, it was convenient at the time and she's a mate. And the noise! She won't turn down her music for anyone. It's like living in a constant party, and not the fun kind. I need some peace and quiet, especially with exams coming up. Fair point. I've been wanting to study in our room but it just isn't happening. She's been hosting parties every weekend, even during term-time. Exactly. And to be honest, it's not just the noise or the mess. It feels like she's taken over the whole flat. Everything's always about what she wants, when she wants it. You know, it's not that I don't like or care about Grace. She's a good lass, really. It's just that she's not being considerate of anyone else in the flat. Exactly. Suppose we need to talk to her about it. But how? We don't want to be the bad guys, do we? Maybe we can approach it as 'we'd love for you to still be our housemate but we need to find a way to make this work for everyone'. That's a good idea. I could say something about setting up a chores rota or something. Maybe even suggest we have a flat meeting to discuss boundaries and stuff. Yeah, the problem is she might not take it well. She's always a bit defensive, especially when it comes to her space. Just be honest and clear, but polite. It's our place too, and she needs to respect that. True. And if she really can't or won't adjust, maybe it’s time we look for someone else. It’s not fair on either of us to live in this state. Yeah, but we also don't want to be the ones leading her on and making her think everything's fine when it's not. We could set a timeframe for things to improve, then have another chat.

Ah, I'm glad we decided to take a walk down to the shop today. Nothing like getting out of the house and seeing what's new. I've been finding it quite monotonous the past few days. You two been doing much? Aye, I agree. It's a welcome change of scenery. I've been finding myself missing the simple things like this. Speaking of which, have you noticed how the weather's been? I swear it's settled into a nice, cool spell. I'd almost forgotten what that felt like. Yes, it's lovely, isn't it? Reminds me of summers we used to have. I've been lazy in the garden a bit earlier today just enjoying it. I used to love growing my own veg when we lived just outside Norwich. Plus, the air's fresher in the places we wandered today. I almost forgot we could still get that smell of the sea sometimes. Norwich! That takes me back a bit. I spent a summer there once. It's a beautiful spot. And you know, these walks are good for both of us. Keeps us active, you know? We should do this more often. Definitely. It's good for the soul and all that. Now what have we got here? [Picks up a shopping bag] Oh, let’s unpack. We got vegetables, some meat, and [looks in the bag] a few bits and bobs from the sale. They were having a good deal on some of those little tea biscuits. I know how much you like them with your cup of tea. That's thoughtful of you. I do have a weakness for those biscuits. But it's not just about the biscuits, it's about the company, you know? I don't get out much these days, so days like these mean a lot. I know what you mean. It's not just the little luxuries but also getting to catch up. You know, things have changed so much since we were younger. There's a lot of loneliness out there for people like us. It's good we're here for each other. Indeed it is. I've found myself in these new routines since I stopped work, it can feel a bit stuck at times. But having you here, we can still share some of that together. You know, I was thinking about those kids you used to look after.

Ah, good day everyone! Lovely to see you all's here. I hope today's no too busy for us. I've got a few things to discuss, talked about our little house project and perhaps some arrangements for upcoming family gatherings. Aye now, let's get down to it then! Can questions be asked if things don't make sense? I'm not one for puzzlement when words get too curly! Irma, as long as I can keep up, I'm set for questions. But remember, keeps it simple, dears. We've had our share of complications before! Alright, let's try keep it simple today then, despite our individual complexities. Firstly, I've been considering the garden project. As you know, I've always liked the idea of having a well-planted backyard. What do you all think? Should we go with the raised beds or keep it more... traditional? Granny, that sounds like fun! But couldn't we also make it so it's easier for you and Granddad or even for me to help with? Maybe something more accessible? Oh, I see where you're coming from, lad. An accessible garden for all ages. Good thinking. But let’s make sure we can get to things easily, not just for us but for anyone who comes over. I agree with Aunty. Accessibility is key. And maybe we could also add some really good blooming plants? For the bees, and all that. And maybe even some herbs? Brilliant! I like that idea. Herbs, herbs would be perfect. We could use them in cooking, and if we're planning more family gatherings, we can have them available for fresh use in the kitchen. Plus, the bees are a great idea. If we're going for herbs, can we maybe have a section for mint? I love mint in everything! Mint, eh? Can't go wrong with mint. Let's not forget about lavender. It’s calming, good for soothing tea, and smells divine. Perfect, we've got a direction now. Let me see about those raised beds. We can probably source some materials locally in Malton. Can I help with that? Perhaps even with the planning? I've got some pretty good ideas from our school project on sustainable gardening. You'd love that, wouldn't you? Alright, that's settled. We'll work on the plans together. Yay!

Hey lads, what've you all been up to since we last caught up? Yeah, not much really. I've been deep into this new series on Netflix and had some uni work. I’ve been playing some FIFA, you know, keeping up with the questions on football. I've been reading a lot this week, "Educated" by Tara Westover, it's really good. Oh, I've got a keepsake for you, Lin. Remember when you mentioned you were looking for essential oils? Oh, mate, you didn’t have to do that! No, no, I thought you might genuinely need some. There’s this one called "Relaxation blend" from that new wellness brand you told me about. It's supposed to reduce stress. That was so kind of you, Steve. I have been feeling a little pressured with the last-minute assignments and exam prep. So, have you guys heard about this new fitness app that’s on the market? It's got a whole community section and personalised workouts. I've tried it. Good stuff. It sets you daily goals and its interface is really user-friendly. If only it could help me motivate myself to go for a run in this rain. Can't blame you, mate. Alright, I'm all about trial and error with tech stuff. I've been looking at smartwatches too. Really? What do you think of them? I’ve seen some of my mates at uni have them, but I’m not sure if I need another gadget. To be honest, it’s convenient. You can check your email, answer calls, and even pay for stuff if you sync it with your card. You can also monitor your steps and heart rate. I like seeing my progress. I don’t know, feels like just adding more clutter to my life, but I suppose it’s different for everyone. Speaking of clutter, does anyone know how the ad ID tracking thing works? I keep seeing ads related to things I just talked about out loud with people and it’s kinda freaky. Oh, yeah! “Influencer marketing” or “dynamic targeting” or something like that. I’ve taken to finding privacy settings in apps more seriously now... True that. We're also talking about DIY health products, like CBD and such. Have any of you tried them? Not really. The youth of London seems all about it

Right, so who's seen any of these creepy crawlies around the house recently? [The speaker is possibly talking about insects] Ah, just saw a huge spider down in the basement. Better not let the kids see that. Still, now that the weather’s getting a bit warmer, I’ll have to keep a closer eye out for these house invaders. Exactly, it’s the time of year when they start coming out again. Speaking of which, did anyone else notice how many moths we got last night coming in through the front door? Yeah, that was pretty disturbing! Even had one of them buzzing around my bedroom light. Does anyone know how to get rid of them? Well, there are a few ways. You can set traps, or even just turn off the outside lights at night. Moths and other bugs are attracted to light, so if there's nothing on outside drawing them in, you'll get fewer inside. Right, and if we’re on the topic of gross things, has anyone seen how those big flies look or heard their high-pitched buzz? I’m really hoping it’s not quite their season yet. Not yet thankfully, but we’re definitely approaching that. I think we need to figure out what to do about the spider and the moths before it gets really bad. Maybe we can come up with some kind of family plan? Like, what if we go through the house tonight and check for any cracks in the walls or windows? Sometimes they get in from the tiniest openings. That’s a great idea! And doesn’t anyone remember that spray we used last year? It was that stuff from the garden center. It was kind of like a non-toxic bug repellent. Maybe we could pick up some more of that. Oh yeah, I think that’s a good point. We should definitely get some of that. It’s better for us and for the environment. And what about if we actually find a spider or something? What’s the best way to get rid of them? Well, for spiders in particular, there’s often no need to kill them. If they're not poisonous, you can just trap them in a cup and take them outside. However, if we're talking about mosquitoes or those flies you mentioned, almost anything to just get them out of the house is fair game!

Hey, I just saw that PE class will be first period next week. I hope today's final games are good, I've been practising my shuttle run since the last match. Are you still into sports after that fiasco in the last match? Yeah, but I'm determined to improve and have fun. Plus, I saw some people talking about this science project at school and it sounds pretty cool. Maybe we should work together? Erm, maybe. But didn't you say that weird keeps coming up with these odd ideas in chemistry class? You'll end up being her guinea pig again. Maybe but I trust her judgment. Plus, I've got a feeling that it's going to be among the best projects we've done in a while. What's new with Sarah? Did she join any new clubs this term? Yeah, she decided to join the school creative writing group. She's been writing these amazing short stories and is even thinking about entering some national competitions. That's so cool! I remember when she was just so focused on her studies. It's good to see her pursue her passions. Indeed. Speaking of pursuits, have you checked out Jasmine's new Insta reel? No, I've been too busy. She's probably sharing some dance moves again, right? Yeah, but there was this one video where she does this amazing lip-sync challenge with her friends. It's hilarious and they all look so confident and happy. But weren’t the teachers getting stressed about that? Some of the content doesn’t fit the school’s policy, doesn’t it? Right. Seems like the teachers are pretty chill about it as long as students aren’t breaking any rules. She said that since they’re all over 12, they’ve had a briefing about responsible social media use and that it’s all good now. Hmmm. I hope that’s true. I heard one of our teachers was really upset about some students sharing inappropriate content in another class. True, but I think Jasmine’s content is harmless fun for her friends and family. Plus, she's been cleared already, so it should be fine. Okay, just being cautious here. We don’t want to see any unnecessary drama, especially around school stuff. Definitely. Oh, and have you heard about the new Maths teacher? Someone said they’re really helpful but can be a bit strict when it comes to homework.

Ah, I'm so sorry you're feeling under the weather. I have a cold today too; these viruses seem to be going around at the moment. Do you think it might be chickenpox? I've heard they're doing a vaccination campaign at the hospital. Still, now, the waiting room might be kind of a nightmare given how many folks must have it right now. Haha, that makes two of us then! But actually, I've been thinking, we should get vaccinated if it's offered. It's weird how even though I'm a bit older than you, I still get stuff like chickenpox. I guess there's always a first time for everything! Absolutely. Lloyd Grossman had a great segment just last night about the importance of vaccination. Do you remember that? Wasn't it hilarious when the camera caught the body language of the kids who were reluctant to get vaccinated? Yes, completely! That was so Ronan. His expertise in cameras, filmmaking, and even psychology really shines through in those segments. It's like he understands human behavior through their body language and facial expressions. But jokes aside, vaccination is a really important topic. It's not just about us but also about keeping others safe. Indeed. I found it rather insightful, how he used the camera angles to emphasize different points. I think it's also why we can't help but gesture when we talk or show emotions - it's a basic human need to communicate beyond just words. Evolutionarily speaking, body language recognition has really helped us communicate and even survive. I read an article about it recently. It's fascinating stuff. But I wonder, doesn't getting a vaccination make it harder for our bodies to recognize that kind of virus naturally? That's a common concern but usually unfounded. Vaccines actually train the immune system to recognize the specific virus and fight it off faster next time. It doesn't diminish our body's ability to recognize or fight other viruses or bacteria. Makes sense. I must admit, I was a bit hesitant at first. But reading about it and watching those docu-series by Lloyd Grossman really helped make things clearer for me. Lloyd Grossman has that effect, doesn't he? And speaking of him, have you watched his latest series on food safety? There was this one segment on health risks linked to undercooked food...

Who knew I'd spend my Sunday educating my friends on etymology instead of enjoying the game of Scrabble. You've certainly landed a few of your 'tough' words. Still, though, the competition’s tough! Indeed! It's a bit like explaining a gridlock of words, isn't it? All very similar and yet so different. Or like trying to get through a butcher’s queue on a Sunday! Well, fitting then. This game of ours is quite fitting for our situation. And speaking of fitting, how's the new cooking class going? I saw some pictures on the family Facebook post. Oh, it's been fantastic! Learned some new recipes. And it's actually served to help me reorganize my mind around playing Scrabble as well. Maybe a more 'coordinated' approach to word-finding is needed? Well, we can certainly 'divide' and 'conquer,' as they say. Ah, but to divide and conquer, one must first know how to 'organize' the available resources, much like planning for a gridlock or understanding the 'root' of a word. I like that, old man! Perhaps we could use a 'grid' to organize our words next time. But the point is less about winning the Scrabble match as it is about the enjoyment. That's the spirit. It’s about the family time and the conversation more than the game itself. True, but changing the subject, did anyone else find that recent music magazine really interesting? I was surprised by how many new artists they featured from Manchester. Yeah! The city truly has a vibrant music scene. Though, if I’m being honest, I got a bit lost in the jargon. Did anyone else find some of the descriptions too pretentious? I did. I thought, “Are we talking about music or a new recipe for fine dining?” Yes, sometimes it feels like they’re using the most obscure words like we're playing Scrabble... except we don’t even know the definition half the time! Exactly like Scrabble here, finding these long words, but not really knowing what they mean. Then maybe there’s a lesson in that. Sometimes, it’s fun to use big words even if we don’t always understand them. It’s all about the challenge and the journey, not just the destination. And the journey, my friends, is what we’re all about. Family, friends, having a good time, enjoying one another’s company.

Ah, I'm so glad we could take a break from all this. I've been meaning to catch up with what's been happening with you. I've heard you talked about working in the print industry down in Surrey, right? Yes, that's correct! It was a fascinating time for me, really. I spent most of my years working on developing and improving commercial printing systems. Oh, I can imagine! I've actually always been interested in printing techniques myself, though mainly in the context of art. There's something about the texture and colour of a beautifully printed print... Absolutely! Even in my line of work, I've always had a keen eye for that. But from a technical standpoint, let me tell you, it's amazing what can be achieved with the right equipment and expertise. [Smiling] Well, you must have had a certain knack for it, judging from your success. [Chuckles] Well, knack might be one way of putting it. I think it was more a combination of experience, a bit of luck, and a lot of hard work. I actually started this side of my career quite young. I can't imagine. For myself, I've always been rather the 'artist' type. Although in my case, that was a lifelong journey rather than a career [laughs]. [Laughs] Well, each to their own, I suppose. Speaking of which, did you ever have the chance to travel for work or exhibitions? Occasionally, but mostly it was related to my gallery. I did, however, travel quite a bit for sourcing and the like. I always loved the research and tracking down those hidden gems. Fascinating career. Seems like the commerce and arts together make for a rather rich life. Indeed. Speaking of travel, your time in Germany for those exhibitions... was that for work or more of a cultural ins and outs you wanted to explore? It was work, but naturally, it often allows for a blend of both. The German fairs for printers and print enthusiasts are top-notch and very informative, but Hamburg, Berlin... so much to learn from the culture and the people too. I wish I had the opportunity. I could have spent hours lost in almost any art gallery or antique shop. But I've had to rely on those trips for my personal interests rather than my work. [Leaning in slightly] I remember when I was just starting out, I met this fellow from the typography scene in Munich.

Dad, I'm really enjoying my English lessons at school. We've been learning so much about the language and its origins. It's fascinating how the spelling of words can change so much over the centuries and be influenced by different cultures. It certainly is, sweetie. That’s one of the reasons English can be kind of tricky. You’ve got your Latin and French and even Scandinavian words sneaking into the vocabulary over time. And the way pronunciations can vary too, isn’t it? Like “bath”, which some people say as “barth” in the north. Yes, exactly! Even geographical distance can change the way we pronounce words. It's a very dynamic language. Speaking of dialects, is it true what they say about Cornwall having its own language? I’ve heard that the Cornish dialect is quite distinct. It's not quite a separate language, but Cornish does have its own history and identity. In fact, it was even recognized as a minority language by the UK government a few years ago. That's interesting! I remember we visited Cumbria before and I noticed it too, they had their own dialect there. Right. Geography and history often shape local dialects. You'll find these sorts of regional variations all over England. [looking at the map] Do you think they’ll have any roadworks or traffic on this route to Cornwall? We don’t want to get delayed. [checks the map] They’re actually doing some works on the M6, and they may affect us if we take the M5 downwards. But it should be manageable if we head through Cheshire instead. Cheshire… I just had a quinoa salad for lunch today. More people are eating that, weren’t they, Dad? Quinoa's definitely getting more popular. It’s a great source of protein, which is why it's been adopted by a lot of people into their diet. Even though it's not native to England, it’s become a common sight in supermarkets and salad bars. Funny, because just yesterday we were talking about gluten-free diets in class. I couldn’t believe that some people are actually gluten-intolerant. Yes, those kinds of sensitivities and alternative diets are quite common now. Maybe worth asking at restaurants or cafes we stop at if they have options for that. Dee-dubs [a colloquial term used in northern England], I hadn’t thought of that.

Right, so who's in charge of dinner tonight? I've got some ideas but I'll leave it up to whoever's keen. I'll help out. We can do something simple. You know I'm not too bad at cooking for a group now and then. You do know, lads, just because I'm retired and all, doesn't mean I'm going to sit back and watch you lot work. I've got plenty to contribute. Absolutely, Uncle Toby! And we'd love your input. What's on your mind for dinner? Well, now that you've brought it up, I was thinking we could have something a bit traditional, like Shepherd's Pie. Sounds great to me, as long as we can include some nice veggies to make it a bit healthier. That's a winning idea, Uncle Toby. Veggies are a must for me these days. Let's plan that. And while we're on the subject of food, did you all hear that new pub in town or even the old one is rumoured to have this fantastic Sunday roast? Ah, yes, I've heard about it. You know, when I was working, Sundays were always about that roast dinner. That's really nice, Uncle Toby. You have some great memories. Perhaps we could try to make our version as close to that as possible, veggies and all. Yeah, and considering we’re making dinner at ANON’s place, it’s like having a home-cooked meal doesn’t it? Indeed it is. ANON does have a good kitchen, and I do appreciate her letting us use it. She’s always been generous like that. We should make sure we thank her properly. She said she’s happy for us to do as much as we’ve planned. We should also consider setting some time aside to talk a bit about family. Uncle Toby, you're always good for a story or two, especially about family. Ah, you're right about that. There’s always something to learn from the past. And speaking of which, did anyone see the last episode of that genealogy show on TV? It was about the history of immigration in this very area. I did! I found it quite fascinating. Yeah, it's amazing how many families have stories similar to Uncle Toby’s, with roots across different places. True that.

Hey there, Sarah! How’s it going? Hey, Tom! Not too bad. How about yours? Pretty good, thanks for asking. Got some down time today, which is always nice after a long week. Still getting used to the morning shift though, kind of kills me after a night out haha. Haha, yeah, those early starts are tough. I used to have some of those when I was actually doing my postgraduate studies. But I think your body probably adjusts after a while, keeps you in shape alongside all the gym time you must have right? Oh for sure! It’s tough to keep up at first, but definitely makes you more resilient. You've been keeping up your yoga, I hope? Yeah, every day actually. It’s become a part of my routine even during summer, keeps me going. What about you? Do you still find time for the gym or do you go with the more relaxed paths now? Hmm, when I can, yeah. But I grab it where I can. You know between shifts and everything else, sometimes I’m running on fumes by the end of the day. I mean, it’s not ideal but you balance as you can. Totally understandable. It’s the same with job and teaching. Kids in class keep you on your toes and then trying to stay on top of lesson planning at home. But it’s rewarding in its own way. Totally gets it. Speaking of which, how’s the new job going? You really picked a groove back into teaching full-time, I think that must be fulfilling. It is, absolutely. I was a bit concerned at first about getting the hang of everything again but the students make it worth it. Plus, all the time off’s a bonus compared to when I was doing side work. Yeah, the time off’s a big pull. Do you ever regret not doing your PhD? Of course, there are times. But I think it’s about what’s right for my life right now. Teaching gives me a balance of stability and creativity, and I get to see kids make progress. Plus I’ve got enough qualifications for now :) Wise decision, I think so too. I’ve always thought about maybe doing a master’s in brewery management or something similar, but it depends on the opportunities. You know how it goes.

Ah, I'm losing track of time! We've got to get moving if we're going to reach that coffee shop before they close at six. I don't know about you two, but I'm down for that caffeine hit. Morning, dear! You've always been punctual, haven't you? But honestly, I think our elderly selves could give up those punctuality notions and just enjoy the journey. Besides, it's not like we have to be anywhere right now. Quite, quite. There's time enough for coffee. But I've just had a brilliant idea, have either of you heard of Munchausen Syndrome by Proxy? Ah, now that's a topic we don't often touch upon. Hence my punctuality, I suppose, want to avoid anything dramatic. But, by all means, Fire away, dear. Oh, Munchausen's - that's right. I remember it from some medical drama I watched years ago. It's quite unusual, isn't it? A person faking their symptoms to get attention, isn’t it? That’s the gist of it, yes! It really illustrates the complexities of the human psyche, doesn’t it? Speaking of attention, have either of you thought about making a donation box for the charities we support? An old coffee tin or something. Now that's a fantastic idea! We can use that donation box to collect spare change or small donations from our friends and family if they're willing. But the question is, where would we display it? How about making a banner or two for the living room? I've seen some nice banners at the library when they host events. A banner? While you’re at it, why not also add some plants to the house? I've got some of my geraniums that are really flourishing. Let's brighten up the place a bit, if we’re already stuck at home. Brilliant! And once this lockdown is lifted, let's use some of that money to travel to Gambia if you're up for it. It's been on my list for years, ever since our friend mentioned how beautiful it is during their company trip. Gambia? That’s quite the change of scenery from here! But sure, why not? If we can get back to traveling again. I miss the freedom of driving, too. Maybe next time, I can take you on a tour across England?

Hey everyone, did you guys see that new mobile app that's supposed to help you with meditation and mental health? Yeah, I saw it. It's called "Mindful Minds". I've tried it out and it’s actually pretty helpful. Did anyone else try it? No, I haven't had the chance. But I've heard a lot about it. Mindfulness and meditation seem to be all the rage right now, right? Definitely. I set a reminder on my phone to meditate for ten minutes a day and it's surprisingly helped my stress levels. That’s great! I was actually thinking of trying out some new apps for productivity as well. Does anyone have any recommendations? There's one called "Forest" that’s really good for staying focused. You plant a virtual tree each time you stay focused on your tasks. It grows if you don't touch your phone and it gets cut if you do. It’s creative and very effective. That sounds similar to "StayFocusd". It blocks distracting websites for a set period of time. I’ve been using it to stay on track during work hours. Interesting, I might give "StayFocusd" a shot. I find myself getting sidetracked on YouTube way too much. Perfect, let's try them out and compare notes at our next dinner! Ah, speaking of focusing, did anyone else watch that new, super scary horror movie that came out in theaters? Oh yes, "The Scream Shows"! I couldn’t sleep that night. I don’t usually get scared by movies but that one kept me up. I went to see it with my boyfriend and I thought it was one of the scariest movies I’ve seen in years. The ending was particularly chilling. I’m a bit more of a chicken. I prefer happy endings or comedies. But I did find it interesting how it played with our fears in a new way. Definitely. It’s making us think differently about how we interact with our scary movies, right? For sure. It's just like when we were younger and watching "The Exorcist". That was a staple of scary movie nights. Again and again with the horror movies. I think it’s because it allows us to face our fears in a controlled environment. That makes a lot of sense. Speaking of facing fears, have any of our friends been doing something adventurous lately?

Ah, good day everyone. I've been meaning to ask, how have you been getting back and forth from your homes? The council has clearly forgotten about our roads. Every time it rains the whole main road floods. Indeed, it’s almost impassable, the road’s so bad. We’ve heard rumors there might be some new developments planned but until that happens, it’s a nightmare. Yes, I've also noticed, it’s very concerning. As I pick up and drop off children from school, I always have to plan it backwards due to the flooding. Sometimes I even have to tell parents to pick up, it’s just not safe. These roadworks have been going on for ages. Seems like they just haven't prioritized it properly. I've been stuck in traffic waiting for the tractors from the works to move - oh, the hours I've wasted! Speaking of getting stuck, I did get caught out during the recent flooding. The water was halfway up the wheels. Had to wait over an hour for it to subside. Quite stressful, especially considering my health isn’t what it used to be. Now that you mention it, I've seen some cars actually get stuck and have to be towed. It's quite silly when we’re just trying to get from A to B. Should be so simple. I used to enjoy the long drives, but now I dread them. Well, technology is supposed to make things easier but in this case perhaps it's actually made things worse. There’s more traffic and in return, more congestion. It’s all about timing and planning now. You can't just set off unless you’ve checked the weather, the roadworks and the traffic updates. Used to be much simpler. I don’t understand why they can’t just fix the drainage. Seems like the simplest solution but it’s taking ages! And, as always, it seems like it’s always our side of town that gets overlooked. Yes, that's a great point. There must be technical reasons but from a common-sense perspective, it sure seems like a simple fix. I do wish our local council would meet more often and address these issues. Our generation used to have better infrastructure, but it seems like newer isn't always better. And the buses are no better. The timing of the buses can be so poor.

Ah, I'm so glad we could all meet up like this. It feels like ages since we've done anything together. How are you all doing? I'm good, thanks for asking. It's lovely to catch up. I've been meaning to tell you, though, I've taken on some transcribing work outside of my usual job and it's been keeping me pretty busy. Fantastic! I'm glad you've taken the initiative to keep busy. I've been meaning to set up my old home office to keeps things productive. You know how it is when routine goes right out the window once you retire. Absolutely! I feel like I need to organise myself properly. I did try setting up a schedule like you have, but then I ended up feeling too restricted. Was a bit odd, actually—after years making sure each lesson had its own time slot and all of that. I get that. It's like your whole identity is tied to how you use your time. But freelance work can give you the flexibility to pick and choose what works for you, can't it? I love the autonomy. I’m really trying to stick to it, though it's a balance between keeping busy and keeping the cabin fever at bay. The paint job I started on the house still needs some work. You’re ambitious, really getting on with those home projects. I’ve been meaning to do some gardening, but the rain we’ve had hasn’t made it easy. Gardening is good for you, you know? For the mind, and all that. And with the right kit, you could make the most of it come rain or shine. Exactly! Just last weekend, I helped my brother with his car maintenance. I thought I knew the basics, but there was so much more to it than I guessed! I haven’t done much with cars since my husband was alive, but maybe I should think about that next. We really should consider moving to Manchester, it's a great changing of pace and not so far from my family. Manchester? I spent a few years there. There's loads of public transport and it’s easy to get around without a car—which might be a good idea for you if you're not planning to dive into car projects.

Hey Mum, did you hear about James' bike?? It's been stolen! Oh, no! That's terrible. Have they found it yet? Apparently, they've managed to recover it. It's been returned. Still, though, the thieves had defaced it before bringing it back! Oh, that's just awful! I hope they catch those idiots! But actually, James posted a funny comment about it online. He says it's become his "make-over" bike due to all the new "accessories" it's got! Well, as long as he can ride it and it's been returned, that's what matters. It just shows how reckless and ignorant some people can be. Exactly! But Mum, we need to be careful. Even though we live in a quiet neighborhood, stuff like this happens. Absolutely. You need to always lock your bike, preferably with a good chain that can't be easily cut. And maybe we should also consider getting a bike tracker. That's a great idea! Maybe we can look into that online or see if there's a local shop that sells them. Definitely. It would also be worth mentioning at school. If everyone knows how to make their bikes more secure, it might deter some of these thefts. Yeah, good point! Do you know anyone who's had their bike stolen, Mum? Actually, yes, I do. One of my colleagues at the office had a bike stolen from right outside their house. These burglaries don't just happen in the evening; sometimes they're brazen enough to do it in broad daylight. That's really concerning. I guess people have the mistaken notion that no one's looking, right? Exactly. But it goes to show how important it is to be vigilant. And, of course, sharing news about bike thefts on social media and neighborhood groups can help too. Right, like James did. It might not be the most appealing topic, but sometimes it gets the attention it needs. That's true. Plus, it can lead to tips or better security ideas for all of us. Speaking of topics most people aren't keen on discussing, have you heard about how this new café just opened? Apparently, their food is amazing but they're already getting some pretty bad reviews online. No, I hadn't! Let me check that out. I wonder what their problem is. Maybe there's something simple that they could fix to improve their online presence?

Who knew I'd spend Easter Sunday educating my friends and family about train dynamics instead of the resurrection story? It wouldn’t be the first time we've landed in a peculiar situation Alison! Did anyone else have a drama with tickets at the train station this morning? I had to do a full roll call to make sure everyone had their ticket to ride! Oh, the memories! Last time I had to deal with such a complicated ticket situation was during that epic Welsh backwards journey. Think about it - you start at Swansea and end up back at Swansea after a few day's journey – without actually deciding to loop back. I was just looking at those ticket to ride cards. Do any of you remember the good old days of train travel before the whole "smart" card setup? Absolutely! My dad used to take us on these long journeys and we’d play “tell a story through the window”. You’d start a story and grab it from the kid next to you – by the time you finished a story or a character disappeared into the distance, it was someone else’s turn. That sounds fascinating! We should give it a go this weekend. Good idea! It’ll keep the kids entertained and we can enjoy the scenery. What story should we start with? How about starting with one of our own holiday cottage stories? We could weave it into a nice fantastical tale of Herefordshire and all the fantastic local characters and landmarks we can't quite catch from the train but definitely would in slow motion. Actually, that jogs my memory - didn’t one of you bring an atlas of Wales or something? More detail for those hypothetical games. Ah yes, I did! Here we are! Now we can name places along our journey and describe the view from each stop. Brilliant! Let's do it! We’ll make the most of these last days in this beautiful place. Alright, who wants to start? I’ll go first. So, the story begins with a holiday cottage in Hereford and our first stop is the nearby Hay-on-Wye. Five of them spend the next few minutes enthusiastically spinning and passing a story, each describing local characters and landmarks as if they’re passing through. And then we sumbled upon the famous Hay-on-Wye castle which had turned into... a book castle!

Ah, I'm losing to you again! But I love this game; it really does teach you to think about your strategy. Do you enjoy using this kind of thinking in your work as well, or is this more just a hobby for you? Oh, definitely! As a lecturer, I need to think strategically about how to convey complex ideas and engage my students. But apart from that, games like this remind me of our PhDs, actually. We used to play Risk and other strategy games during our thesis writing. It was a good way to get our minds off the stress. Oh, that's actually really similar to my experience too. When I was doing my postgraduate studies, I'd often play board games with friends just to unwind. It was a great social activity as well. Absolutely! And speaking of unwinding, I suppose this game doesn't quite have the same impact as, say, a few pints at the local pub after a long week, does it? Well, yes, it's quite different, but I love both! So, do you often drink while playing games or is that a bit unusual? Not unusual at all! We've had plenty of game nights with drinks. I think the 'drinking culture' here in England is quite different from the US, for instance, right? It's very integrated into social life, even at informal gatherings like game nights. Oh, absolutely. I think it's quite deep-seated in our culture, really. But it also means we’re quite aware of the contexts where it’s 'allowed'. Like, if I had been in Norwich for a family gathering and we were playing a game, that would be very much 'on the menu'. Right! I guess that's the thing with drinking in England - it's very much tied to social events and, as you said, the occasion. On a warm summer afternoon at a garden party or something, or at a meet-up in someone's house after work and it's Friday… Exactly! It's almost ritualistic, really. And board games fit perfectly into that – it’s a social but also intellectual activity, for sure. It's interesting how much so much of our cultural identity is tied into these social activities, isn't it? Like the pub culture, board game nights, even the way we talk about them. Every culture has its own social markers, I suppose.
