Hopefully not, but you never can predict with British weather. Just hope we'll still be set for the dinner party tonight at keeps changing plans due to this. True, but at least we have a great alternative plan – James has a massive collection of board games and I've been wanting to try his homemade mojitos again. Oh, I'm sure that will make up for any travel disruptions. Speaking of which, did you get a chance to look over the directions one more time? Just gave them a quick glance before we left. Google maps seems pretty confident we're on the right track. You know how sometimes these village names look alike in Poland, though. Hopefully, we won’t get lost. Agreed. Well, if we do, the upside is we’ll discover some quaint local spots. You never know what unexpected gems might be along the route. Especially if we’re looking, right? Absolutely. And technology usually hasn't let us down. Plus, we have a pretty good feel for navigating rural Polish roads by now. True, considering we’re here fairly often. But never hurts to be prepared. Just hope we don’t encounter any road works or restricted areas. Exactly. Just last weekend our journey to Zakopane turned into an adventure because of unexpected road closures. Fortunately, side roads usually lead to scenic surprises. True. Okay, let’s just hope today’s journey is as straightforward as we can make it. While you’re at changing the world’s weather, can you try to magically conjure up some of that sunlight? I’m running low on Instagram-worthy photos for my social media and today’s weather hasn't been co-operating. I’ll summon my best English showers for sunlight and good vibes. How about you? Making progress on that new TEFL project? Oh, yeah. I started reading up on blended learning. It seems like everything these days is moving online or hybrid. It’s both exciting and a bit overwhelming all at once.

I was thinking if McDonald's's ever sponsored a football team. Imagine how that would turn out. Oh, the thought is quite funny. Would be interesting to see the uniforms if that ever happened. I'm picturing Ronald McDonald on the shoulder patch. Or even a McNugget shape on the kits. And the players would probably never go hungry. But seriously, that's an interesting thought. Companies with food would actually make sense for teams training hard, seeing that players need to eat plenty. Exactly, and I can imagine the advertising campaigns. Sports sponsorship is a huge business, you know. Brands get exposure and boosts through mascots making appearances on the sidelines. Hence the importance of choosing the right team. Absolutely. But looking at the football strip designs...some of them are just terrible, don't you think? Some are, for sure. And those shirts end up being rarities. Like the Forth Wanderers third uniform. I mean, who thought that weird design through? I assumed that while the mainstream designs are fairly standard, the third kits are often over the top to increase sales, right? Well, they usually do try to stand out to generate buzz, perhaps for commercials or limited edition merchandise. It's a marketing strategy, even if it doesn't always hit the mark. That's true. And sometimes these designs become iconic. Like the Norwich City 'Yellows' kit from the 90s. That one went down in history. Yes, or the Manchester City 'Turbo Peach' one from 1995. At the time, they were trying to be futuristic. Weirdly, it aged well. It's quite interesting, really, seeing how strip design has evolved over the years. You'd think after all these years of professional football, they'd have standardized some of the design elements, but no. I suppose it's because each team wants to show off their individuality. And of course, it's all leading to commercials. Did you see the new Adidas advert during this half? Yeah, with Martin Tyler. I thought it was quite clever how they got football commentators to talk about the match rather than directly about the kit, but then suddenly there's the new strip. Exactly, it’s a master stroke in hype-building. Brands know that when you've got the commentator talking about the spirit of the game, the new strip just feels like the logical progression, even if it’s from a different segment.

Hey, I've been reading about how to improve social skills. Did you know that today's society values active listeners more than ever? That sounds familiar. Plus, when you think about all the online scams and people's patience for confrontations over false posts, it can be quite a turn-off. You can’t even go on YouTube without someone screaming insults over a misunderstanding. I know what you mean. But there’s lots of reputable online places, Coursera, for example, they offer zero-cost learning with real university credentials.

Ah, I'm so glad we could all meet up like this. It's been ages since we've had a proper catch-up. It sure has! I have been meaning to get into more of this. It's nice to have the time now, though. Oh yes! I just love conversations like this. It gets me out and about, you know? I know, I'm right there with you, Ma. Table manners and all! Speaker_1 keeps coming backwards and forwards with refills for our hot drinks. So, how have you been keeping busy since retirement? Mainly keeping up with my grandkids, just trying to keep up with them. You know, it's nice now to finally have the time to do things that I wanted to do while working. Like watch those old documentaries about nature and history. Oh, I know how you mean. I'm barely keeping up with my own kids. And then there was the time I thought I missed a turn and had to circle the roundabout a few times. Oh, that reminds me! There's something to be said for having to think things through and explore a little, isn't there? Absolutely. It's amazing though, thinking back, when I was just driving all over for work and had no Sat Nav to guide me.

Hey, I'm so stressed out about maths tests coming up. Our teacher just told us that these are important and that we need to do well. Do you know much about her? Oh yeah, Ms. Thompson? Maybe we can also talk about the new art project. I've got a rough idea, but I'm not sure if it's good enough. Oh, that's cool. We should also check if we can use some of the equipment from the science department for your project. We can show it to Mr. Smith when he's free. He's almost always available if you just ask.

Hey everyone, did you know that Catholicism is pretty prevalent in Ireland? I was reading today that nearly 80% of the population identifies as Catholic. Oh wow, that's a lot higher than England isn't it? Over here, the numbers are a lot more split between different religions or none at all. What's a religion? Mummy says I should share my cookies with others. Is that like a religion? That's very kind and generous, but it's a bit different. You'll learn more about religions when you're older. Right now, it’s more about being good and sharing. Is that a Catholic thing? Sharing is caring, right? Well, many religions teach the importance of kindness and helping each other. And being respectful and polite too. It's not just about the big church buildings and going to mass every Sunday. Like in that movie about the Matrix? They talk about a higher authority and beliefs and whatnot. Hmm, yes, beliefs can be about anything from religious doctrines to scientific theories. The Matrix is more about philosophy and science fiction, but it does touch on the idea of questioning what we believe in. I found it pretty interesting. The idea of living in a simulated world or something bigger than us. But isn't that more like scientology or something spiritual? Oh, well, scientology is quite controversial. It’s a set of beliefs that were developed by a guy called L. Ron Hubbard. But it's not a widely accepted religion and the Church of Scientology has had a lot of criticism. Really? What's the criticism about? Well, a lot of it’s about how it handles money. It’s expensive to be part of, and there’s suspicion that they are more interested in making money than in providing a spiritual path. Plus, there’s a lot of secrecy and some really odd beliefs. Like what? Well, they believe that we are all the spirits of aliens from a long time ago who became trapped in human bodies. And they have this idea about spaceships and alien stuff... it sounds pretty unusual to most people. I guess that sounds strange! But then again, all religions have some beliefs that can seem weird if you're not part of them. I went to a talk by a Buddhist monk once and his beliefs about reincarnation and... stuff were hard for me to wrap my head around.

Hey, I'm so excited for our little road trip! We've got enough time today to make it to Southport. I've never been there, but I've talked to a few folks from there and they say it's beautiful. Hey lads and lasses. I was thinking last night's recording was epic but today's task might just top it. Ideas anyone about how to make it even more talked about? Ah, I'm starving. I forgot my lunch again. That's alright, it happens to the best of us. Are you heading out to grab something? Just need a quick fix – something simple and filling. Hey lads, what do you think of this social networking's impact on our jobs today? I mean, we're always telling people about new ways they can access information, but at the same time, we're also competing with technology that does the same thing for free or drastically faster? Oh, absolutely. I had this one time a student came asking me about a particular book, "Pride and Prejudice," but she said, "Sir, I've read it on BookTube, but I want to know if we have a keepsake edition here." That whole experience made me think... knowledge is no longer about physical books but the experience and the journey behind it. That's true. I had a similar conversation with a parent who wanted to know what apps her kids should use for research but didn't want to step foot in a library. I had to explain the value of curation and the exploration aspect which is sometimes missing in online platforms. Exactly! It's not just about information anymore; it's about the trusted advice and guidance. Plus, it keeps us on our toes, making sure we're adapting. Like how Forbs talks about this revolution, we have to see ourselves as both gatekeepers and guides in this digital age. I once tried using one of those digital book readers; it was quite interesting, to be honest, but you can't beat the feel of a physical book. I know right, especially for books that have a lot of imagery or nuanced contexts. Digital is great, but sometimes, the experience is lost. I know what you mean. Even in Australia where the digital shift is more pronounced, there’s still this nostalgic aspect to libraries that persists, and if we're honest, it’s a unique value proposition that the digital world hasn’t fully replaced yet. Speaking of value propositions, did you guys see this meme about librarians being the last bastion against insomniac algorithms? While it was humor, there's something in there about our role in curating valuable, human-curated content versus automated aggregators. Funny and a bit true. We need to show people that there's a value to human recommendations that algorithms can't replicate. It's about the 'what you might like based on this' versus 'here's something worth exploring because we think it has value beyond popularity or algorithmic suggestions.'

Thank you for seeing me today. I'm really excited about the upcoming opportunity to establish a new hospice in Kent and wanted to discuss some of the aspects of our business plan with you. You're welcome. I'm glad you're excited. A new hospice is a significant project and one that requires careful planning. What specific aspects would you like to focus on today? I've been thinking a lot about our location choice. As you know, I grew up near Stratford-upon-Avon, and it's struck me how even in an area as resonant with culture and history as Shakespeare country, there's still a significant gap in localized healthcare services. It led me to wonder about the potential for our new hospice to have similar positive impacts in our chosen locations here. Your insights as someone familiar with Britain’s geographical disparities can be invaluable. I agree that making the right location choice is pivotal. Tunbridge Wells is a strong contender due to various reasons, such as its central geographic position and availability of skilled workforce, which aligns with my rationale. That makes sense. But have you considered the potential impact on local businesses and the existing or proposed infrastructure? For instance, there might be interest from estate agents and local contractors who could support our build. That's a good point. I assumed we might engage with local contractors but hadn't thought about estate agents as much. Their expertise in identifying suitable locations or properties could actually be beneficial. We could also consider using agents to find a location or current building that might be converted or significantly renovated, which could save costs and time in comparison to building from scratch. An astute observation there. And what about working with local health services and hospices? Our new facility needs to integrate well with those existing services to maximize benefits to patients. Absolutely. That’s one of the most critical aspects of our plan. We should be looking to build those relationships upfront and see where collaborations could enhance care. For example, we might look to ease the burden on other local healthcare providers by taking on end-of-life care cases or offering specific services like palliative care that are currently underserved. It might also be good to discuss with local health service administrators about what they foresee in terms of new health budgets allocations and priorities in the coming years, as that could impact how our service is perceived and utilized.

Ah, look at this one. I remember this was from's Royal Ascot last year. The sun was so strong that day, and yet the food was amazing. You wouldn't believe the number of well-dressed ladies in hats. It really does bring out the best and the most eccentric, doesn't it? Oh yes, absolutely! I always manage to make my way down there every year. The food and hats are a highlight, but also the atmosphere of sophistication mingled with that slightly eccentric feel? It's quite unique. Right, let me pull out my phone before we start making this souffle. Remember when we all went and I got into a bit of trouble over a hat? Your friend's was lovely, but mine might have been... over the top? Definitely over the top! But, it was fun. I do wish we could have managed to attend this year though. It'd be a new challenge, and if I'm honest, things have been quite stressful lately. The interview was... intense, but I did my best. We'll just have to keep our fingers crossed then. While we're at it, I was thinking of getting a new phone case. This one is really done for. I saw a nice new one on sale the other day, something quite elegant but also practical. And it's always fun to get something new for the phone, Ah, I know what you mean. There's something satisfying about a new phone accessory. You know what, during the company dinner the other day for the book launch, I realized how much work we all put into our own particular ways of presenting ourselves, you know? Accessories, style, all of it. It really is about that intersection of professional and personal, isn't it? Definitely. Though sometimes, there’s also the danger of going overboard.

Hey, I'm on a film marathon right now and decided to watch some classic scary films. I just finished watching 'The Exorcist' and let me tell you, it's scarier than I remember. You should be here to see the look on my face! Oh, I’ve heard of 'The Exorcist'. It’s one of those films where the build-up and suspense make it truly terrifying. Although, I have to admit, I'm more of a fan of 'The Conjuring.' Ah, that's an interesting choice. I haven’t seen it in a while. It’s definitely a good one. 'The Exorcist' was rough on me, though, especially the possession scenes. The acting is superb though, right? Definitely, the acting in 'The Exorcist' is incredible. But 'The Conjuring' has its own special way of creeping under your skin, doesn’t it? It's more psychological horror, which sometimes makes it even scarier because you can't predict when it's going to come. Absolutely. Sometimes it's the things you can't see or explain that are the most frightening, like in this film. You ever watch 'Paranormal Activity'? The first one is the scariest to me, just because of the way it was shot. It makes the entire experience feel very real and invasive. Yeah, 'Paranormal Activity' is definitely unsettling. But have you ever tried watching 'Insidious'? It’s got this really deep build-up in the beginning, really sets the scene for things to go wrong, and the 'flying dream' scene will definitely get your heart racing. Actually, no! I haven't watched that one yet. I might add it to my list then. Speaking of build-ups, 'The Shining' is great at that. More slow burn than anything, but just the atmosphere... it's unnerving. Oh, 'The Shining' is a masterpiece. The atmosphere really is everything. From the tension to the setting of the hotel, everything just adds to the feeling of isolation and danger. Definitely. What’s your take on 'A Quiet Place' and 'Get Out'? Both take a different approach to horror but they're both really effective. Both are fantastic films for different reasons. 'A Quiet Place' uses almost complete silence to create tension which is really innovative. You almost feel like you should be quieter while watching it! 'Get Out' on the other hand uses social commentary in a very clever way, so it’s just as much horror as it is a critique on certain themes.

Ah, I'm so glad we could catch up tonight, Dad. I was just going through some of the emails from work and noticed a few things we could look at together. You mean the usual indispensable emails that can't wait till the morning, eh? Something like that. But I also wanted to chat about this gadget I'm thinking of buying. I saw it online and it looks like it would be really useful for school. This one keeps coming up in a lot of tech reviews. Oh, an iPad. I've had my fair share of gadgets over the years, but I never really got into tablets. Yeah, but this one is supposedly really good for drawing and writing notes. What's wrong with a good old-fashioned notebook and pen? Well, it's not that. It's just...some of my students might benefit from it, you know? Maybe even help them with writing and drawing. I suppose so, especially if it's easier for them to use. I'm all for making learning more accessible. But do you really think it's necessary? I think so, yes. Some of the kids really struggle with handwriting and stuff. It might really help them. And I could probably even manage the technology easily for lessons. I remember when all we had were paper and pencils at school. And look at us now, we're talking about all these gizmos. Okay, okay. True. I'm just trying to do my best for the kids, you know? Of course, I know. I'm just saying, a few changes, and we're sitting in a whole different world now. Yes, I know. I really should've saved you from listening to all the technological changing times. Don't worry, dear, I'm old but I'm not obsolete yet. Speaking of which, have you explored Airbnb? It's been quite the experience for us and it's even made planning holidays more accessible and affordable. As if I needed more things to keep up with! But no, I haven't looked into it. My holidays were always more about counting the pennies and making sure we could afford a nice cottage somewhere. I know, the older generation can always be counted on for frugal traveling tips. You'll make a fine accountant one day, young one. Thanks, Dad. I'll take that as a compliment.

Ah, I'm so glad we could find some time to get together. I've been meaning to catch up for ages. How are things with the studies department? It's all well. You know how it is. Endless reports to write and students to help through their own research drama. But we're managing. I can imagine. Speaking of drama, have you been into anything new in terms of books lately? Or perhaps you've taken up any travel? I've just finished 'Kitchen', it was quite moving. Ah, 'Kitchen'. I'm thinking of picking it up, actually. I've been lazy with my reading lately. What did you think of it beyond just being moved? It just felt very real, you know? The way each character was weighted in life, and then the big questions they start to ask themselves. And the writer’s voice is wonderful. It's one of those books that makes you feel like you've met the characters, even if you haven’t. Right. And you’re always on about this kind of thing, aren’t you? Aye, I suppose so. I don’t know, it feels important to me that stories ground us, you know? Remind us of our roots and all that while also challenging us. I see where you're coming from, really. It's like the books you connect with the most are often those that force you to re-evaluate your own life experiences. Speaking of which, have you considered writing in any capacity? You have a knack for understanding people through words and all that. Oh, I don't know, I've thought about it a couple of times but the nagging voice of self-doubt always seems to kick in before I can even start. Plus, my work already involves communicating. Seems like the best way for me to help tell people’s stories. That said, since we're at Brucefield Farm now, this could be a good place to start if you really wanted to write some descriptive pieces. The setting is changing a bit from what it used to be, might be an interesting backdrop. True. I hadn't looked at it like that before. You're right, the farm has so much history. It could indeed make for fascinating writing. Speaking of history and change, have you been following what's been happening in Edinburgh this year?

Hey Mum, did you have any chance to look at the job application I was going to apply for? It's for an architectural role at a reputable firm in central London. Oh, sorry love, I've been meaning to. It's just that the days have been a bit of a blur lately. What kind of role is it exactly and what makes you think you'd be good for it? It's a position as a sustainable architect, designing buildings with environmental considerations in mind. They specifically mentioned working with local councils and rebuilding existing infrastructure to be more green. It seems like a really interesting project and it aligns perfectly with my interests and experience from my Postgrad. That sounds perfect for you then. Is there any particular part of the job description you're concerned about or feel uneasy about? Not really. It's mainly just that this is a pretty stellar company and I want to make sure my application stands out. It's a very competitive field and I know they'll have hundreds of applications. That's true. But you've got so much experience and knowledge already, and what you lack in years on the job, you make up for it with passion and relevance. Remember when you were working on that community project in your studies? You specifically designed a sustainable housing system for a low-income area. That could be really relevant to highlight. Yeah, exactly! I think that project could be a key point for them to see my commitment to sustainable design. Maybe I should expand on it in the cover letter or talk about it during the interview if they ask about my experience. That's a great idea. Plus, it's always good to talk about what tangible impact you've had rather than just skills. And do you know who the head of the department is? Sometimes, if you can find out who the recruiter or hiring manager is, you can do a bit of research and tailor your application to be more relatable. Ah, actually, I did a bit of digging. It's Mrs. Edwardes and she's been quite vocal about the firm changing the way architecture impacts the environment. You know how I can do a bit of advanced research sometimes? I found some of her public talks online and saw she often mentions the importance of community outreach in sustainable projects.

Ah, good day everyone. Lovely to see you all's here. I hope today's no too dreary, weather's been less than desirable lately don't ya think? You're right John, it's been raining almost non-stop now, grass is practically floating! But hey, what can you do? It's England after all, we're used to a bit of rain, right? Anyways, welcome back to your place, John. Thanks Sarah. It's always great to have you here. You know how it is, routine can get pretty dull if you don't have a bit of company. Definitely. I've been stuck in the same 4 walls for ages, it's nice to catch up with others. How about we turn the old TV on, perhaps there's a decent film on or a programme you guys want to watch? That's a thought. I've been meaning to watch that new ITV drama. But first, grab a cup of tea, it's still hot in the pot. Sure thing, I'll bring some milk too. I'll grab a couple of biscuits while I'm at it, while the kettle's on. So, how've things been? Any new developments in your lives? Well, I couldn't have asked for a quieter life than when I retired from childminding. But it's been hellishly busy the past few months with babysitting for our nephews and nieces, so I've not had much time for much else. Yeah, I've tried to keep myself busy with gardening but the weather's been against me. Next job is to get me greenhouse sorted but without any income, it's been tough. I'll tell ya that. We all sit here twiddling our thumbs waiting for something to happen, that's for sure. You know, it's funny, but I've found a bit of solace in reading lately. I've discovered a love for English literature, something I never had the chance to explore while working. That's great! I used to love those Saturday afternoon readings, you know? The wireless. Nowadays, it's all so digital. I miss the tactile quality of a book sometimes. I wouldn't know anything about that digital stuff anyways. My old mind can't wrap itself around it. Well, there's still a lot to be said for simplicity. But youth today, I'm told, are pretty savvy with these new-fangled contraptions.

Ah, good morning Peter. I've been thinking about our plans for the Grace House today. The space is looking more and more promising and I believe we've got potential to generate even more income if we open various activities to more of the community. Good morning, Liz! You're awfully enthusiastic this morning. What kind of activities have you got in mind? I remember last summer we had those workshops and children's classes, they generated some good buzz and useful income right? Yes, absolutely. Our budget is still a bit stretched even with the money we get from hire. We could try and negotiate a bit better with some of those new companies coming in. I’ve been thinking about creating a little arts studio on the weekends or evening classes in things like yoga, that kind of thing. Interesting. The yoga in particular could be big now with the whole "well-being" push everywhere. Though I have to say, our facilities manager responsibilities have been keeping me busy - finding decent storage options for all our supplies, and we need to sort the fire escape inspections, you know? Can't stress those enough. Absolutely, those are all legitimate concerns, especially the fire escape. I'm looking this up actually on the government website - it seems like we need to have a professional do the initial assessment. Where did you get the last time? Was it Brix's in-house maintenance crew? No, not the last time. We used an external company for that. It's always a bit of an upfront cost, but as you say, it's non-negotiable in terms of safety really. But you're right, we should also be considering some storage solutions. I found that through a conversation with one of our regular tenants - they have a fantastic team redesigning the use of space which we could learn from. That's brilliant, thanks for the tip. We could actually invite them in for a meeting, a sort of workshop for the rest of us. I'm sure our tenants would love to share some of their strategies. That's a great idea, but we should also keep an eye on the holiday cover next month. You know how it can be a challenge to find staff willing to cover when some are off. Our standard contractors are usually reliable, but just in case...

Everybody, I hope you're all enjoying the holidays here in beautiful Hereford. Indeed, we are. This cottage has a wonderful charm to it. And I love how close the countryside is for nice walks. Especially if you're interested in local produce. Speaking of which, have you all seen the local farmer's market near the town center? Ah, yes, we went there yesterday. It's a fantastic place to pick up some fresh foods before we start cooking, isn't it? Absolutely, I got some amazing cheeses and hams. And I brought back some excellent Welsh lamb. Oh, brilliant! We can do a mix of traditional British and Welsh dishes here. That was my plan too. Let's have a Welsh English fusion feast. I think that'd be wonderful. And maybe we can ask Howard to do some roasting of this lamb. I'd love to. I've been practicing some new herb seasoning for lamb roasts. That sounds excellent. Do we also have enough potatoes? We did pick up some lovely roasting potatoes from the market yesterday. And isn't it time we start planning for Christmas dinner? Yes, but first, let's enjoy this holiday dinner together. Well, I think the plan now is to gather all the ingredients we need, and then start prepping for tonight’s meal. Seems like the kitchen's our battlefield tonight. I'll be our general. And I'll be the quartermaster. As long as my roast lamb gets a front row seat. I can help with any of the prep work if needed. That's very kind of you, Eirlys . And we almost forgot about Howard’s famous cawl. Yes, we can make that for tomorrow or maybe as a starter tonight. Sure, but I propose we start with some lighter dishes... How about some Welsh rarebit to start? That sounds perfect. What about some herby scones too? Great idea! I'll help with the scones, don't worry. And perhaps some finish with a nice apple crumble, a classic British dessert. That’s lovely! A bit of everything for everyone. Howard’s lamb, Eirlys ’s cawl, my rarebit, your scones... And my apple crumble. We have to make sure there's enough for the remaining guests, don't we? Though I think today might be more a family session. Agreed. And we can always make a big hearty supper together.

Hey, I'm on my way home from work, can I pick you up? On the road, we can talk about what we're up to this weekend? Cheers, sounds good! Are you still keen on heading into town for that new restaurant everyone's talking about, or is there something else on your mind this week? Yeah, I'd definitely like to try that out, but my colleague just mentioned they're watching a film and drinking at the new multiplex cinema out in the suburbs? They said it's really immersive and stylish. Are you up for something else instead? Oh, that sounds cool. I've been meaning to catch up on some old movies since I got back from that project last week. Yeah, same. I've been so busy at work, but my big project is finally almost over. Just need to finish this bit on compiling corpus data and everything should be sorted. That sounds important, good on you. I know how it feels, been tied up with these contracts at work too. You ever thought about taking a break and escaping the city for a bit? I was thinking maybe we could head down to Newcastle for this festival they've got coming up. Newcastle is lovely, especially around this time of year. I love the vibe. But don't they have St. George’s Day celebrations coming up too? Maybe we can fit in some time there. Exactly! The street performances and local music are always highlights for me. And you know I love all the good food they have there, it's really the best of the north. Definitely worth a trip. How about we check the festival dates and if they clash we plan something else around it? Perfect, let's make sure to do that the first chance. Say, have you noticed any good adverts lately? I was thinking of grabbing a new gadget or something since my phone's been playing up. Yes! There's this great spot for an augmented reality gaming console. I saw it last week and it caught my attention. You'd really enjoy it, especially since it's out of your usual area of work - something completely different for a change. That could be interesting. I’ve always enjoyed trying new things, especially if it has anything to do with software or engineering principles. Right, and speaking of tech, have you seen this new music streaming site I joined?

Thank you so much for inviting me over to your place, I've been meaning to catch up. It's been ages. How are you and the family doing? Thanks for coming! We're all just doing our best, really. You know how it is, life gets busy. Speaking of which, have you had any kind of medical appointment recently? Hospital stays can be quite daunting, aren't they? Oh, I'm actually struggling right now. My mum... I had to take her to hospital about a fortnight ago. They've given her a pretty bleak prognosis. Oh, I'm so sorry. I can imagine how tough that must be for you and your family. It is, but we're trying to be as positive as we can. We're just following the doctors' advice and making the most of the time we have together. That's exactly what you need to do. You know, last year, it was my sister who was going through a bit of a rough patch health-wise. We were all really worried, but thankfully she's on the mend now. I'm glad to hear your sister is doing better. It can be so upsetting seeing loved ones in pain. It is really unsettling. And the waiting... you can spend so many hours sitting in hospitals, worrying about what news you'll get next. Exactly. But as I said, we're taking it one day at a time. That’s the approach to take. I've found that it helps to have things to focus on beyond the hospital visits. Like our conversation here today, for example. More pleasant distractions would be a blessing right now. Do you need any support with getting her to appointments or anything? I know personally how hard it can be, but also how much a friendly face can help. Thank you so much for offering. I really do appreciate it. I've got a few friends who are helping out but more hands are always useful. No problem at all. And if you need someone to talk to or just some moral support, don't hesitate. That means a lot. Speaking of ups and downs, did you hear about... well, about the funeral I'm having to sort out for an uncle? No, I hadn't. I'm so sorry to hear that. How are you handling all the arrangements?

Right, so everyone's seen the photos from my last trip to Chile. I brought back so many bottles of wine and even some instructions on how to make a traditional Chilean dish. Cool, can you cook Chilean food really well now? I'd say I do okay, but I haven't had the chance to serve it up yet. Ah, Chile! I wish I could have gone with you. I was tied up at work, but I saw some of your posts. The Andes look epic from what I saw. Totally! I spent a few days exploring the mountains. It was fantastic. What's the best wine you've had from Chile? Well, I was really impressed by the Cabernet Sauvignon from the Maipo Valley. It's rich and full-bodied. I've had that too—it's excellent. Did you visit any specific winery in the valley? Yes, I did. I went to this beautiful place called Casa Lapostolle. They have some amazing reds and even a really nice visitor center. That sounds different from anything we have here. You’re always going to these cool places. It’s a lot of fun to explore different parts of the world. Though, sometimes I just want to stay in my own backyard and enjoy nice British food and perhaps a walk in the country. True! There’s something really special about walking in the countryside of the UK. We have fantastic local food and drinks here too. Absolutely, it's the same with the Midlands. There’s this really good cheese from a local farm near Fradley if I remember right. Indeed! The Midlands has some of the best cheeses in the country. The local pubs serve a lot of those. Speaking of local, did anyone hear about the skiing trip that’s being planned? Yes, sure. There was some talk after dinner about planning a weeklong trip to the Alps next winter if everyone can make it. Ah! That would be so much fun. I've never been skiing but I've seen it and want to try. I could use a break from work and it sounds like a great idea. Maybe I could even take some time off and join if we can coordinate. We’ll need to make sure everyone’s schedules are clear. For me, it just depends when my marketing projects are finalized. I’m definitely interested!

Ah, I love going through old photos like this. It's amazing how vivid our memories still are of those moments, even after all these years. Oh, definitely! I've always found that looking through old photos really brings back all the emotions and sensations of the time. It kind of makes me want to get back into taking more photos. Like this one, for example . I think this was right at the start of our Japan trip, wasn't it? Yeah! Can you believe it's been years since then? This one's really good, though, isn't it? Even with my less-than-fluent photography skills back then, it's still really evocative. Well, I think that's part of the magic of good photography - it doesn't have to be technically perfect to capture the spirit of the moment. Like this photo of the cherry blossoms in Kyoto. We were looking for the perfect angle, and we kept getting distracted by those badgers over by the food stalls! Ah yes, the badgers! I remember that day. So many of us were lined up and they were just gobbling up all their nuts and whatnot, with complete disregard for everyone else! Exactly! It was quite surreal. They were almost like tiny furry locals, really getting on with their day, while we were all there desperately trying to get a good shot. Like tourists, I suppose! I've been thinking about maybe trying to go back to Japan. It’s a bit chaotic with work and all that, but I've always been drawn back there. Oh, that would be amazing! Perhaps we could plan a trip for next year? We could do it during cherry blossom season again. Maybe we’d get better photos this time! That would be wonderful. I'd love to see the cherry blossoms with you again. As long as we don’t get distracted by badgers and end up with a photo series of cute, overfed critters instead! At least it would be a different kind of local wildlife photography. Oh, and have you seen this one? I think this was taken at this really tiny local café in Tokyo. The owner was so nice and we ended up having an amazing conversation. She even gave us some local recommendations. Oh, I love that! Those kind of serendipitous moments are often the best part of travel.

Right, so everyone's seen the photos from my first trip to Ireland. I discovered today that nearly every pub there serves an absurdly large breakfast. I don't know if you guys saw the Instagram post, but I managed to shove down a full Irish breakfast. It was madness, but hilarious. Oh, I've had those breakfasts before! And totally agree, they're a part of the fun. Have you ever tried skinny dipping? I did it once at a lake in the countryside and it was bizarrely exhilarating. Oh, we should try arranging a skinny dipping trip – somewhere discreet, of course! Speaking of trips, have any of you guys been to Australia? I've heard so much about it. As an Australian, I feel like I should say we're all well-dressed and have stellar table manners. Jokes aside, Australia's amazing. The landscapes are stunning, the beaches are incredible, and the wildlife – well, you have to be careful with the wildlife. And it's funny because despite being so far from the rest of the world, or maybe because of it, our culture is a really unique mix. Right! The different mix is fascinating. I once read this poetry by an Australian while studying 'diverse cultural influences on written literature.' It was quite interesting, actually. Do you guys ever think about a zombie apocalypse? Honestly? All the time, especially when I'm making bread in batches at the bakery. One time, I even joked with a customer about how we’d barricade the bakery with all the bread… would that work as a zombie barricade? That's kind of genius. Speaking of genius ideas, have you guys heard of Claudia Roden? She’s written this incredible Jewish cookbook and her recipes are always matched with interesting anecdotes. Speaking of food, I once made some of her recipes for a cultural meet-up at the café. It was a hit, but I think I might have missed a key ingredient in the stuffed cabbage. Oh, Claudia Roden? She's amazing. Her stories about Jewish food often capture a sense of community and tradition that truly fascinates me. I've always been interested in how food ties into cultural identity. Speaking of identity, does anyone have good Jewish jokes? Not sure if they're offensive or not, but... Well, there's the classic one: Why don’t Jewish people play hide and seek?

Hey, I'm so glad we could catch up without any distractions. I brought today's newspaper and we can talk about the articles related to our conversation topics. Cheers for that. You know I love diving into current events while munching on these peanuts, though I kind of regret bringing questions on border security just now. You've been researching for your PhD and I'm sure you could explain a lot to me. True, but I've been out of academia for a while and it's good to get out of my research bubble. Plus, how else can we apply all knowledge if not to discuss, explain, and sometimes debate. Exactly, and I've been wanting to get a better grasp of the complexities and the reasons why certain policies are as they are. But let’s start with something a bit more light-hearted. What's been your favorite computer game lately? Oh, oh - I’ve just been hooked on this one fantasy role-playing game. It's amazing how big the community is and the strategy it involves. It’s like every decision you make has consequences, which I find fascinating. I’m more of a strategy and puzzle game person, but I’ve played that one as well. I think what really got me was the world-building. It’s so detailed and immersive. It’s a shame though, we never seem to have enough time for those now that life gets busy. Completely agree. Like, my last visit to a theme park was years ago. I can only imagine how much more impressive they’ve become with all the advancements and all. What do you think about that? Theme parks… they’re like a hellscape and the best place at the same time, aren’t they? I mean, the technology and design just improve so much year-over-year. But yes, definitely need to do that more. We could, for instance, do a ‘theme parks world tour’. Get to all those famous ones, and maybe even discover some hidden gems. That’s exactly what I’ve been dreaming of. You know, Birmingham’s theme park, they’re actually planning a new ride next year – I heard it’s going to be completely VR experience. Birmingham? That’s so local for me. I might have to see if I can get an early preview. But have you heard about the film about those kids who turned theme parks into giant escape rooms?

Ah, I'm so glad we could meet up here, Kim. It's been ages since we grabbed a meal together. How are you, by the way? I'm good, thanks for asking. It's been quite a while since we last caught up, hasn't it? How's life treating you, Sheila? It's been okay, you know. Busy with teaching and all that but I’ve recently taken up rowing. Really? That sounds quite challenging. Oh, it's a whole different ball game. You'd think it's just about pushing and pulling but there's so much about timing and coordination. I can imagine. I've tried kayaking and it's even harder than I thought. Exactly! But the feeling when you get it right is amazing. I want to try it out one day. You should. It's a lot of fun and you can actually join a club here in Cambridge. I'll keep that in mind. What was the hardest part about learning this skill? At first, it was the different rowing techniques. But most difficult was getting the hang of the timing – it's about pushing with the legs first, then leaning back and pulling with the arms. That does sound tricky. It is, but once you get the hang of it, you feel a sense of satisfaction, really. It’s great that you're keeping active. It is, and I've found that it's helped me unwind too. Speaking of things that help with unwinding... I've been trying to find some decent waterproof clothing for kayaking. Every time I go out, I always end up soaking wet. Oh, that's a nightmare! Yes, I've also been on the hunt for some good waterproof gear. Yes, and it’s harder than I thought. Absolutely. I've looked for reviews online but it's just so much information, isn't it? And it's always about trying different things until you find what works best for you. Did you find anything you could recommend? Not really yet. But I did find that looking for brands that specialize in outdoor gear is a good starting point. Oh, that makes sense. Yes, and for rowing, they often have specific clothing designed for that unique movement. That's interesting. I'll look into that. Oh, by the way, did you ever meet Lucy, from the family side?

Dad, I'm so nervous about tomorrow! Results day can't come soon enough but also not nearly soon enough. Well don't panic, little one! You've worked hard. You'll be fine. What if we squeeze in a study session now? Nah, I think I'm done for now. Besides, Morse code or texting? Texting, obviously. It's so much easier to convey emotions via emojis, right? Absolutely! Morse code for “emojis” keeps coming backwards. Anyway, how would you like to hear your results first? Text, voice call? Depends on Vodafone, lol. Hopefully we don't get a London signal here in Manchester like last time. But seriously, texting would be safer in front of my friends. Then I can compose myself before telling everyone. Fair point. Careful with Vodafone there, they've got a notorious signal sometimes. But, your mum’s been on the phone a lot, arranging food shopping for the dinner tonight. How about you help her pick between these amazon delivery options or or go eBay for any last-minute stationery? Ebay for stationary sounds good! Oh, I found the perfect pen. It’s heavy and writes smoothly. Only if it’s not leaking at university. Remember that fountain pen incident? Not on us again! Haha, no, Dad. I learned my lesson. Also, speaking of university, how silly is it that we still use paper for some things? They’re still selling glass water bottles there, but mostly it’s all digital. I don’t think anyone understands Morse code anymore. Morse code has its place. Just last weekend, we helped a new neighbor with some DIY who had no signal upstairs. He communicated with us via flashlight - beginner’s Morse code! I'd probably need a cheat sheet for that. Texting seems so much more practical nowadays. Legit or not, show me the link and we can decide. Also, what about student finance? Done any thinking on budgeting or job hunting? I started reading up but my head’s all in a whirl. I know I need to make money somehow, maybe do some part-time work. But it’s like I’ve realized university is like a mini-city.

Ah, man, it's so good to see you, mate. Took us ages to finally catch up. How's uni going and how are you keeping up with the exams? It's all good, thanks for asking. Uni is intense now, the pressure’s on with all the deadlines and exams. But I've been managing so far. What about you, how are you getting on? To be honest, I'm right there with you. What are you guys studying about Japan in your class? We mainly looked into how their tech industry has developed so much over the years. It’s fascinating how they’re on the cutting edge with everything from robotics to software. I’ve been considering taking a gap year maybe and planning a trip. You should totally join me. That’s a solid idea. It'll not only help us financially but also give us a valuable experience to add to our CVs. But what’s your plan for the next few months before we could head out? Well, I’m finishing off my semester with a couple of exams to pass, and then I’ll start applying to some tech companies.

Ah, I'm so excited about our upcoming trip to the Lakes. I've been looking at some of the pictures from last year and I just can't wait to go back. You love walking in the Lakes, don’t you? I've just signed us both up for a photography club trip on Facebook. It's just for local folk but they often have tips and group hikes. Oh, I've heard about those, actually. Now, don't get too caught up with social media. It can be time-consuming keepsakes for trips like this. Remember when we used to just bring back physical photos? Oh Grandpa, you're just old fashioned! But yes, we did have those physical photos. Still, social media’s helpful for getting in touch with our friends who can recommend us spots we might have missed. And this photography club tour sounds wonderful. Exactly. We should also be thinking about insurance, though. While we plan the vacation, let's make sure our policies cover travel. That reminds me - did any of you see the news about David Cameron? I’m not surprised it turned out he had some ties to tax havens. Yes, it's all very suspicious. Makes you wonder about the integrity in politics. It also really highlights the importance of responsible financial management. Well, at least for us, we prioritize making sure we're covered for any eventuality, tax havens or not. True, true. Alright, I'm glad you're all responsible about that. But speaking of responsible - doesn’t anyone else think that it's about time we talked about that cruise we've been considering for our next big trip? Oh, the cruise? Yes, that would be wonderful! How about we research and plan that for after the Lakes? I've been dreaming of a voyage to the Mediterranean. Mediterranean's lovely, but I’ve heard great things about cruises to Scandinavia too. You get to see the Northern Lights, which would be a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Wonderful! But for now, let's make sure our cars are in good shape so we can travel to the Lakes safely. I remember last time we went to Buckfast Abbey, we had a bit of trouble with Gran's car. Yes, and this time we should consider looking into services like AA or RAC just in case. Totally agree.

Mum, Dad, I'm so glad I could finally catch up with you. I've missed talking to you both. How was your holiday in Belgium? Ah, it was lovely, dear. You know how much we love exploring new places. The food was just amazing, especially the waffles – we discovered this fantastic little cafe just outside Ghent. Yeah, the whole thing was very quaint and fun. I wish I could’ve joined you actually, but I had to work. And how was driving in Belgium? I’ve heard people say it can be a bit tricky with all those roundabouts. True, it took some getting used to but we used that SAT NAV faithfully. Though let me tell you, even then, sometimes we ended up in the most unexpected places. Like this one time Dad and I almost ended up driving into the city centre by mistake. It was a fun adventure though! OMG, I can imagine. So did you try the cycling? I’ve been reading so much about the cycling infrastructure in Belgium. Yes, we did! We rented bikes for a day in Bruges and it was brilliant. The paths were so well-maintained. You’re right about that, the infrastructure is top-notch. If only we had the time and stamina to explore further, right, Mum? Perhaps next time, but nice for you both to enjoy it as much as you did. Speaking of which, I’ve been thinking about maybe buying a new bike too. That sounds like a great idea! I could help you shop doesn’t matter if it's a road bike or a mountain bike? Actually, I’m thinking of getting one for commuting. Maybe something not too flash or expensive but practical and comfortable. Oh, I saw a nice local shop near here in Brighton that gets good reviews. Next time you come over, we can pop in together if you’d like. That would be great! And Dad, how are you finding retirement? It’s been a year now, isn’t it? It’s... busy. I wasn’t prepared for it. I always thought I’d want to travel more, but turns out I actually enjoy the routine of working. However, it’s definitely given me the chance to focus on my interests and community work. You’ve been involved in those gardening projects, haven’t you? Yes, and I’ve also taken up some woodworking.

Ah, I'm so glad we could finally schedule this cooking night. I've been meaning to try these new recipes from that food blogger from the Midlands. Me too, and I've been meaning to experiment with some new fragrances for our dinner. You know how candles can really set the mood for dinner, right? Oh absolutely! I've got a lovely lavender and orange blossom one that matches our floral theme tonight. And you, why don't you use that new cedarwood and orange set you bought last week? We keeps coming across it on Facebook. It seems like everyone from my school friends to some colleagues are using it for their lazy Sunday afternoons. You're right. Everyone's suddenly an online perfumier or florist. Do you remember that one friend from university though, she really does have a good eye for that. She started selling her own homemade potpourri and scented candles. Oh, yes! I kept seeing her creations pop up in my feed. Did she ever get into this kind of thing professionally or is she still doing it as a hobby? As far as I know it's still quite informal. She's a marketing specialist by trade but enjoys the craft. Speaking of fun hobbies, while the food is cooking, would you like to light the fireplace and make it cosy? Sounds perfect! Let's do that. You know, it's interesting how different regions in Britain have distinct fireplace traditions. I never realized how much until I moved here from Edinburgh. I know what you mean! Even accents change a lot from London to the north. I always notice the slight differences in vocabulary, pronunciation... do you find you still slip into your Edinburgh accent sometimes? Sometimes, especially when I'm tired or when I'm around people from home. But funnily enough, living in London for so long, I've picked up this Londoner's way of saying things, but I still use a word here and there from Edinburgh. We could sit here and discuss accents all night! Yes! But for now, let's enjoy the scent of the cedarwood and the delicious food coming up! Can you see if our friend would like to join us for dinner next weekend? Sure, I'll drop her a message. Maybe she could even bring some more of those scented candles or potpourri.

Ah, I've always wanted to teach in Australia, but never had the chance. I heard the students are very open and enthusiastic about learning. Have any of you had the opportunity to work or teach there? Yes, I did work for a short time in Australia as a company director, though that was years ago. It was quite an experience, the pace and culture were vastly different than back home. The "laid-back" attitude that they're so famous for... it actually influenced how I managed my staff back in the UK. Speaking of keeps changing, I've always been fascinated by the differences in dialects across Britain, especially in Scotland and the North. Have you heard about the Sheffield dialect, with its distinctive rhotic pronunciations and northernisms? Oh, absolutely! As an EFL teacher, we often used dialect samples from around the UK to illustrate pronunciation differences. What's interesting is how strong dialectal identity is in certain regions, like Sheffield, but its influence on standard English pronunciation is sometimes overlooked. That's very true. I find similar characteristics in the North of England as well. You know, I once had to accommodate a Scottish or a Yorkshire accent when translating a document. It was a challenge, but quite rewarding. Exactly! I often tell my students that learning English is not just about the textbook version. Dialects and regional variations are a real part of communication, not just an interesting side note. Have you encountered any issues with language barriers while in Australia? Not as much, surprisingly. There is a large British expat community, and for the most part, we’re used to communicating with different accents. But it's not just about speaking. The cultural doesn’t come across in language classes. It’s about the implicit values, behaviors... that’s harder to teach. Right, and it can be quite different from what we expect from British culture. How did you fare with the Australian bank loans, for example? I hear that the banking system is quite different. It was manageable, but figuring out ins and outs like mortgages and credit scores was a challenge. It reminded me of my time in the States, actually. Interesting. I teach in a city with a high student intake of international students. A lot of them want to learn 'standard' English, but we also help them understand local nuances. That must be rewarding.

Ah, I'm so glad we could find this vegan restaurant here. I've been meaning to try more plant-based food since my last visit to Spain. Oh, that sounds like a great experience. I’ve been doing that for a while now. Actually, the podcast, “The Plant Paradox” has really encouraged me to explore more about the diet and lifestyle. "The Plant Paradox"! I've heard about it, actually. I've been trying to reduce my meat intake and it’s not easy when traveling, keeps coming across loads of local meat dishes everywhere. Definitely, yes. It was such an eye-opener for me. I just had to learn how to navigate pubs and restaurants more effectively. It’s like speaking a different language sometimes. “Talking plant” maybe? What’s been your favorite thing you’ve learned or discovered? Well, it's been really interesting how it links to how our bodies process certain foods, like lectins and how they affect inflammation. But also the environmental impact of reducing animal products. That's really enlightening. We really don’t think about it until we start learning about it. Exactly. And funnily enough, while I was listening to the podcast, I started following the author, Dr. Gundry, on social media. It’s surprising how much you can learn about how people take to adopting new lifestyles from just observing their posts. Oh, isn’t it? I find it fascinating how social media can both be a positive and a negative influence. For sure. It can definitely open up new horizons but sometimes it also feels like we’re kind of living inside this curated bubble, especially with accounts that focus on one’s perceived ‘perfect’ life. Absolutely. Have you noticed the same thing with the shift towards podcasts? It feels like everyone is either listening or producing one now. Definitely. There’s a huge array now, which is changing the way we consume information. I was listening to one recently about…I think it was called “The Rise of the Instagram Cleansing”? It’s about how a lot of these wellness gurus and so-called nutritional experts are really just trying to sell us things. That’s so interesting and sad at the same time. I find it upsetting that people can just brand themselves as experts and put anything out there without much accountability. Yes, and what’s concerning is how easily some of these podcasts get into your head.

Hey everyone, gather round for a bit of family conversation. We've got some fun today planned; we're going to play with Pippy and Blue Peter, and talked about whether ANON would really be interested in a Blue Peter badge. Blue Peter badge! Wow, that's so cool! Why does ANON want one? Because last week we were looking at a book with a Blue Peter badge and ANON seemed really interested, especially the part about being on TV! Right! And we even thought about how we can get a photograph for the badge. You'll need to do some good work or help someone in need. Like offering to help at the beach, or helping out with something here at home. I think ANON likes helping with the cats. Could that be something good for the badge? Yeah, that might be a good idea. ANON loves the cats so much, I'm sure helping them would count as doing good. Definitely. It's all about showing kindness and responsibility. And if we're successful, we should also talk about what next. Like joining a local scouts group or something similar. So, we need to take a photograph of ANON doing good. Where should we do it? Maybe at the local park? ANON could help pick up rubbish or something like that. It's good for the environment too! That's a fantastic idea. I love how we're all thinking together here. And in all seriousness, if ANON is considering something like scouting or a club, it'll also help with learning to plan events like this, and learn about responsibilities. Speaking of responsibilities, how about pocket money for ANON? Should we start now? We can link it to things like helping or doing good deeds. That could be a great idea. It teaches them the value of money and hard work. Absolutely. It’s about learning to appreciate the effort and the value you get from it. We could start with something simple like 50p for doing a chore or helping with dinner. I think ANON loves having money like that. It gives them a bit of independence too. Yeah, and we could help ANON save up for something special, maybe like a toy or a book. That would be a great way to learn about saving and planning for what you want. Brilliant! So, next on the agenda for ANON could be helping out more regularly and then we link that to pocket money.

Hey, I wanted to talk to you about something that's been bothering me. Yeah, what's up? You don't look yourself. You know how men can sometimes have trouble... um, you know, sustaining stuff? Oh, sexual performance issues? Yeah, that's a pretty common thing and it can happen for a variety of reasons, right? Exactly! I've been noticing it in Sam, and it's really stressing me out. Sam? Is this something Sam has told you about, or are you observing it? Well, we've talked about it a couple of times. He's just like, "I know, I know, I read online about erectile dysfunction and all that." But I don't think he's really dealing with it properly. It can be super tough for guys, especially if it's linked to stress or anxiety. But also, it's just biology sometimes. What if it's him feeling pressured or something? Yeah, he's under a lot of pressure this year with A-levels and everything. I worry it might be affecting him more than he's letting on. Definitely. You know, if he’s not open about it, it might also be a sign of deeper issues, like insecurity or fear about how he's perceived in his relationships. Like, perhaps he's anxious about being a "good enough" partner? That could be it. We've always had an open relationship, and I feel like we could talk about anything, but… this is somehow different. It feels too private for him. You should encourage him to talk about it more openly. Sometimes the fact that you're there to listen, without judgement, can help him feel more secure. I'm there to listen, but he doesn't even mention it unless I bring it up. Last time we talked, he just brushed it off and changing the subject. Well, maybe you need to find a better time to bring it up. Not in the middle of something stressful or when he’s anxious about something else. True, maybe we should plan a quiet evening together, like have a walk and talk about it then. Good idea. And you might want to let him know that we’re here to support him, not judge. It's also good to remind him that he's more than his ability to perform sexually. Absolutely. You're right, it’s not just about sex...

Hey, I'm going to make cauliflower cheese. We have enough cauliflower left from last week's veg box and I know we've got cheese in. That's a good choice! Is that for our dinner tonight? Yeah, do you want some? Yeah, sounds good! I'm going to get some quorn to add healthy extras. I'm still struggling with actually using those free foods I bought last week though. I've been more active recently though, I think that must be helping. Good job! Do you also exercise or just the physical activity from work? Both, to be honest. Good idea. I’ll text you a rough outline. And can we discuss our thinking on saving money? I just realized I'm losing money by not using the frylight properly - I hear it can work across multiple dishes and cuts down on the oil/fat used. Absolutely, I've noticed that too. Also, did you make any plans for your work targets this week?

Hey, I was thinking we might want to discuss our plans for the upcoming holiday. We still don't have anything set in stone, and I know we've been talking about wanting to do something different this year. You were mentioning something about Ireland, right? Yeah, I was. I kind of want to experience some of the real Irish culture instead of just staying in a resort and eating the food we get at home. Something like a food and drink tour, and of course, seeing the countryside. But we also need to budget it. The kids will be older this time, so maybe they can help with some of the planning too. That does sound good. We can check out some itineraries and see what's within our budget. And yes, involving the kids more with the planning is a great idea. They’re at that age where they can start to contribute ideas - though we might need to keep them focused on the budget aspect too! Definitely. And maybe we could combine the holiday with a creative project we both want to work on. Like, you want to start your travel blog and I want to try my hand at writing that fantasy novel I’ve been thinking about. Oh, that is an amazing idea! We could balance tourist activities with working on our writing. Plus, Ireland has such great scenery - lots of inspiration. Though, I might need more time at the end of the day to write - you can't keep up with an IT consultant’s workload easily! I know right, it’s good to have different schedules in that respect, isn’t it? Plus, we’re always talking about getting some downtime away from screens and stuff. This trip could be a nice reset for that. Absolutely. I was just thinking, what if we didn’t bring our phones with us or just had them for the really important stuff? Maybe just for emergencies or together as a family to plan the next day. The kids are so used to being constantly connected, it might actually be nice for them to have some time without it too. Brilliant! I was actually changing the subject to something hypothetical. What if we did a whole holiday without screens, no phones, tablets, anything? Like, back in the day. Just books and board games, talking and observing. That’s an interesting thought experiment.

Ah, I'm glad we're all gathered here tonight. We've got a lot to catch up on, haven't we? First and foremost, let's talk about the coming weekends. I have bookings for that weekend golf trip, right? And Alison isn't going because of the school concert, correct? Yes, that's right. You've already squared it with us and the group. Anyway, how about our other plans for the weekend before? I thought we agreed to a quiet lazy Sunday – perhaps a brunch at home and then going through some of those postcards you brought back from your holiday? Absolutely, I’m ready for that. Though I did find a few photos we could look at during brunch. And while we’re on the topic, have you thought about birthday cards and gifts yet? Well, I must admit, it’s an interesting topic – particularly given the implications for jobs, economy, and identity. Speaking of which, did you see that one political pundit's analysis? It was quite enlightening, I thought. Yes, I saw that. Though doesn’t it seem that every time the subject comes up the arguments are so different? Just last weekend at the pub, I overheard someone saying it’s all about economics and another saying it’s about cultural identity. Exactly, and that’s exactly why I find it fascinating. It's not just about money or politics; there's a deep dive into what it means to be part of a country or a union. You’re right. It’s complicated. I do wish we could discuss these topics more often. Anyway, I need to go for another helping of that pie – it’s absolutely delicious. I’m with you on that one. And maybe while we’re at it, we can start thinking about the postcards. I’d almost forgotten about those.

Everybody, I wanted to talk about something that came up at school today. We're discussing various ways to help the Syrian refugee crisis and my class decided we could start by drawing pictures for them. What do you think? Would be nice to send out some messages of hope and solidarity. That's such a lovely idea, mom! I've always loved drawing and I think kids like me can make the messages really special. And, like, they won't have as much of other stuff as we do there, won't they? Maybe it can make them feel better? Yeah, it's like when we get really good reports from school, it makes you feel good inside, doesn't it? These drawings could be like reports of kindness and friendship from us. Is that a good idea? Exactly. It's about showing we care and that we're thinking about making life better for them. So, have you thought about what kind of pictures we should draw? Maybe we could draw... how we imagine a chair for them? You know, like comfort. And it could be any kind of chair – maybe a rocking chair, a bean bag, whatever makes them feel cozy. We could draw it on a piece of paper and then... is it like a postcard or...? I think 'like a postcard' is a great idea. We can even add a little message on the back. And do you think we should draw more than one chair? Maybe different types for kids, adults, families? That's a wonderful idea, combining the chair for comfort with different life stages or situations, and all contexts they might find themselves in. Plus, it gives us plenty to talk about in terms of design and purpose. How about we start brainstorming this weekend and then we can make some sketches, and if everyone’s happy, we could consider sending them off? Yeah, I just thought, maybe we could do like a little chair for every person. If we do 20 chairs, that's like 20 acts of kindness from us. That’s quite a collection, right? Yes, and we might want to do a mix of advanced and simpler drawings. Some art for kids to relate to for sure. I know a few at school who are very skilled so we can ask them if they want to join too. That's brilliant!

Hey, I was thinking about our friends Rachel and Tom. We've not heard from them in a while. Have they moved to that new place yet? Oh, yeah, I remember they were supposed to move into their new house last month. I've just been meaning to catch up with them – do you have their contact details handy? I think so, yeah. Let me check my phone. Yes, here it is. Now, shall I pick up the phone and give them a quick call? That's a great idea. We could also send them a WhatsApp, but a quick call would be nice to check in properly. Hi Rachel, it’s Rachel speaking.. is this a good time? Oh, oh we're on speaker. They must be together. Oh! Wait Tom, Ron here. Hi how are you both? What have you guys been up to these past few weeks? How was the move? I don’t know, they might be a bit busy still. Yeah, well no, the move finished up last week. Kids are ok; settling in. Just been getting things to the right place, but otherwise all good. We're really excited, though – the new space is amazing. Shall we invite them over for dinner soon? It’s a good chance for us and they to catch up properly. That sounds great! Thanks for catching up with us. Actually, that’s a lovely idea, come over for dinner sometime soon. How about this weekend? We can have a low-key dinner, no fuss. Yes, that's perfect. I'll send them a message to finalize a time. You know they’re really good at cooking, especially these new recipes they’ve been trying. Yes, Tom’s so into trying different cuisines these days. Speaking of cooking, have you still got the recipe you found for that quiche Lorraine? Yeah, I think so. Why? We've got all the ingredients at home and I’ve been wanting to try making something new. Maybe this weekend could be a good time too? That’s a great idea! We could also make a DIY dinner with what we have at home. How about we plan a little menu? Yes, and then we can get Rachel and Tom over and make an evening of it. So, quiche Lorraine, maybe some roasted vegetables and a salad? We can do that. And maybe have a bottle of wine ready too, seeing as they’re coming for dinner.

Ah, isn't this just the most beautiful spot to take a walk? Look at that wildflower meadow over there, and the sunlight filtering through the trees. Absolutely! I don't think there's anything quite like the English countryside on a day like this. You know, I've always found questions about superstition quite intriguing. Do you have any particularly British superstitions you stick to? Well, I always touch wood when I wish for something good to happen. Not really religious about it, but it's become a habit! I also have to mention, there was this time when... Oh, you're telling a story about a lucky charm moment? Yes! So there was this time when I just had to have a certain exam passed for a project at the university. And of course, I brought my "lucky" wooden pin cushion to the exam room. It made me laugh, but it did actually make me feel calmer! That’s quite funny. I have to say, similar habits in various situations. But this reminds me of an old joke - Do you know why policemen always have such a firmly held belief in superstition? No, why? Because the sergeant always says, "You know, we can never have too many superstitions on the force; it often leads to a lucky break!" Well, that's certainly one way to keep everyone on their toes! A bit like how, at university, we'd pull all-nighters before a big exam, and then resort to ridiculous "good luck" charms. I know exactly what you mean! My friends and I would always "cleanse" the exam area with a certain song, like we were on some comedy challenge or something. And let me tell you, there was the time I went in with a total stranger who was also hitting the "lucky spot" on our table. Oh, that's just wrong and right at the same time! I guess changing the subject to publicity - have you noticed how they often try to sell us products using these weird, repetitive soundtracks for ads? Horrible, just horrible. I always hit mute so fast. Reminds me of trying to find a real holiday destination that's not overwhelmed by too much commercialism. Did you go anywhere nice this year? Yes, we went to Scotland. Ah, I'm losing my mind with this latest project at work. It's just stress after stress these days. How do you all manage your stress levels when things get overwhelming? Right, so as we're driving through this pretty village, I've been thinking about today's road trip topics. How about we talk about hilltop villages? Who here is a vegetarian or vegan? I've been thinking about vegetarianism for a while, but I still enjoy some cheese and fish occasionally. And I think that any type of farming—whether it's for synthetic meat, dairy, or veggies—needs to be done more sustainably and less cruelly.

Hey lads, what've you got planned for the weekend? Not much, just been hanging around the house and tinkering with my PC. Hey there, Sarah! Long time no see! How's life been treating you since we last spoke? It's been good, Helen! Just enjoying my life as a language research administrator here. How about you? Hey hun, did you finish reading that massages module from last week? I'm really struggling; these muscles and anatomy stuff is all a bit confusing. Yeah, I did. And it's great if you want to plant a mix of things in a small space. I love the idea of being able to plant a variety without using too much space. Do you know which specific plants are best suited for this layout? For beginners, it's often recommended to start with leafy greens, radishes, carrots, and herbs like basil and mint. They're all quite easy to grow and don't take up too much space. Plus, they're fast-growing, so you can see results quickly and can rotate the crops easily. That makes a lot of sense. I'm particularly interested in growing some herbs since we both love cooking. Yes, that's a great idea. There are also companion planting techniques you can look into. For example, basil grows well with lettuce and can help deter pests that target leafy greens. I wasn’t aware of that, but it's helpful to know. And what about tools? Do we have a comprehensive list of what we’ll need to get started? Excellent question. We’ll need basic gardening tools like trowels, a hoe or cultivator for weeding, possibly a rake for leveling the soil, and some watering can or a hose with a sprayer head.

Hey, I'm so glad we could catch up! I've been thinking a lot about what we discussed last time about balancing friendships and university work. Do you think you've found a good rhythm yet? Hey! Yeah, it’s been a bit of a struggle to be honest! But I’m getting there. It kind of helps to plan out my day and make sure there’s time for both studying and social stuff. That’s a great tip, thanks! Speaking of which, did you hear that Sarah and Jon are moving out of Doncaster? I was a bit surprised when she told me. Wonder what’s behind that? Oh, yeah! I saw that post on social media. I’m really going to miss them around. Might have to go up to Cambridge more often. Do you think there’s a party of some sort to celebrate or say goodbye? That’s a great idea. I can imagine they’d want to have one. We should definitely be there! How about we organize something? We could even start a group chat to get everyone’s thoughts on it. That’d be brilliant! I’ll talk to the others and see what they think. Maybe we can plan something fun for them before they go. It’s not easy to leave a place where you’ve had so many good times. Absolutely. It’s a lot like leaving home for uni, really. You form such strong bonds. Anyway, another thing. Are you still going to that indie gig at the weekend? I feel like we haven’t done much fun stuff in Doncaster lately. For sure! I couldn’t miss it. It’s always a highlight of the week. Plus, it’s a good chance to see some new and local talent. I might even recommend it to our Cambridge friends. Let’s all meet up for that and then plan the farewell party. Sounds like a plan. I’ll make sure to check the venue’s details. We should also invite them for another catch-up before they leave. It’ll be bittersweet, but it’s good to have these moments. Definitely. We should sit down and make a plan for both events. Don’t you think? Plus, I want to catch up with Sarah and Jon before they leave. We should take advantage of the time we have left.

Right, so did you finish Dark Souls? Yeah, nearly. I just got stuck on that boss fight at the Kiln of the First Flame. It's bloody tough. Is that where the game gets super challenging? I just started the PS4 remaster, but I heard rumors it's kind of brittle at times. Yeah, it's quite brittle at times, but stick with it. The game's worth it. Definitely worth it. But it can be... frustrating, to say the least. Especially when you're not used to the Soulsborne formula, you know? Fair point. I just need to learn how to pace myself. I did watch a few let's plays though to get an idea. Right, let's plays are actually really helpful. And yeah, it's all about learning your build and mastering certain patterns. Absolutely.
