I've played all the Dark Souls games. It's like learning a new language each time, but once you get it, it's so rewarding. I love the world-building too. The Forlorn Estates, it feels so atmospheric. Anyone plan to dive into Sekiro after this? Definitely interested. I heard the combat system's really refined. Have either of you tried any FromSoftware games before? I played Bloodborne. It was intense. The atmosphere was really dark and foreboding. Bloodborne's got its own vibe, right? I mean, it's another fantastic FromSoftware game but a different beast altogether. Right, entirely different doesn't even start to cover it. The Yharnam feels so different to the Lordran or Drangleic. True. And let's not forget about Elden Ring, right? That's all I've been hearing. Elden Ring is the talk of the town. I mean, who can resist George R.R. Martin and Hidetaka Miyazaki teaming up? It's sure to be epic. From everything I've read, it sounds like a more open world take but still retaining the complex lore of the Souls series. I'm just hoping it doesn't overwhelm players like some of the later Dark Souls areas did. Agreed. Hopefully they balance it well. Speaking of which, anyone care for a snack or something? We've been gaming for hours. A sandwich would hit the spot. Maybe some leftovers? I've got those cheese and pickle wraps if that works. Sounds perfect... I can heat up the leftovers if anyone's up for it. Yeah, please do.

Ah, I'm so glad we could all meet up today. It's been ages. How have you all been? You too, Sarah. Oh, we've been doing alright. Just really busy with work and other commitments, but it’s great to finally have a bit of a breather. How about you? Well, my hair has decided to abandon all structural integrity and right now, I'm just trying to stay on top of that. Seriously though, even with keeps changing backwards and forwards, nothing beats having my loved ones around. True that. I've just had a bit of a crazy week. But then I saw that new film and it completely shifted my perspective. Which one? I've been meaning to catch up on some new releases. Anything worth watching? It was “The Social Dilemma”. It’s a documentary but it’s quite impactful. Makes you think about how these social media platforms are actually manipulating us. That does sound interesting. I’m really trying to cut down my screen time, to be honest. I know what you mean. Sometimes I feel like I’m trapped in a bubble of notifications and endless scrolling. I used to think it was technology improving our lives, but now I’m not so sure. I’m trying to balance things out too. Well, we should definitely discuss all this over some tea and biscuits. How about we plan a movie night soon? But this time, maybe we can watch something less thought-provoking and more enjoyable, like “The Italian Job” or something? I'd love that. I just tried to explain “The Italian Job” to a colleague and failed. Oh, really? How hard could it be to explain a great Michael Caine classic? Well, I was trying to explain the premise and somewhere along the line, it turned into “a multi-ethnic heist involving a lot of driving and a red bus.” Typical South London storytelling! I think we just need to watch it again. We could all do with a good dose of Michael Caine and The Beatles. Well, I can't think of a better plan. So, movie night it is then. You two can book a slot, and I’ll bring the snacks. I'll get that done today. What day works for you? How about next Saturday? None of us are too busy then, right? Next Saturday is perfect.

Hey, I'm so glad we could catch up without any distractions. I brought today's newspaper and we could try that quiz together at some point. It's been ages since we last did something bookish together. Hi! I had almost the same thought, but I saw a really compelling article in the questions section this morning. It had this piece about language evolution and how people's speech changes over time, especially across different regions. I thought of you immediately, of course, as our language research coordinator! Oh wow, that does sound really interesting! I wish I could share it with my team. It's fascinating seeing how certain terms or pronunciations become more widespread or die out over generations. Do you think I could have a look at it later? Definitely, I can save it for you. But can I ask something? Did you hear about the invitation to this new writer’s anthology? It’s a collection of short stories from emerging writers and I thought it might be appealing to us creative types. No, I hadn’t come across that. What makes this one different or notable? From what I’ve read, it has a very diverse range of themes, including unusual viewpoints on some well-known literary tropes. Plus, it's edited by a woman who has a great reputation for spotting new talent. That does sound exciting. I also really enjoy bringing attention to different voices. Do you think they accept submissions from outside the UK or would I need to be more established in the literary scene here? From what I read, they accept submissions from anywhere, but I'm not sure if there’s a language barrier. I don’t think they’ve mentioned anything explicit, but you never know with the literary world. Maybe we could look it up together to make sure. Good idea. Also, have you seen Season 3 of “The Undateables”? I recently started it and it’s funnier than I expected. Different from what we normally watch, but still engaging. Not yet, but I should! We could make a night of it next week. You know how much I enjoy a good laugh. Or better, we could try for that board game night we’ve been putting off. Either works! I’d prefer the board game for now. Maybe we could do that before getting overwhelmed by too much TV and still be able to talk.

Hey, I'm going to unload the washing machine, would you like to help? It'd be quicker if we do it together and then we can grab a brew afterwards? Of course, I need a break from thesis work anyway. A bit of manual labour will do me some good – and who knows, it might just give me some new ideas! Ah, that's the spirit! I'm glad you can actually find some benefit in doing chores. Right behind you. You know, this reminds me of when we first moved in together. I remember we had to scramble to adjust to having to clean our socks from then on. Yeah, that was quite the transition. But we've adapted pretty well, haven't we? I suppose it's all part of living together – learning to enjoy the little tasks too. True. It also helps that we both work in higher professional occupations. Gives us a bit of flexibility and we can afford to make sure our living conditions are comfortable, which I’m very grateful for. Absolutely. And maybe it's our north-east and Midlands heritage that makes us appreciate the little things. You know, growing up, I never took for granted having access to decent facilities like this washing machine. My nan used to do all the washing by hand at home. She'd spend hours scrubbing away at the kitchen sink for the whole family. Wow, that sounds really tough! My grandma was similar. She never complained, of course, but it must have taken a toll. Exactly. Today, it's all so easy with just the press of a button. Sometimes I wonder what our lives would be like if all these time-saving technologies weren't around. It’d be interesting to see, but I’m glad they are. Speaking of which, have you checked out that new film we were planning to watch? “Last Night in Soho”? It’s supposed to be brilliant. Yes, and we also mentioned trying a new recipe from that cookbook I borrowed from the library. Lamb in a red wine sauce, if I recall correctly. We should do something tonight, maybe make lunch or dinner together if we're both free? That sounds perfect. Plus, could use a break from this thesis once in a while. It’s going well but I’m sure you can relate. I started my PhD not too long ago and things can get overwhelming.

Ah, I'm losing my patience with this VW scandal. It's hard to believe that a major company would try to cheat and lie to its customers like that. Yes, but I suppose that's the way of big business isn't it? You think? That questions the status of all corporations don’t you? It’s a scandal and an embarrassment for the industry at large. I think this VW scandal just goes to show that greed and cut corners can lead to massive consequences. But even worse is how they deceived us. It's like they have no respect for their customers, ethical responsibilities. It's a clear case of corporate greed, that's true. But I also think that we, as consumers, have to be more vigilant too. We can't just blindly trust big companies. Hence the importance of independent reviews and third party testing. It’s a shocker but it’s not the first time, and likely won’t be the last, that big corporate entities have been found wanting on ethical grounds. I heard that many EU countries are taking legal action against VW. I hope it leads to changes in consumer protection laws. I think most of us have learned that we can't just rely on the label 'German engineering,' 'American innovation,' and so forth to mean quality or morality. It’s a bit of sobriety check for all of us, isn’t it? Speaking of German engineering, I wonder how in hindsight they missed the emissions tests? For a company that prides itself on quality, it's a bit of a fall from grace doesn’t it? Indeed. I think that’s kind of the issue—it's like they thought they could get away with it because people have the habit of trusting big brands. More reason for us to question everything and conduct our own research. Speaking of research, I once worked with a couple who were environmentally friendly but were very interested in electric or hybrid vehicles. From what I know, they're changing the car market in a good way. It might be a good time to consider such a move more seriously. Yes, I've been considering it. The environmental benefits and the potential cost savings in the long run are quite attractive. However, have you considered the resale value aspect of buying an electric or hybrid car at this point in the market?

Ah, I'm losing patience. I don't understand why's it taking so long. These pensions are meant to be simple, but clearly they're not. Cheer up lad. You're right though, it is odd. Specially after all these years of honest, hard work. We do deserve questions answered easily. It's the bureaucracy, and the internet. I've spent days trying to sort our papers out, and I'm right at the end still. I had to call the local advice center for help. But even they keeps changing requirements due to new regulations. That's right! And those new 'secure' online systems – they seem to have a mind of their own. I’m sure they're designed to prevent fraud, but I just want to know if I’ll have enough money to buy some nice little retirement trip. [chuckles] Well, you always said you wanted to take that canal boat tour. Perhaps we can plan a surprise for your birthday? Just to take our minds off the pensions. [smiling] That'd be lovely, but between us, I've been thinking more about finding a decent bed and breakfast so we can have a short break somewhere local. Just to get out of the house for a bit. Staying at home all day is getting rather tiresome. [nodding] Speaking of which, I saw there's a new development at Thorpe Market. Maybe they’ll have some decent rooms? Aye, that's a good point. New developments can sometimes exceed expectations, but I remember they were considering housing for the elderly too. We should look into it. How about we check that out tomorrow? It’s only the train ride away. We could have a day out, look at the rooms, and make plans in case things improve in the near future? Sounds like a plan. And maybe we'll hear back from the pension people tomorrow too. [sighs] I just wish there was more clarity. From generation to generation, it feels changing rules complicates everything more. I do think it's upsetting – all these rules for people like us who just want to know what's coming in, when. Us, stuck at home, it's not easy trying to navigate all these changes. [chuckles] It’s the digital age. We’re almost as confused as youngsters with all their fancy gadgets. Clearly, they need to make it simpler for us old folks.

Hey guys, did you hear about that math question that's been making the rounds online? It's like, “The clock struck thirteen and it was late for two hours”, so what time was it really? Yeah, I saw that. It's kind of weird, but also kind of fun. I think the answer is like five? Actually, it's more about understanding idioms and not just doing the math literally. I'm pretty sure the answer is two. The word “struck” is for “o'clock”, so it means it was two, but it was late. You get it? Hahaha, nice one. But seriously, speaking of stuff online, I saw this really cool science video about how ants use antennas like tiny computers to communicate. Have any of you read anything about that? Yeah, we covered similar stuff in biology. It’s amazing how simple creatures can be so advanced in certain ways. It also shows how we humans often underestimate the intelligence of other species. And it’s another proof that evolution works in incredible ways. Right, and it's also a great example of how gender isn't about biology as much as culture sometimes makes it out to be. What do you mean? Well, the way we interpret masculine and feminine traits, right? Like ants apparently do whatever job is needed, without this idea of “strong, aggressive male jobs” and “gentle, caring female jobs”. Evolution hasn’t made them gender-biased, so why should we? And that’s why feminism is important – equality isn’t about us being the same, it’s about recognizing and respecting that differences are okay, but we’re all equal in rights and opportunities. Exactly. And it’s also about realizing that “feminism” isn’t a dirty word. It doesn’t mean you hate men or anything. It means you believe in equality. I've had friends who don't get it, they think changing the world means having to fight all the time. Change does sometimes involve fighting for what’s right. But most of the time it's just about being aware, being kind, and trying to make small changes in your own life first. Like, I realized how some of the language used in our school sometimes is quite sexist. Not intentionally, I’m sure, but we need to actively choose words that don’t make assumptions about genders or races.

Oh, did I ever tell you about my passport situation last year? It nearly delayed my whole holiday. No, you never did! What happened? Well, I had just renewed it but, as luck would have it, I left it at home and had to rush and get it back. Oh, dear! That's a right pain, isn't it? Yeah, keeps you right on your toes. Something like that! Even with my job, you'd think I’d stay on top of such things. Well, sometimes we all need a reminder. Was it for your trip to Switzerland or Austria? Exactly. I was going skiing with some friends from work. Luckily, I decided to check one last time before we left. You're lucky it was just a major inconvenience and not something more serious like an operation or something. Very true! Though, I’ve got an appointment coming up to check on this cold I’ve had for weeks. Suppose I need to start taking those tablets the doctor gave me more regularly. Indeed, keep them up, woman! They're not just for decoration. Yeah, as I've learned through experience. What do you do for that cold? I've had it for ages myself. I've tried everything from honey and lemon to steam inhalation, but I think I might give acupuncture a try next. A friend of mine who's had it for his back problems vouched for it. Acupuncture? Now, that's something new. Do you think it's just for back problems though? Apparently not. It can help with all sorts of things, including colds and flu, though I haven't tried it for that yet. Well, if it's good enough for the wife, it might be worth a shot. Just you let my Tom try it and see how he likes needles. I can imagine. Still, thinking about trying new things isn’t a bad idea. Maybe there's something out there that could help me with this arthritis that's been acting up lately. Definitely, there are many alternative therapies worth exploring. You know what I really wish I could hear about more often? The rugby team news. How's that coming along? Ah, what we get up to living out here in Peterborough! I still keep up with it, you know I do. Yes! I had plans to go to one of the home games but everything got cancelled because of this virus and all.

You both know that our country has had a very complex history. Today we talk about some of the toughest aspects of it, slavery and war. Slavery? Wasn't that just in the old, old days? Yeah and it was something America and other places had, not England, right? Well, it's true that England wasn't a major slave-trading nation like America or certain other European countries. However, many British merchants and industries were complicit, investing in the slave trade or benefiting directly from it. But that just sounds like a bit of history, not something we did. Exactly that. It's easy to see it as history, not something that affects us. But during the 18th and early 19th centuries, the enslavement and transportation of millions of people from Africa to the Americas wasn't just far away - English businesses and people profited from it. So we didn't have slaves here, but we helped the people who did. That doesn't sound right. It definitely doesn't feel right. It also means we can't just look at history as something 'they did over there.' It's also about what we as a people did, how we benefited or were complicit. So, all white people in England were bad then? Oh no, not "all" and certainly not "were bad." People then, like people now, had different views and levels of understanding about what was happening. But the point is, those views and actions did real, harmful damage to a lot of people. Why didn't they just stop it if they knew it was wrong? Many people did try to stop it, they were part of the Abolition movement that campaigned against slavery for years. But these efforts faced significant resistance and took a long time to succeed. It must have been a really hard time for the people being enslaved. It was. And the harder truth is that even after we outlawed slavery here and came to see it as morally wrong, we didn't just suddenly become a society that didn't oppress or harm others. There were and are still many problems related to discrimination, inequality, and unfair treatment... Like racism today? Yes, very much like racism today. And it's still an issue we need to face and work on. That's really sad. It is sad, but it's also part of our history, and talking about it honestly, as hard as it is, is the only way we can learn from our past mistakes and make a better future.

Everybody, I'm so glad we could all make it. We don't get to catch up nearly enough these days, do we?      Agreed. It's always good to see everyone together. Especially here at the house–there are so many good memories here.      Absolutely! I've had the best time researching for my last few copywriting projects about historical Kent. You'll not believe the bits of history I uncovered right here in Kemsing.      Really? That's interesting! You know, growing up here, I never thought much about it.      It shows – always good to have a fresh perspective. What's been going on with the project? Is it any good?      It was really rewarding. And the places I wandered into while doing the research... Just amazing! Plus, gave me some stellar ideas for our next talk on local history, if anyone's interested.      That does sound quite interesting. Though, I admit, history doesn't grab me like carpentry does. I've been meaning to fix up the old shed in the garden. Now that I'm self-employed, I have the time for it!      You’re always tinkering with something, aren't you? Makes me think of the time when I was head chef at the local pub. They had the wackiest contraptions in the kitchen – worse than the shed for upkeep! A bit like trying to manage all of us here isn't it?      That's certainly true! You always had quite the crew to look after…      Speaking of that, how about the royals? There's been some news lately. We should catch up on things.      More like try to make sense of! Between the various divorces and marital dramas it's hard to keep track.      It's more entertaining than the parliamentary debates sometimes, but we should probably keep up for the sake of having some idea on current affairs.      I was just listening to a radio discussion about the economy after Brexit. It's a bit concerning.      Oh, indeed! Though, honestly, some of that's over my head already. I just wish they could fix the roads more than anything else.      You're right–I mean, I work part time and stuff, but the joys of the economy don’t affect us as much as the current state of the A20.      That’s a given. And it’s strange but true – the older I get, the more I find myself discussing things like road repairs, rather than the latest novel or TV series.

Who knew I'd spend Sunday unloading the dishwasher? At least it gives us some time to talk about George Stephenson. Oh, yes! I've just read about George Stephenson in one of our family history books. Did you know he was a kind of a famous steam engine inventor? Wow, I knew he made the Rocket but I didn't know he was from our area. Is that right, Mummy? He lived in Norwich? Pretty much, kiddo. Well, not exactly Norwich but in those eastern regions of England. He was born in Wylam, Northumberland but I believe he spent some time in London too. And just like you, he started learning about steam engines from a young age. Oh, that’s so cool! He was like a kid playing with steam engines? I love that. Well, maybe not exactly like that… but you know, his interest in steam engines did begin when he was quite young. And you know what he said? He said, “Safety is a cheap and honorable insurance.” Isn’t that something? Where did he get that from? Was it because of his work in the mines? Absolutely. He worked in coal mines as a young lad, just like a lot of us from Dartford used to do. His experience there made him realize the importance of safety, as it often got neglected back then. So that's where he got the idea for the safety valve in steam engines! I remember seeing that in one of my books. You're picking up all these historical facts like a sponge! That's right. And did you know, his invention of the locomotive made the Industrial Revolution faster and changed the world as we know it? No way! So without Mr. Stephenson, trains might not have been invented so quickly? Exactly! You see how one person's curiosity and drive can change so many things? Plus, he was known for saying, “There is a world beyond Wylam,” which was quite forward-thinking back then for a village kid. That's almost as inspiring as Harry Potter being from the real England. Indeed. Speaking of inspirations, I think George Stephenson and Harry Potter have something in common. They both bring to life what many might think is impossible. I guess that’s true. Both took something ordinary and made it extraordinary with a bit of magic... or innovation. That's a great way to look at it, kiddo.

Right, so did you guys see that message from Alex about coordinating online games for tonight? He said he's been super addicted to Words With Friends lately. Oh yeah, I saw that. Are we still on for the usual trivia night or are we switching to this game now? I've kind of been missing our trivia nights, but playing a digital game might be a fun change of pace. Have you all played Words With Friends before? Yeah, I've played it a few times during breaks at work. It's pretty addictive when you start getting competitive with friends! Exactly. I've been playing with some old uni mates, and we've been going back and forth for weeks. Might just sneak in a bit before dinner. You can probably do that. We can have the game going on in the background while we eat and chit chat. That sounds doable. So, are we on for a bit of supper club tonight then? I brought over some good food choices. You're in charge of the drinks, right, Speak 4? Left, actually? I’m more of a coffee and pastry person, but sure, I can grab a few good wines. Or we could even do a bit of the 'supper club' thing in the way of a potluck, if everyone is into it. That could be fun. We've been talking about maybe doing some more 'real' supper clubs, you know, the old fashioned in-person ones, but for now this is a good compromise. I'm all for a compromise. Plus, doesn’t cooking instructions seem like it's the last thing we need now? We're all foodies here, but following recipes on the fly can be stressful. Hehe, true enough, but together, we could just wing it. Cooking should be a casual, fun thing with friends, right? For sure. It's about making good food and having good company, isn’t it? Yes, and we might just learn a thing or two from each other’s cooking styles. I’ve been trying these new recipes from Jamie Oliver, but I’m sure what you've all brought will be better. Speaking of food, did you hear about that new bakery opening up near my place? The display almost makes you wish you could just walk into the shop and cull all those pastries. Yeah, I saw that!

Ah, I'm so glad we could take a break from coordinating covers. I'm starving; these GCSE exam times are always tough. Have you had a chance to eat yet? I had a quick breakfast at home before coming in but now I’m considering grabbing a sandwich from the canteen. Those chicken wraps sound good today isn’t it? What about you, you prefer the canteen? I do love a proper canteen lunch, especially when we’re busy. But today, I think I might just stick with leftovers from last night's dinner. My kid was being picky and it was a bit of a culinary exercise. [laughs] I’m sure you've had your share of that with a teenager at home, right? Mine’s 16 and sometimes it feels like a constant battle to get him to try new things. He won’t even touch a salad unless you throw grilled chicken into it. Exactly! I’m constantly playing the game of "what shall we have for dinner?" and it often feels like a major negotiation between what they want and what I’m willing to make. But that’s just part of being a working parent, right? Totally. I often feel like a short-order cook, but the kids eventually grow out of it. Mine’s gotten a bit better at eating things I make over the years. Though now it’s more about negotiating technology time over dinner table time, which is a new battle altogether. [chuckles] I know exactly what you mean. My 13-year-old is always on her phone, and getting her to put it down is like leading a horse to water. But it’s good to hear the progress with your son. What about finding some common ground? I’ve started allowing them one screen time during meals, but only if we’re all together, no phones during dinner. Smart move. I might give that a try. Seems like a couple of small concessions can go a long way. Indeed! Speaking of dinner, last week I made a vegetable pie and we had a little family party. It was a bit more effort but it was nice to see everyone sit together and talk about their day. Oh, that’s lovely! I’ve actually taken to baking a lot more since the lockdowns. It’s good for the kids and stress relief for me.

Right, so Mum, what did we need to get from Mother Care? I know today's task was quite a few things. Hi, I talked to her before the trip and we need to pick up some nappies and baby blankets. Plus, now that the new room is ready, we might need some cot sheets too. Oh, isn't it lovely how everything is coming together? Yeah, and I'm right there with you, moving out of the old house and into the new one. But even with all that, I still get a bit nervous about leaving the old place. It feels like saying goodbye to a part of my childhood. It's only natural. I remember when your Grandma and I moved to this house, I was feeling the same way. But change can be good, especially when we're planning all these improvements to the new place. That's true, but it's also strange thinking about the room we grew up in, the attic where we'd play, now being somewhere entirely new. It's like, for the next few months, I'll still go back to the old house and think of this new one as maybe somewhere to visit, not fully home. I think most of us feel that way, but the 'new' soon becomes 'home'. You'll make memories there too, and before you know it, you'll look back on the old days and think about how far you've come. Like, remember that blanket we used to all snuggle under when we were watching films as a family? One of those is still here, and it might be nice to pass that down through families now. True that. I haven't seen that blanket in years! It'd be nice to have one in the new house as a keepsake. You know, speaking of moving, any preferences on where to place the couch or the bed? Yeah, we’ve had a few ideas. We want to make sure everything is safe for baby, so a cozy corner for the crib and then perhaps we can use part of the room for a reading area, somewhere comfortable for story time. That sounds wonderful. Story time is something so special. Reminds me of when we'd read to you and your sister. Speaking of which, how’s the college going for you? Anything exciting planned?

Hey everyone, did you hear about that new internet game that's making waves these days? It’s called "Virtual Earth" and it’s causing quite a buzz among my friends. It’s very immersive and you can create your own world within the game. Oh, I’ve heard of it! My grandkids love gaming so I’ve had a little glance into what it offers. Isn’t it amazing how much technology has evolved? I remember when I was a kid, the most impressive games were on the Commodore 64. Yeah, it’s impressive. It seems like games have become so advanced, they’re almost reality. But at the same time, they can have such a huge impact on our mood. Have you noticed how your mood can drastically change based on how your game is progressing? Totally, I feel like that’s a major theme in many of these games. If you’re doing well, you’re happy, but if you’re losing or stuck, you can get really frustrated. And these things can seep into real life too. It’s like it’s all mixed up - playing a game or even just scrolling on your phone, it can affect how you feel about the day. Exactly, I think most of us kind of assumed that while gaming may boost mood in some situations, if you’re not careful it can become an escape, right? Like a way to leave all your stressors behind, but then you might forget to deal with them in reality. Also, it seems like a waste of time sometimes because if you’re not careful, you end up spending hours and hours in there and you feel like you haven’t achieved anything in real life. That is the risk. I kind of see it as entertainment, like watching movies. If you can control it, it’s fine, but if it starts to take over your life, that’s where the problems start. Exactly. It’s another argument for maintaining balance. But personally, I find it interesting from a psychological and scientific perspective too. While some see it as a distraction, others are using games to improve cognitive skills or even for therapy. Really? I hadn’t heard that. Therapy through games? That’s quite something. How do they manage that? Oh, it’s not as wild as it sounds. There’s this field called 'Gamification', which applies game design elements to real-world problems.

Hey everyone, did you know that many of the first metals that humans have worked with today still play a major role in our lives? You mean like iron and copper? My Minecraft house is all made out of iron and copper. It’s just so useful! Yeah, and they're so strong! We could build pretty much anything with them. But do you know why they're so strong and useful? It's because of their chemical properties, and I bet we can find similar properties in materials we use every day too, even if they're not metals. That's right! And, actually, you can find similar properties in many different types of materials, like various types of fabrics. For instance, materials like cotton, wool, or silk have properties like warmth, stretch, or elegance that make them useful in different ways - just like metals do, but in a different context. Hmm, I didn’t think of fabrics like that. It’s creative how we can use the properties of things around us to make our lives easier or cooler in general. I love making stuff or even inventing things in my Minecraft games. Like, we found this really rare block that made all our tools super powerful. It’s like discovering a new kind of iron, but for gaming tools. It’s interesting how we use these ideas in our lives and in games, isn’t it? It’s similar to how people used to invent new materials or tools to solve problems, like using bronze instead of stone for tools thousands of years ago. Yeah, and sometimes they even made up "legends" about how those materials were special or connected to gods or magical powers just to make them seem more valuable or important. That’s so cool! Maybe we could make up some legends about Minecraft materials, like "The Legend of the Sparkling Silver Block: The only block that can shatter the Great Minecraft Curse." That's a great idea! It's like how in history people used stories to remember where certain things came from or why they were important. Plus, thinking creatively like that helps us appreciate and look at things differently. Even take something so simple like vitamins. We all take vitamins because we know they're good for us, but have we ever imagined a legend about vitamins? Like, "The Vitamins of the Wandering Wizard: Those who take these daily are granted 20% more strength and wisdom!"

Alright, so I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen Grace's new YouTube video? She's really nailing it with the guitar lessons. Yeah, I've seen it. I love how she explains chord progressions. Still, though, the fingerpicking is kind of tricky for me. You need to practice more then, and maybe try those exercises she suggested. You'll get there. True. I was thinking of joining a local guitar group too. They meet at this old pub near my place. It's a bit medieval inside but they have a great atmosphere. That sounds like fun! I'm sure it'll be great to learn from others. Have you connected with anyone on that platform we use? Not really. It's mostly pros but from what I've seen, they're all pretty supportive. And funnily enough, I saw a talk about paedophiles infiltrating music forums a while back. It’s crazy how they try to get near young people. That's just wrong. It's so important for us to be aware and keep each other safe. But yeah, that aside, the group is a perfect opportunity to network. Exactly. I just hope we’re all genuinely there for the music. Absolutely. Speaking of music, I found an old band you used to like. I think you'd still enjoy them. Should we catch a gig sometime? That would be great! There's one coming up in Sheffield next month. They're playing at The Leadmill. It’s a pretty iconic venue. I saw that. How about we check it out together? It’s been ages since we’ve done anything like that. I'd love to. It’d be a blast catching up and enjoying the music together. Plus, I've always wanted to get a better understanding of what you do at uni. You seem so into it all. Yeah, it's pretty intense but I'm loving it. I'll probably be applying for master’s eventually, maybe after a year or two of working. Good for you! It’s good to have such a clear plan. I’m still figuring mine out, to be honest. Everyone is at different stages. But it's definitely great to see you have interests outside of university too. Like that new indie band you showed me. You seem really into them. Yeah, they just got a new album out and it’s brilliant!

Hey guys, did you hear about that new art exhibition at Slough gallery? They're featuring some local artists and it's free admission this weekend. Thought it could be a nice little trip for us. Yeah, I saw that. Was thinking the same thing, but wasn’t sure if you guys would be interested. It kind of depends on what we’ve got planned for the break. Honestly, I wish I had more free time right now. My EPQ is getting really stressful. All this secondary research for a project that’s keeps changing requirements. You guys handling it OK? Oh, for sure. It’s not lazy, it’s just… overwhelming at times, right? I’ve been questioning if the amount of work we’re expected to do is even fair. I mean, we’re just in Sixthform, not universities yet. Agreed. And have you guys noticed the impact of schoolwork on the already strained socio-economic issues in our area? It’s crazy how uneven it feels. Some of us have the means to juggle private tutors and trips to montenegro, for example, while others are just trying to get by. We really don’t talk about it enough. It bothers me how unequal things can feel in school. And just because some of us can afford the 'luxuries', it doesn’t mean everyone’s at the same level to even think about university courses properly. It’s a bit of a blind spot in discussions about schoolwork and academic pressures. Speaking of, did either of you see that new study on the effects of poverty on education? It really opened my eyes to some harsh realities. Food for thought, you could say. Yeah, it’s tough to keep the bigger picture in mind when you're trying to complete your coursework on time. But it’s stuff like that which really makes you want to do something more significant in the future. Maybe we can even relate it to our EPQs if we were to choose a topic? That’s a great idea! We could maybe argue for some systematic changes or something in our projects. You know, add a bit of personal fulfillment to all this academic pressure? Exactly! I was thinking, for mine, I might look at how we can structure our society so that education isn’t so heavily impacted by personal income. And maybe, as a group project, we could even do something about it.

I swear I'm spending way too much money on these takeaways. It's like my bank account hates me. Don't worry about it, you've got uni to blame. Who needs cooking skills when you've got Deliveroo on your doorstep? Speaking of uni, have you all seen the new accommodation they've offered? It's like they're trying to fit two people in a space meant for one. Right?! I mean, it's fine once we've all figured out the best way to squeeze our stuff in, but initially... it was quite the challenge. I think my bed is officially my entire flat. It's the only place my clothes fit! Well, you could always sleep with the table if you run out of room. It's a very chic look, apparently. Chachi! You're so funny. You should do stand-up. Maybe someday. For now, this is my on-stage appearance! Speaking of appearances, has anyone noticed how often we talk about the 'uni life' but hardly discuss our families? It's like we're trying to forget them or something. Yeah, maybe because it's hard to relate to people here about family stuff. There's so much cultural and personal context... But it's nice sometimes to hear about everyone's family. Like, how many of us have a sibling back home and the rest are at different uni's or work? Except, I think I'm the only one who's got parents who still live in Falmouth. Really? I've got parents in Liverpool, but they've got another job now so they’ve had to move out of the city. It's nice though, they still support me a lot even though they're not close. No way, I've got siblings at uni too. Both of my sisters are at different uni's. But we always make sure to catch up, like over family WhatsApp groups or something. That's almost as bad as uni gossip being the unofficial class schedule. Oh definitely. Like that rumour about Dr. Smith and his “interesting” relationship with textbooks? And hasn't anyone heard any gossip about... well, not sure if you all want to hear it, but... the new student that looks like the lead actor from a Bollywood film? No kidding? That's hilarious. We should ask them if they know who they look like.

Ah, I'm so glad we could find a table here. It's been ages. How have you been, Ian? Oh, Helen, you know the usual. Busy working but I love every minute of it. Just, busy is kind of a theme for all of us this time of year, isn’t it? Absolutely. It feels like the pre-Christmas chaos has started even earlier this year. I had a laugh though; I set up my desk so that I could respond to emails alongside a puzzle. Felt like a game of Whac-a-Mole. I can imagine. I’m only just starting to get excited for the holiday season. Our nephew, Ollie, was asking for a weighted blanket but my mother in law is insisting on making him an arm knitted blanket. As much as the intentions are lovely, aren't they? But sometimes, creative grandparent thinking can get the better of practicality. Exactly. Anyway, between the lessons preparations and the general Christmas orgy, it's been hectic. We’re trying to stick to a budget this year too, so it’s different from when the kids were little. Less flashy, but hopefully more meaningful. I completely understand. I found myself at the local charity shop last week, trying to find some thoughtful yet cheap gifts. But it’s nice to see less focus on commercialism. Speaking of which, how is the new TEFL book coming along? It’s a work in progress. I’m over halfway through now but the publication doesn’t come out till next year. It’s great to be able to share my experiences and teaching methods, though. That sounds fantastic, really proud of you. The world needs more practical, accessible teaching resources. I've always been fascinated by how you can explain complex concepts in such a simplified way. Your students must really benefit from that. Thanks, Ian. I hope they do. You know, working with different cultural backgrounds really forces you to think about what English is – it’s not just grammar rules or vocabulary, it’s about communication and understanding. I can imagine. I've been doing a bit of freelancing for an international business project, and the cultural nuances of the language can be quite something. Really? Tell me about it. Well, it’s all about adapting your training to fit their environment, understanding their needs rather than assuming what they want.

Dad, I'm so glad we could finally meet up after all this time. It's been nearly two years, hasn't it? Yeah, it sure has! I'm really happy you could make it. There's been a lot to talk about since last we spoke. You've seen some real changes around here, haven't you? Absolutely, and I'm sure you've noticed them too, with that customer service job and all. But actually, I've been thinking a lot about moving to Brighton. Work-wise, it could be really beneficial for me, and I love the town. You ever think about it? Actually, I have. But to be honest, I've got kids to consider here. Plus, I've just gotten used to the area. Still, I can see why you'd be interested. It's a great spot for young professionals. What's been keeping you back from making the move? It's mostly just finding the right opportunity. But I also thought about how it might affect you since you're my dad and all. I know it's not the same without family around, even if you're capable of joining me on trips. Did you notice the speed cameras around here? It's been giving some folks a headache. Oh, yes. Where did you get stopped while driving? Was it near the town center? I swear, they're everywhere now. I also heard there are more license checks, especially with all the technology. It's like they're getting more efficient at catching people. Yeah, I got a notification suggesting I check my license details online, which is actually quite helpful. Shows there's some improvements in service over there. I've had my share of close calls with speed cameras too! On a more serious note, how have you been finding the work? Anything new on the horizon? The job's been okay, just okay, you know? More of the usual, nothing out of the ordinary. I did have to take time off for a cold or couple of months ago, but other than that, no major changes. But you know me, I'm always changing the channel to catch up on things. Speaking of which, did you catch any of that series on BBC? The one with the phantom people? Or was it Game of Thrones? I always manage to miss the latest episodes.

Hey, I had such a hectic day at work. We've got a big PR campaign for the new course coming up and I've been slumped over my laptop all morning. You poor thing. I've been dealing with a bunch of niggling queries from students, but other than that, mine was quite calm today. But then, as I was about to leave, my colleague just spilled coffee all over her notes and of course, I ended up helping her out. Sounds like a typical day in our line of work. By the way, did you manage to stop at Sainsbury’s for your shopping? No, not this time. I was just too knackered to even think about it. Do you fancy popping in there tomorrow when you're free? I could send you the list and you could pick up some of those fancy razors you want? That would be amazing, thanks! I’ll check the list tonight when I’m home and let you know if it seems okay. Perfect, I’ll send it over. Oh, on that note, did you happen to notice how many different podcasts the BBC Music has coming out this week? I saw the list and I need to catch up on Starling and its follow-up episode. Ah, no, I haven't yet. But I promise to check it out when I have some downtime. Speaking of downtime, have you got any plans for the weekend? I was thinking of attending this free music event that’s been advertised locally. Apparently, they’re showing films about 20th-century music and having live performances. What about you? I haven’t thought that far ahead yet, but it sounds marvellous. Shall I just see, maybe we could do it together? That sounds fun! It could be a lovely change of scenery for us after all these weeks in front of our screens. Yes, and we might even spot some interesting concepts to discuss over dinner on the way back. I can check the schedule of activities tonight and send you the details. That would be great, thanks. And have you had any time to listen to the new Sam Smith album? I just listened to it and thought it was really well done. Not yet, but I’ve heard good things. We should make some time for that. Agreed. Maybe over a glass of wine this evening?

Ah, I'm so glad we could finally sit down and have this chat. I've been thinking a lot about what we're going to do with this living room. It's just so dull, and we've had the same decor for years. Yeah, I agree. It's time for a change. Why don't we start with the cushion thing? It was something you mentioned last time we spoke, about knitting a bean bag. Oh, the bean bag. I'd almost forgotten about that. But it's a great idea! It could be really cozy. Do you remember those ones my aunt had? They were so plush and comfortable. Exactly! And I can imagine us just sitting in our new bean bag, cosy up with a cup of tea, and planning our next decorating project. [laughs] That’s actually perfect. Speaking of plans, have you thought about what we're going to cook for tonight? I thought we could try that new recipe for a Sunday roast. Ah, yes, that would be great. And maybe next week we could try something new. But while we're cooking this, it just struck me – we've been meaning to sort out the shower curtain for ages. I know! It's been years. It’s really nasty at the bottom and we keep hoping the mold won’t show. [laughs] But then again, it might be a nice little project for us to do together. Exactly, and as long as we're thinking about bathroom décor, maybe we could also look into getting a new shower curtain rod? I like the look of glass ones, they seem modern and sleek. Ah, and while we're in there, we might as well just re-do the tiles around the bath too. It’s dull and old, and a few nasty grout stains. [laughs] You know, we’ve had enough of just patching things up. If we're going to start with the shower curtain changing, why not just refresh the whole room? It’s a good opportunity to update our bathroom too. Yes! It’s actually about time we tackled it. We always manage to put it off because it seems overwhelming, but if we break it into small projects like the show curtain and the tiles, it could be manageable. And once the bathroom job is done, who knows, we might even feel inspired to update some of the other rooms too.

Ah, I'm losing my train of thought again, Alan's passport. I know today's the 23rd. It's not until the 27th, so we've got plenty of time. You're right though, Alison, we should get all the other forms ready as well, just in case. We don't want any complications just because of bad planning. Don't worry, Tom. We'll get it all sorted. I'm right behind you with the organisation. Just trying to think of anything else we might need. Maybe some keepsakes for Alan's trip. You know how he loves collecting memorabilia. Actually, I have an idea. What if we make a little album with photos and some notes about each place he visits? I think he'll treasure something like that when he's back in retirement. That's a brilliant idea, Paul! He'll love it. Alison, can you see about setting that up? We've got photos and maps, and we can print out a few facts about each place. I'd be happy to help with that. I've got a good scanner at home. But while we're on this, it might be a good idea to check if all his travel insurance is in order. We don’t want any last-minute surprises. Alan, are you sure you’re all squared up with travel insurance? We don’t want any hiccups. He's got the policy, but I'd love to take a quick glance at it. Alison, could you help me dig that out? I should be able to find that no problem. I know exactly where it is in that drawer of Alan's. Just while we’re on the subject of travel, what if one of us tagged along? Alan might enjoy some company and it's always nice to have a family member on hand. On one hand, it's a wonderful opportunity to spend time together and personally see the places he's going. On the other, it's a significant trip and changing plans now could prove complicated. What do you think, Alison? Well, I think it's a lovely thought, Paul. But I know Alan's always been quite independent when it comes to his travel. He might want to have this adventure to himself. Understood. No pressure. Alan, if you're feeling lonely or just in the mood for company, we're always here and happy to go.

Right, so who's seen any of the latest Christmas catalog's online? I discovered today that nearly every major retailer is discounting all their early Christmas stock. Oh, yes! I've been flicking through a few myself. Some of those offers are just ridiculous! The kids might need some convincing before we start putting together their lists, don’t you think? Honestly, I wish I could wrap myself up right now and be done with it. All this Christmas stuff coming in earlier every year! Makes you feel like backwards time travelers or something. Thanksgiving has barely passed and we're already talking Christmas lists! These catalogs are going to make this year feel like a never-ending holiday season, aren’t they? It's actually really nice for planning, though—if you start early, you can spread out the costs and avoid those last-minute panic buys. True! And for my department, it’s very timely. We’re already planning our big sales event, so having early options from all the suppliers is helpful for us. So, plans for the big event? I’m really hoping it’ll be quite the affair this year! Absolutely. We're thinking a weekend event this time, given everything else going on. If the weather plays nice at least... Yeah, fingers crossed for good weather. But really, have you thought about perhaps avoiding the big stores, especially if you’re looking for something unique? I found really good deals online for things we’re after, and they might not even sell it in physical stores. That’s a good point! I’ve been meaning to try that myself. The only issue is delivery times, but if you order early enough... I’ve been seeing some great handmade, locally sourced items online. For certain presents that way, it's almost better. It feels more personal and environmentally friendly too. Good call! And we should talk to Emily about the party. With her copywriting background, she’s got a knack for making things feel more unique and special for our event. Maybe she could help with flyers or something? Oh, definitely. I was thinking we should also include some of that local food she loves so much. It always goes down a treat. And maybe turn it into a bigger communal event? Get everyone involved in a little more than just attending. That sounds like a plan!

Ah, good morning! I hope you're enjoying your time in Northern Cyprus. I've heard so much about its rich history and stunning scenery. Have you had a chance to explore much of the area yet? Morning! Yes, it’s lovely here. I must say, it's a very different pace of life compared to the UK. I've been here for a few months and I'm still getting used to the local customs. Have you been here before? No, I'm actually on my first visit. I'm a bit of a history buff, so I’m really looking forward to exploring the archaeological sites here, especially the ones related to the Crusades. Oh, that sounds fascinating! There are many interesting sites around here, just like the castle in Kyrenia. I went there last weekend, but from what I've heard, Famagusta’s Venetian walls might be a highlight for you too. It's amazing how much history there is just lying around. Yes, I've heard a lot about Kyrenia and Famagusta. And it seems like the food here is amazing as well. I've been trying some local dishes like Kleftiko and Halloumi. I'm curious, what’s your favourite dish from here? Oh, difficult choice! But if I had to pick, I’d say it’s Turkish Cypriot kebabs. Perfect mixture of flavors, really hits the spot. And they have such fresh vegetables here. It’s like a different world for food compared to home. Yes, absolutely! And in terms of daily life, how have you found it? I imagine there might be some differences in services and shopping? Hmm, definitely some differences. It can be a bit inconsistent at times, but generally, the people here are very friendly and willing to help if you need it. Shopping for groceries is interesting because availability can vary widely depending on the location. But they have a lot of good markets. Ah, I see. I’ve had similar experiences in my own travels. It always takes a bit to adjust to the local rhythms. You know, one thing I’ve found is that because of the unique political situation here, sometimes things can be a bit… delayed. Either because of bureaucracy, or because so much of the infrastructure is still recovering from past conflicts. That’s understandable, I suppose. Did you have any issues with paperwork or registration when you moved here?

I keep reading about strict air pollution regulations in China. I never realized the extent of it when I first started teaching here. Yeah, it’s really affecting our quality of life now, even though it's supposed to have improved significantly over the years. It's insane when you think about it. I mean, Norwich, where I grew up, hardly has this kind of problem. Now, with two kids, I worry about their health. Absolutely. That’s something most people don’t consider when they think about living and working abroad. Even our colleagues have started using air purifiers in their homes and cars. I was talking to one of my students recently, and she said her parents barely take her out during the winter because the smog is so bad. It's not just about your lung health; it's also about going outside, playing, being able to breathe comfortably. True. It's also impacting the academic performance of our students. Off the record, some of them have major sinus and respiratory issues due to the pollution. For me, it's the impact on our lifestyle that’s the biggest adjustment. I miss being able to walk with the kids through a park without needing a mask. It’s a harsh reality. I also miss being able to jog outside, let alone take the kids to the park without worrying about their exposure. Honestly, it's been challenging to balance wanting to raise a healthy family here versus really doing so in terms of health risks. And yet, working here is a dream come true for our careers… it's just a hell of a trade-off in other respects. Have you found any local initiatives to combat this that give you hope? Some, but it's true that progress feels slow. There was a clean energy project that the local government backed a while back, but it ended up being more about appearances than actual impact. Well, at least it's a start. Even if it's more symbolic than effective, it’s a step in the right direction. I suppose. But what’s really needed is systematic change in policy. The structure of our economy, industry, all of it needs revision if we want to see lasting change. It’s good that you're involved with academic circles here; perhaps advocacy through our networks and collaborations could help put more pressure on local and national bodies to act.

Right, I think I've got all the vegetables chopped and ready. Now, do you think we should start with the sauces or the main course? You always manage to make everything sound so complicated, Emma. But honestly, it just comes down to, shall we say, "putting two and two together"— starting with the sauce and then marinating and cooking the meat while everything simmers nicely. I was just thinking I'd love to get some photos set up for dinner tonight. We keeps coming up with these great meals but never get to capture them properly before we dive in. That's a great idea, Sophie. I have this new camera in my phone that's just fantastic. While we're making the sauce, you can start setting up a little photo area by the window. And make sure to get some shots of the individual components too—our table will look so fancy tonight. I think that's a brilliant idea. And shall we actually take a photo of the finished dish before we eat it? Just for the next time we want to remember how to make this? Sure, that makes sense. But first, let’s get the sauce going. You’re on sauce today, while I handle the vegetables. I’ll set up the lights and the camera. Do you remember that one TV show we were watching where they always took a photo before eating? It was really inspiring in its own way. And that’s why we needed to plan our lunch today doesn’t it? Last week we were so busy we ended up eating sandwiches behind the desk again. Exactly. This week let’s commit to togetherness, a family dinner, and of course, fabulous photos. Oh, and before we dive in, should we plan what we're going to watch later? We could use a lazy evening after dinner. Well, that new drama series I started has got me hooked. I could watch just one more episode, but I don’t want to spoil anything for anyone else who might be watching. How about we pick something we can all enjoy? There’s the new series I’ve been meaning to catch. I heard it has a lot of mystery and suspense. Oh, that sounds perfect. Since we’ll have plenty of time after dinner and I'll have taken care of these photos, we can all settle down and see how any of the puzzles fall into place together.

Hey, I just heard that they're gonna reroute the busses stopping near our house. Did you hear about that too? Actually, yes. I think it’s because they’re trying to prioritize the new one–way system around the corner, near the university. Oh, I see. Do you think it’ll make a lot of difference? It could potentially reduce traffic congestion, right? Although I do hope there are enough service updates so people know about it. It could get messy otherwise. Definitely. You know how it is here, people don’t love change. I’ve been using that route for years, so it's a bit of an adjustment. Yeah, but change can be good. It just means getting used to a new routine. Plus, maybe the reroute will help to reduce your daily walk time slightly? That’s possible! But man, sometimes I just miss how easy it used to be. Like, you know, going to grab a book from the Cambridge University Press bookstore on that route. I love that shop, it's so quaint. We should go there sometime and grab some books for both our literary tastes. That sounds like a great idea! I’ve been meaning to check out the new architecture section at the university book store. I hear there are some interesting new releases by Cambridge University Press themselves. Oh, really? I'd love to hear more about that. Between the new bus route and the bookstore, you never know what we might stumble upon. True! Speaking of stumbling upon things, did you hear about the student protesters the other day? Yes! I saw some footage of it. What do you think of it all? Well, I understand the spirit of the protests. I studied at Cambridge myself, and there’s definitely some merit in students trying to have their voice heard about issues confronting us and the future generation. While I might not always agree with their methods, I think it’s important to at least hear them out. I totally agree. It’s good to see young people taking an interest in issues beyond just their own lives. Though, sometimes I do worry about the impact such actions have on the surrounding community, like disruption to the bus routes. Fair point. Maybe there are better ways to go about it. I believe in peaceful protest, dialogue. It seems Cambridge University itself is trying to encourage more open discussion and consultation now.

Ah, I'm so glad we could all meet up today. It's been ages. How have you all been since last we met at the Christmas dinner? Oh, it’s been quite busy but good. I've been really enjoying my job as a transcriber and editor, though the deadlines do get stressful at times. The same for me, and I'm looking forward to taking a break and just having some quality time with you all. And, of course, I'm really excited about your coming visit. Ah, yes, about that. We've been discussing it before we left, and I think we've made some good arrangements for your visit. You're staying with us, aren't you? Yes, definitely. I’ve brought my own car so we can easily visit places without relying on public transport or having to worry about parking charges. Good move! So, did you decide on anything specific yet? Any particular places or activities you want to do? Well, we've always thought it would be lovely to take you for a walk in the Lake District, or maybe visit some of the local castles. But, it would be great to hear what you prefer. That all sounds wonderful. I’d love to visit the Lake District. The landscape in the pictures is just breathtaking. Do we also have time for a bit of cultural stuff, like visiting an art gallery or something? Absolutely! We have quite a few good ones here in Cheshire and near the lake. But you should also try the local food and ale. What do you and your family like to eat? Food is a great topic! I’m the one that loves cooking for others, and our family has always enjoyed traditional Irish and British food. Maybe during your visit, we can have a true British picnic or do a cooking day where we make some of the local specialities together. Oh, I’d love that. My partner loves trying new recipes too. And what about kids? Do we know if they’ll be joining us at any point? From what you told me last time, I think there’s a good chance. But for sure, I know my niece will want to meet you. She’s such a bright kid, and I’m sure she’ll enjoy playing with whoever is here. That would be lovely.

Ah, I love this view. I don't think I've ever felt more relaxed. It's like we're walking through history, and yet it's completely silent. It's surreal. You're right. There's something really peaceful about walking by the river, isn't there? I miss this part of London when I'm working in the office all day. "Practically living in the office" as you once said. Oh, I've got that wrong coming backwards and forwards, don't I? Tell me about it. After our last holiday, I had to set up a timer to remind me to actually walk out of the office. You know, to get some air. Ah, yes - "Two hours of writing reports and then a five-minute walk around the building." We're rebels, aren't we? Definitely. But seriously, that holiday was good for us. We both felt so... free for the first few days, at least. For me, it was the not having to drive anywhere. I'm so glad we don't have to own a car. You know, I sometimes still marvel at the idea. Me too. I used to think, "This place is too big, you have to have a car." But no, the public transport is fantastic here. Though, I do admit to missing the silly things sometimes, like walking into a pub with a car key around my neck, feeling all 'British'. Yes, definitely a stereotype! Well, maybe we can plan that pub walk for this summer. Yes, or just planning another holiday. We've been talking about the US, right? But we keep bringing up the fact that the cup measurements are so different there. Yes, it's so frustrating! Why can't they just stick to metric and cup measurements at the same time? I know! It's like they're teasing us with all these weird sizes. A 'cup' in the US is like 240 ml, but here, it's so much less. It always throws off my baking. Baking is already hard enough without that. But almost makes you wish for the simplicity of going to a pub and ordering without looking at the menu, you know? Oh, definitely. But, food aside, have you ever thought about how different measurements change the way we perceive things? Like, time, distance... True. I was listening to a podcast the other day that mentioned how our brains work differently depending on the system of measurement we use.

Hey, I'm so over this rain! Can you believe we've had non-stop rain for nearly a week now? You would think we're living in a British soap opera. Right! And to top it all off now, the mobile signal is rubbish in this house because of the outside wall. You try and call for a taxi and you're lucky if you get a signal strong enough to get out of our street! But at least we've got each other, eh? True! Can't imagine what it must be like for people who live in really rainy places, like Scotland. I've been lazy with potty training too much, just had to set up a timer again. Seems like I've got a full-time job keeping up with this. Potty training is such a battle! I'm making my summer project to get through all the rain and master potty training with Grace. You mean, your very own little potty training summer? That's ambitious! Did I tell you about this new Build a Bear for the kids that I heard about though? For me or for this summer project? Both! But seriously, have you heard the one about the stuffed bear that becomes this huge deal for kids? They can design it online and pick the clothes and accessories and stuff. It's really cute, but apparently super popular. Ah, I saw that! Honestly though, I'm all for anything that makes the kids excited and occupied, especially if it's something they can actually use, like a cuddly toy for bedtime? Yeah, definitely something that's not just a toy but can be part of their routine or help them with transitions, like bedtime, which has been tough lately. But the rain isn't helping with the outdoor plans for sports day, I just hope the sun comes out for just one day. If it does, will you remember to take some decent photos for me? Last year's sports day was such a mudbath, not a single photo that didn't look like we were stuck in a swamp. Absolutely! Though in this weather, I'm more concerned about whether we're going to get soaking wet taking those photos! Can we not just light some sweet-smelling candles and show off the photos and pretend the kids looked like they were having fun in this indoor café we created?

Hey, I've been thinking. I believe we've reached a point in our lives where setting some solid personal goals and professional development plans would be beneficial. What are your thoughts? Absolutely. It's been quite a while since we've had these kind of talks, but I think they're essential given where we are now. Between our careers and house-sitting in Australia, it feels like a good time to reassess our priorities and where we want to go from here. Exactly. I set up my company about five years ago and while it's slowly growing, I feel like I need to re-evaluate the long-term strategy and potentially upskill myself to keep up with the industry advancements. I've been wanting to get into some mentorship or professional online courses to boost my digital marketing skills. That sounds like a great idea. As a teacher, I always emphasize the importance of continued learning and development. On my end, I've been thinking about going back into writing and publishing again. It's something I used to do when we first met and recently, I've been itching to get back into it. That's brilliant. A side project that could lead to more financial security on both ends might be a good idea. Now that we're in the right setting, how about reaching out to our friends for a bit of a social reunion in Australia? They often speak about wanting to catch up, and we can also use the opportunity to connect with them about our goals – perhaps they can offer some guidance or perhaps join forces in some projects. I love that idea. I've already messaged a few of them, and they seem excited. It’s always helpful having a support network that understands our unique circumstances and goals. Speaking of that, how about we also make some serious plans regarding family planning? We've been talking vaguely about it for years, but now that we're more stable in terms of our careers and living situation, it might be a good time to discuss our dreams and aspirations for having children, if we choose to. That's a sensitive topic but also very important. I think we're both ready to take on that responsibility if we decide to go ahead with it. However, let’s make sure we discuss all the implications.

Right, so did you hear about James getting into that fight at the pub last week? He nearly got arrested. Yeah, I've heard. It sounds like his 'fight or flight' response just kicked in immediately. He's lucky no-one else got involved. He's always had a bit of a temper. You remember that one time he got into an argument with the waiter at Costa about the wrong coffee order? I do! He was so defensive about it. And poor waiter just keeps coming backwards due to his whole 'I'm not getting my coffee'. Even lazy millennials like us have to learn manners sometimes. I swear, pubs are getting more and more like service stations - endless line ups and waiting for the wrong food. But at the same time, the service at Costa has definitely improved since they introduced those automated ordering machines. Still, nothing beats looking someone in the eye and ordering a nice cup of English tea, right? You two should try the new Costa next time we're in Warrington. Now that I think of it, it would be quite funny to see how they handle an accident involving a spilt cup of tea. Reminds me of that time I accidentally spilled my After-Eights in the pub’s garden. Ouch, that must have been a sticky situation. Actually, I love those After-Eights. They remind me of childhood summers at the campsite. One time, we even used them as a 'prize' in some silly game we made up. Your camping stories are always so different to mine. When I was younger, my family would always pitch up next to some football match grounds or near service stations just for the convenience. No games or adventure like yours. I used to complain whenever we ended up near football grounds because of all the smoke and crowds. My family's really into football but I always found it so overwhelming. Yeah, I'm not a fan of the chaos that comes with match days. But you know what I miss? The smell of smoke from the service stations. I mean, those were the days when you could light up a cigarette inside. Now it's all smoke-free. Speaking of which, I've just put off quitting again. I started using a Fitbit to track my activity but whenever I stress or feel down, I still reach for a cigarette.

Ah, I'm so glad we could all make it tonight. It's been ages. You know, I was thinking about when we used to watch the cricket together. It seems like a lifetime ago. Oh, isn't it just though, George? You were always quite the enthusiast, weren't you? I don’t remember a single England match you missed. Yes, I was a big fan of Geoffrey Boycott back in the day. He was a very set batsman, wasn't he? I'm more of a football fan, but I do love how sport can bring everyone together. What about you, dear? I heard you have been watching a lot of golf lately. Indeed, I have. The Masters was really good this year. It’s interesting how even though the game isn't as fast-paced as others, golf can be so compelling, can't it? Compelling, yes... but maybe not as thrilling as when we used to go carp fishing together. Though between us, that was more about drinking or catching something to eat. Oh, no kidding! Those were the days! We never expected to catch any carp, but we still had the best time. Good times, indeed. It really does show us how different people can connect over different things. It's like our love of food – nobody argues over a good roast dinner, does they? Oh, no. One thing we all agree on, and it’s fantastic. Speaking of food, did you two catch the Great British Bake Off last night? I missed it. Yes, we did. It’s such a lovely show. But the really impressive thing is how the contestants can try those elaborate recipes so consistently. I couldn’t even keep up a casual Sunday roast without losing track of time. Oh, I know what you mean! I remember when I tried changing the recipe for Yorkshire puddings on my own. Let’s just say I won’t be attempting that again anytime soon. It’s alright, George. Precision isn’t your strong suit, but who needs that when you’ve got such an impressive collection of anecdotes? True, he’s quite the storyteller. Whether reminiscing about cricket, fishing, or even cooking adventures gone wrong. Well, I think between us, we’ve covered food, sports, and company. Someone’s got to bring up politics though, right? How about those recent local council elections?

Hey, I'm losing my mojo to keep going with uni. To be honest, the thought of another two years feels too much at the moment. Do you remember back in sixth form when everyone was like "uni life will be amazing!"? Oh, yes, definitely! But real life is very different. I'd never encourage you to drop out if you truly want to be here, but at the same time, it's okay to admit when you're burnt out. I've had those feelings plenty too. It's weird how it goes from being this whole big deal in school to suddenly just another thing to try and cope with when you're there. Exactly, and I used to be so sure of what I wanted to do, but then ... you're among people who are genuinely passionate about their subjects, and it can make you feel a bit useless, or like you're just trying to survive. Plus, the tuition fees, I feel like I'm just looking for a job afterwards, not a career passion. And the pressure from home doesn't help. My parents keep saying "just carry on," but I feel like they don't fully understand what it's like. Whereas maybe they see it as just another stage. I know. It feels like everyone assumed we'd just 'figure it out' once we got here. It’s like, we were all the golden children in sixth form, and then we’re suddenly supposed to become adults overnight while balancing studies and jobs . It’s a lot to navigate. It's funny, I was reminiscing about childhood with you the other day. Remember when Mum used to yell at me for getting dirty shoes back from the park? [Laughs] Oh, all the time! I had muddy pants at least once a week from playing in our garden back in Liverpool! I used to think that whenever I ended up with dirty shoes, Mum would know I’d had fun. Now, I just feel guilty walking into our room here with muddy shoes because it's not even my room, it’s a shared space. [Chuckles] Our generation loves to multi-task and balance multiple worries. Fun, isn't it? [Laughs] Definitely a skill we've developed! Speaking of skills and interests, have you ever looked into the origin of your name? Like, the actual history behind 'Smith' or 'Jones' or whatever common name you have?

Ah, I'm so glad we could finally meet up! We've been meaning to catch up for ages. Me too! I've talked so much about the tea and food here that I'm actually a bit excited to see if it lives up to the hype, haha! Oh definitely. This place has been around for years and years, they do a mean English breakfast and their scones are to die for! But actually, before we get into that, how have you been? Work-wise and life-wise? Pretty well, actually. The marketing game is always changing, but it's keeping me on my toes – always something new to try out, new campaigns, you know. And life-wise, just your average grad trying to make a name for themselves. Yeah, same here – project coordination can be a handful but it's rewarding when you see a project through to the end. Definitely. It also keeps your admin skills in shape, right? Like, you can juggle a million things at once and never forget to send the reminder email at the last minute or whatever. Exactly! But it's funny, sometimes I find myself wishing for less admin and more actual creative work. I feel you. Sometimes I think they might be more fun at the end of the day to, you know, create something from scratch. Ah, but then you’d miss all the office politics right, all the little victories of making a dull process slightly more efficient? Haha, true. And we're definitely overcompensating for the lack of creativity in our day-to-day now with our Netflix obsessions. Oh, Netflix? I've been watching "The Crown". It's really making me want to move to the countryside and have tea parties just like the Queen. Haha, you and your royal fantasies. I've been binge-watching "Bridgerton". There's something about 19th century England that just calls to me. Right? I think because of our shared history, but also the nostalgic feeling of simplicity and elegance it represents. Anyway, speaking of old England, have you ever visited the North? Yeah, I have! Again and again with family. The Lake District is almost breathtaking, isn't it? Oh absolutely! And I've always found that there’s such a strong community spirit up there. It's something we don't get as much in London, I find. True, but I hear the city never sleeps.

Right, I'm going to unwind for a bit and have a browse online. Fancy joining me? Sure! What are you looking for? I don't really need anything immediately, but I occasionally find some great deals on eBay, especially with things for the house. You've been buying so many things on Amazon lately, haven't you? Yeah, and it's brilliant. I get free delivery right to my doorstep and I can return things if they don't fit. Exactly. But with eBay, you've got to be a bit more careful, don't you? Sellers can be a bit... unpredictable. True. But there's also so many second-hand and rare items. Like, I bought a really old science book from a university study group that was dirt cheap. That's true. I've bought some amazing items from there myself - vintage clothes, books, sometimes even toys. You just have to have a bit of patience and read the descriptions carefully. And it's often cheaper than Amazon, for sure. So, do you think eBay is just for this sort of stuff, or can I find new stuff there as well?
