Distributing the weight might help reduce strain on the string. I've seen them use small weights during racket restringing. Seems like the commerce is quite in the racket! Indeed. Speaking of commerce, did you know that historically, ‘fleet’ wasn't just about ships but also referred to a collection or group of something? It's interesting how our words change meanings over time. Indeed, that’s quite fascinating! Though in this case, I wasn’t using ‘fleet’ in its nautical sense, but rather thought of all these badminton rackets as a collective to fix. It’s the linguist in you coming out, isn’t it?

Ah, I'm so glad we could all come together like this. It feels like ages since we've done anything together. That's true. It's particularly nice with the art theme, I love that you've really set this place up. Yeah, I love the way everything kind of ties together isn't it? I mean, from the paintings on the walls, to the little sculptures that you’ve placed around the room, it all feels cohesive and I think really sets the mood. Absolutely keeps it very engaging and it actually affects how you engage with the space too. Tell me, you two with the academia background, what do you think about modern art? I've always been a bit of a traditionalist to be honest. I prefer the paintings that look like something but from your view, what are the attractions to the modern stuff? Well, modern art is fascinating because it challenges our traditional views of beauty, form and function. It often breaks free from the need for representation and instead explores concepts, emotions or experiences. That's right. Sometimes it's the process, the idea behind the work that's more important than the finished piece itself. It's a whole new way of seeing and experiencing art. I think I see what you mean. Like that painting over there with the random shapes and colours, it doesn't look like anything to me, but according to the little card, it's supposed to evoke feelings of chaos mixed with serenity. Chaos and serenity? To me, it just looks like someone spilled a few paints on the canvas and needed a name for it. Well, see, the beauty is in how it makes you feel or what you bring to it, not necessarily what’s depicted. Sometimes the lack of clear representation actually allows for more personal interpretation. I suppose so. I used to go to exhibitions at the Tate when I was younger. There was one time I saw a chair in a room with a light bulb hanging over it and people were taking photos like it was the most incredible thing. I must admit I walked out because I couldn't understand what I was supposed to see in it. Ah yes, that’s a classic example of conceptual art! It was a piece called “One and Three Chairs” by Joseph Kosuth.

Hey, I'm so over this week already. Another Friday's here. Oh, Jeez, tell me about it. I had a crazy day at the ward. Right? And to top it all off now, the kitchen’s a mess. We need to have a serious talk about who cleans this up every week. Oh absolutely. I'm pretty sure it’s the universe fracturing at the thought of me cleaning again. Right, let me guess, you're blaming some divine intervention. Pretty much. But seriously, have you been following that new health language initiative? They’re trying to use more "patient-friendly" language. Yeah, I saw that article. It's an interesting concept. Though sometimes I feel like we're losing the exact nuance we need with more simplistic terms. Totally. I mean, it’s like they’re trying to dumb it down. As if healthcare wasn’t already confusing enough for patients. For sure. We’re practically speaking two different languages as it is. Exactly! I often feel like I should prep my patients with a 'glossary' of medical terms before each appointment. That’s a good idea actually. Perhaps we should start a side hustle, 'Dictionary of Medical Terms, Explained Simply’? Oh, that’d be a hit. And we’d make a fortune. First lesson: what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger. True, but the paperwork that follows might. Too true. Speaking of paperwork, the project I’m managing is just piling up. Every day I just want to procrastinate and watch another episode of that new show. Procrastination is my next of kin. Last week I legit forgot to respond to a very important email because I was reading about the benefits of microdosing for mental health. I know, right? Imagine having to talk about that in family therapy. “Yes, so I procrastinated on an email because I was researching the benefits of microdosing for anxiety... Again.” Yeah, my supervisor would just nod and say, “valid concerns.” Do you ever feel like the language around mental health is turning into buzzwords? Everyone’s a ‘mental health advocate’ but when it comes to the real issues... Definitely. It’s like the true meaning is getting lost in the hashtags. Though, it does get people talking, I suppose. That’s true. At least it brings a little more awareness, but sometimes I fear it dilutes the importance and specificity of professional help.

You know, sometimes I wonder if educating people on common sense is more important than intelligence. I mean, isn't that what gets us through the day-to-day, much more than theoretical knowledge? I see your point, really. But don't you think intelligence is what empowers us to learn common sense questions? It kind of goes hand in hand, doesn't it? True, but sometimes I wish I could just give some of these common sense lessons to people. You know? Like when it's really obvious how things should be done, but still, people won't do them. Yeah, I've had instances like that too. Remember when we were at the supermarket and I saw this guy picking up a 10kg bag and trying to balance it on one hand? I mean, weighted down but balanced? [laughs] Oh God, that's exactly the kind of thing! It's not even complex thought, it's just not observing the physical world around you. But then again, these things can be culturally bound, couldn't they? Very true. Sometimes what we perceive as 'common sense' is just so steeped in our own cultural viewpoints. Take for example, how many different ways there are to greet people. Where I lived in Spain while studying, it's customary to kiss twice on the cheek. Here, if we were to try that, people might think we're odd. Exactly. And I wonder if that's why sometimes, especially in this day and age where we're all more aware of each other's cultures, we sometimes confuse genuine cultural differences with a lack of "common sense". Or vice versa! I mean, I've had instances where my own upbringing or socialization meant I made certain assumptions based on my cultural background, which really turned out to be just that, assumptions. No common sense to apply, blurred by my own biases. And yet, despite all this, feminism is still misunderstood in certain circles. Last week at work, someone said to me, "You'll never be able to manage on your own if you can't even do it all without a man." What’s the 'common sense' for that? [chuckles] Oh, that’s just absurd. It's not about being dependent on a man or not, it's about being given the right to have choices. And yet... it's just common sense to them, maybe?

Ah, I'm so glad we could take the kids on that farm trip today. I think it's really important for them to get out and experience different things, don't you? Hi Emma, isn't it great now? Yeah! I liked the sheep the most! Did you hear them say "baa"? I did! It's amazing how much the children can learn out in the open isn't it. Emma, did you have fun? Hey, while we're talking about fun things, I found these DVDs at the house, they're kids' films. Maybe we could watch one tonight? That's a great idea. The kids could really use some downtime after such an eventful day. What did you think of the farm today, sweetie? Did you like the animals? Uhm, yes! The cows were funny because they went "moo" and then they ate the hay! I'm glad you found it funny. These visits are not just fun but also educational for them, aren't they? They learn so much in a more interactive way than sitting in a classroom. Definitely. Like, perhaps Emmy could even show pictures from today's trip for a school project someday? Yeah, I can take photos and show 'em to my teacher! I think that's a brilliant plan. And speaking of school, how did today go? I know earlier we were discussing behavior in class. Well, there was an incident at lunchtime. The teachers mentioned that Emmy ended up chasing some other children around. But before we dive deep into that, let's finish dinner, shall we? Definitely. Let’s take a break. Now, about the school incident earlier today. I hope it's not something too worrying. I was just playing. I like running and I just wanted to play tag or something... I know you were just playing, sweetie. But at school, we need to remember to be gentle and not chase other children. It can make them feel scared. And also, we don't want to be disrupting the class or hurting others, even if it's by accident. Remember, like at the farm, everyone needs space. Maybe next time, how about playing a game where you don't have to run after someone, like "Stop, Go"? Okay, maybe I can try that next time. I'm glad we could talk about it. Oh, and about that DVD we mentioned, do you two have a favourite film at home?

I'm so excited about the upcoming Olympic games. Have you thought about who you'll be supporting this year? Ah, you know the Olympics are always exciting. I'm still deciding. I really enjoyed watching gymnastics last time, but this year might be different – I heard questions are being asked about some of the athletes and their eligibility. I've been working on this jumper for ages. I bought the yarn online; it says it's 100% wool, but it feels a bit synthetic to me... I need to check if that's okay. I used to try knitting in uni, but let’s just say my elephants looked more like hedgehogs. But actually, have you seen the new Anthony Joshua painting making the rounds? He's selling his paintings and it's all for charity. Yes, I've seen that. It’s creative and very appropriate for the cause. It speaks to his diverse talents, I suppose. And Easter next week, or whenever it is. Did you get time to buy any eggs for the kids this year? I assumed we’d buy some when we did the food shop this week, but I’ll check to make sure. Ah, we’ve got eggs for sure. A bit rushed this morning, but we’ll have a proper in-a-few-minutes-tea time session. Perfect. So, you saw that Justin Bieber doesn’t come from the UK, right? I keep saying how he’s from Birmingham, but it seems he’s Canadian. That's right. Seems like the North East and Birmingham are both a bit overshadowed by international popstars. But funnily enough, even Lady Gaga was born in New York, but she's got a great connection with our region, doesn't she? Definitely. We could sit here all day talking about knitting, celebrities, the Olympics, and art if we want. But for now, I think a cup of tea is in order. There you go. Black or green? Black, please. I’ll just finish up this jumper row and we can talk more. Take your time. So, have you ever thought of knitting for charity? You're often doing research projects; it might be... Ah, no, I think knitting for charity is a bit like guest blogging for a finance website – I'm just not sure it’s my thing. Though, come to think of it, there are definitely some creative ways to fundraise if you think about it.

Ah, I'm so excited for today! We've got tickets to that new museum exhibition. I've heard it's absolutely stunning. Ah, that's the natural history one isn't it? Yeah, I've really fancied going that now, the kids have been awfully keen on dinosaurs lately. Exactly! And what's more, they've got this incredible interactive section that makes you feel as though you're actually in those ancient forests. Oh, that sounds marvellous! I wish they'd had something like that when I was a lad, all those museums were just dusty old bones behind glass. Haha, true! But I think that's just part of why it's so appealing. Everyone gets to engage in their own way. What's the plan then? After we're done here? Are we going for the Imax afterwards or going back home for a nice afternoon tea? Well, we were thinking about doing both. There's a late afternoon showing of that new 3D film, and I think it would be a nice cap to the day. Sounds grand! But do you think we can manage with the public transport logistics? I assumed we'd take the tube, but don't they often get packed at this time of day? A bit of a worry, isn't it? But we can plan for it, perhaps look at the tube schedules online to time our journey right. Yeah, or we could even take a bus part-way. It’s always a bit more relaxed. Plus, doesn’t give you that tube rush. That's a good idea! Except, we've got all our bags with us. And you know how I am about not missing that last train home. Ah, come on, we'll make it. Anyway, another argument for taking the bus—more room for all your knick-knacks. True, true. It might just be a knick-knack extravaganza today. Well, I suppose it’s worth it for the day out. I mean, doesn't public transport give you a real feel of community? It does. Though, let’s hope it’s less crowded than usual. Oh, we'll manage, love. Can't wait. It's been too long since we've done something like this together. Me too! You know I love a good museum, but this one has particularly caught my eye with its modern approaches to teaching history.

Ah, I'm so glad we could all make it back home this year. It's always a bit of a challenge balancing the celebrations and work commitments, don't you think? You can say that again! I was just telling our mutual friend about how the semester was dragging a bit – couldn't have timed this break better. Absolutely, and now we have the perfect opportunity to catch up with everyone. I've heard there's a great new Christmas movie out I'd love to watch with everyone. Which one did you have in mind? That's exactly what I was just thinking about! I'm actually a bit of a film buff myself. I think Idris Elba's recent Christmas film – you know, the one where he plays a down-on-his-luck DJ - is fantastic. It really captures the spirit of the season - though maybe not the cold that usually comes with it while watching Christmas films! I didn't catch that yet, but sounds like it could be a nice film night. What about Sunday? We could have a Christmas dinner and watch it together. That's a great idea! Sunday works well for me. We could keep it low-key, just us and maybe a few friends who are around. Low-key is the way to go. Too much stress in the peak holiday period. Speaking of which, I saw there's a list of the must-watch Christmas movies according to some British magazines online. They always forget about 'Love Actually', of course, but 'The Nightmare Before Christmas' makes the cut for some bizarre reason. 'The Nightmare Before Christmas' is a classic, definitely a Christmas cult film. Though I do think 'Love Actually' is the quintessential British Christmas film. Haven't seen it since I was in Manchester though. It's strange how those films feel so quintessentially British. The sense of community it brings year after year. Exactly! And movies are one of the best ways to get into the holiday spirit when you're not at home. Speaking of which, my family always had a tradition of watching 'Home Alone' on Christmas Day before the festivities. Ah, 'Home Alone' - so much nostalgia! I always preferred 'The Muppet Christmas Carol,' but that's a show more for the family. Really? I've never seen it. Maybe we could include that in our film night.

Yo, anyone seen that stupid review on Twitter? Some bloke's annoyed because we're out of avocados. Like, what are we, the avocado police? Haha, yeah, but I love how you've got this new design on the menu, the old one was a bit boring. That’ll keep some folks interested. I saw that, yeah, the new design looks cool. Makes me wonder if I should modernize my café’s website as well. I’ve had some bad reviews and it’s all about how outdated it keeps coming across. Totally get it, some people just don’t understand how lazy millennials are about food menus. But, honestly, some of our customers are dead giveaways that they probably live in a cave. Like the other day, there was this dude who demanded free fries because we didn’t have ‘freshly squeezed’ orange juice. What? Does he think we're a juicer? That's wild! My customers are usually reasonable, except for that pair last night. Demanded gluten-free bread because apparently, they don’t understand their own diet. So, I explained that we’re a bakery, not a gluten-free factory, and they just got all defensive. You’re lucky you get customer interactions. My job's about hospitality so it’s more about smiling and nodding to people who, really, can't give two hoots about what you recommend. But, I did get a really nice review recently for my new sandwich, so it's not all bad. Yeah, it is tough sometimes, but all part of the job and working in the service industry. Plus, doesn’t your café do well in the local reviews? Margate’s quite good, to be honest. We attract visitors and locals alike. But the secret weapon is getting into the local food festivities. Gives us real exposure. That sounds fun! Speaking of getting exposure, I saw this hilarious tweet about some dive restaurant they went to in Margate. Apparently, it was so bad but so charming. Yeah, I saw that. It's like sometimes, the worst reviews are also the best anecdotes. Funny how a bad experience can actually increase interest because people want to see if it's that bad or not. Speaking of places in Margate, have you guys heard about this new coffee shop opening just near the sea? I might go check it out next weekend. Ooh, now that sounds amazing!

Everybody, I hope you're all enjoying the dinner! I've made a special theme today to see how we all like vegetables since Oisin is such a young one and still learning about his meals. We've got raspberries for dessert, but let's talk about healthy food now and how we can encourage Oisin to eat more of it. You know, I was surprised last week when my science exam included part about the digestive system and how important it is to eat right. It was interesting to learn that, and it made me think about my own eating habits too. Right, and Mommy said if I eat my veggies, I can have extra raspberries after dinner. But I just had a little bit of salad. Can I have more raspberries if I finish it up? That's a good deal! But finishing your dinner gives us all a good example, and you know raspberries are great because they're like nature's candy, full of goodness and flavor. [smiling] Oisin might be a little young for that reasoning, but we're heading in the right direction. When I was little, my mum used to tell me that if I finished my vegetables, I could go on a bike ride. Now I love biking, especially around our garden. We could make fun active plans if we all eat well, right? Yeah, and it's not just about the food we eat but also the activities. Biking or even just a walk outside can help to motivate you to eat better because you feel good and energized after. [excited] Walking? Can we walk after dinner and look for bird eggs? I saw some in a nest at the park. Oh, that sounds like a fun idea, but we need to be careful with nature and respect the birds. We can just look without touching the eggs or the nest. It’s also a good opportunity to talk about what the birds eat, right? Most birds eat berries and insects, like those raspberries we have or even worms for the birds that eat them. [chuckling] Careful now, Oisin. We're not making bird food for dinner. [laughs] But you know, I have a garden at home where I grow some veggies. It’s fun for all of us to help out and see where our food comes from. It might be a bit of a stretch to turn them into bird feeders for the moment though!

Ah, I'm so glad we could all meet up today. It's been ages. How have you all been? I've been keeping busy with work and keeping the house tidy. You know how it is. How about you, Judith? Any new projects? Oh, I've just been enjoying my retirement. You know, ticking off those little jobs around the house and taking my time to read a bit more. It's been lovely actually, quite the change of pace. Oh, I've got so much to catch up on with you three. Speaking of jobs, did you hear about that new supermarket on the edge of town? I heard they're doing some delicious specials. Yeah, I just went there last Saturday to do some food shopping. They have fantastic deals on fresh produce from local farmers. That sounds lovely. I used to love doing the food shopping when I worked. Nowadays, it's mostly for my grandkids and friends. But, you know, it's still a rewarding thing to spend on. How about you, dear? I love food shopping, it's like a whole different kind of shopping. You get to see everything new and fresh, and it always gives me good ideas for meals. Where did you get that great idea for that roast lamb recipe the other day, Susan? Oh, that was from my mum. She's always been my go-to for traditional family recipes. But I'd love to try some of those new things from the supermarket. Maybe we could even arrange a meal out one night? Just the four of us, or maybe even with the kids and grandkids. Now that's a fantastic idea! I'm all for catching up over a good meal. Except, dear, do be careful if you're planning to have the grandkids along. The young ones can get a bit rowdy in restaurants. She's right, but it's been ages since we all got together. It would be lovely to see the kids and grandkids enjoying each other's company. Maybe a family-friendly place would be best. Absolutely, family-friendly is key. I know a place near the park that often has a special deal on Sundays, plus they have a play area. What do you all think? Sounds wonderful to me! And perhaps afterward, could we arrange for someone to give us all a quick eyebrow trim?

Ah, I'm so glad we could take some time to catch up. Look after you and the baby are doing super. How are you finding the weening process? Honestly, it's been a bit stressful, but baby Xander is doing well, considering. He's a bit fussy but he's adapting okay. It's me who's struggling more! That's totally understandable. It's always tough, isn't it? Definitely. But it's also been nice that he keeps coming to get a cuddle when he needs comfort. That's such a blessing – it means your bond is strong, dear. I used to find it really helped to have a support system like you have with your husband. You're right, though. We've been lucky. Anyway, I wanted to ask you about signing. I’ve started taking some sign language classes – its being really interesting! Oh, that's fantastic! I've always thought it was such a useful skill. How are you finding it? Great! It's amazing how early they can start picking up visual cues. Absolutely! They say it really helps with communication and can reduce frustration for both the baby and the parent. Plus, maybe one day he'll be able to communicate his needs before he speaks. That would be such a blessing, especially in times like now when you're weening him. Communication really is key. Have you ever thought about taking a class? It’s really easy to learn and it's useful skills for life, even if you don't end up needing it with Xander. I have actually. This week Xander's nursery has been running some parent-child signing sessions. I think that would be a lovely activity for us to do together. Ah! That sounds great. I can give you the details if you like? That would be so kind of you. I could use the support and company. No problem at all. As for plans for the week, I've actually got a bit of a social whirl – we've got a few meetups lined up with friends and family.

You know, I have never been this far into these hills before. The scenery is breathtaking. Do you think they have always been the same way? I'm not sure, but this area has a fair few hundred years of history. I'd imagine the landscape has changed a little over time, but the essence of it, the rolling hills, the quaint villages, I'm sure they have been relatively unchanged. That village in the distance, for instance. Do we know much about its history? It's Oakton Village. I've read a bit about it. It dates back to the 12th century, but from what I recall, the church we see on the ridge has parts that go even further back. It's been updated over the centuries, of course, but the site itself is ancient. Really? That's quite a claim. It never ceases to amaze me how much history we overlook, don't you think? I mean, we're just walking through this landscape, and there's so much stories lying beneath our feet. Absolutely. It's easy to get caught up in our daily lives, but every place has a story to tell. It's one of the reasons I love coming here, especially as someone who studies history. It connects the past in such a tangible way. I feel that too. As a lecturer, doesn't it sometimes feel like it's hard to keep the past relevant for students? It can be a challenge, yes. But experiences like these, where you can literally touch and see the past, make it much easier to connect the dots. I've tried to incorporate as many field trips and local visits as possible into my teaching. It's incredible to see the interest spark in students when they can see historical sites firsthand. I'm sure it does make a difference. Imagine having grown up surrounded by this, though. How do you think that would shape a person's perspective? Again, it's about those stories. Living here almost makes you a custodian of sorts, doesn't it? You hear these stories and histories, and it inherently makes you more mindful of your place in the larger timeline. That's interesting. I sometimes wish that was more of a part of city life. Maybe because we're so used to building new and moving fast, we lose sight of our roots?

Hey, I was thinking we might catch a movie tonight if you're not busy. On the road, of course, unless we decide to stop somewhere for a bit. Oh, that sounds fun! There's a really good new release on Netflix now, the sci-fi one with the British director. I think we'd both like it. Yeah, I've heard good things about that. Have you watched it? No, not yet. But your friend Alex mentioned it was quite good. How is he doing, by the way? Oh, Alex is doing really well. He's been pretty busy at work with the new project he's been assigned. Seems like it’s going to open up a whole lot of new opportunities for the company. That’s great to hear! Job well-done to him. It’s wonderful when people you care about succeed, isn't it? Definitely! It’s quite the challenge, though, I can imagine. I barely keep up with the corpus when it comes to these technical things, and I’m just an administrator. But that’s what keeps this job interesting too, I suppose. I understand the sentiment. There’s a certain satisfaction in managing the intricate details that make a project work. In my line of work, even as a consultant, there are always new variables and challenges. But it’s rewarding to see a piece of infrastructure or design become functional and benefit people. Speaking of functionality and infrastructure, have you noticed how much more cyclists we’re seeing lately? We almost never used to pass so many cyclists on the road. Yes! I’ve been noticing that too. It’s great for the environment, but sometimes I worry about them when I see people not wearing helmets or going side by side, taking up the whole lane. I worry more about our safety. Sometimes they seem to come out of nowhere and before we know it they're right beside us and it’s always a bit of a heartstopper. It’s a good thing we drive carefully, then. No need for any incidents. Hopefully, city planning will start adding more bike lanes. I hope so! It would make cycling safer and maybe even encourage more people to give it a try. Mobility and green solutions are definitely in the future of urban planning. As an engineer, I’ve been part of several projects that aim to increase cycling infrastructure across cities.

Ah, isn't this just the most beautiful spot to take a walk? Look at all the wildflowers. They remind me of my grandmother's garden when I was a child. She used to tell me about each one. Indeed, it's lovely here. You know, I've always been fascinated by the kind of wildflowers that grow across England. Speaking of plants, have you heard about the government's new cash crops initiative? It's causing quite a stir in our economics circles. No, I haven't keeps up with it. What's it about? Essentially, they want to focus more on growing crops for biofuel and other industrial uses rather than food. There's a moral argument that we should be prioritizing food production given world hunger issues. But there’s also a good economic case to consider - the demand for biofuels is going up and it could boost our agricultural economy. That's interesting. I was thinking more about the wildflowers in a research context. Like, how similar or different various wildflower species are across England. Someone should study that. That's a great research idea! I can see it now: 'Socio-Economic Impacts of Government Policies on English Floral Biodiversity'. Well, perhaps not quite that dramatic, but yes, there's certainly an academic angle to explore. It's nice to see you take an interest in this, especially after your hectic academic schedules in London. How was your last conference? It was good. Actually, that's where I saw the most incredible socio-linguistic study on the colloquialisms of Southeastern England. The influence of technology on dialect, especially among the younger generation, is just fascinating. That sounds intriguing. How do you think these changes affect the sense of community or belonging? That's a question we’ve had before, hasn't it? I think it's multifaceted. While dialect often gives people a sense of shared identity, especially regionally, the global spread of language through technology is making it harder for some dialects to survive in their purest form. However, there’s also evidence that it allows people to maintain community ties across distance, which is a positive. Absolutely. This reminds me of the football fans I used to work with on my ethnographic studies. They use unique dialects and slang in their communication online, which really strengthens their sense of identity and community across different regions.

Right, so we’re planning this trip to Newcastle first, right? To see your parents. Yeah, that’s the plan. I talked to my mum the other day and she said they're all excited to see you. Nice, I need to get ready for questions about football then. Going over the league table and all the last few matches. You’ve been right hooked on that fractious Sunderland season, haven’t you? They’re your club, through thick and thin. Well, yeah, but being from Sunderland, you’ve got football in your blood whether you want it there or not. That’s true. Seeing the Stadium of Light at games is always a treat. It really stands out. Though I must say, I’ve always been fascinated by the Angel of the North when we take A1 up to Newcastle. Yeah, it really is a landmark now. I actually used to drive past it almost daily when I worked over in Gateshead. But it’s not just about the giant sculpture, it’s the whole environment around it, the industrial backdrop, the design...the effect it has on the landscape. Definitely a national symbol, blurred the lines between art and architecture. Speaking of blurring lines, remember when we discussed flats near by before? You were looking for somewhere closer to campus? Oh yeah, the search hasn’t stopped. I was on the lookout for a flat that isn’t too pricey but also not too far out. I’ve been working on a similar thing, looking at viability for a project up north. The housing market's been quite the rollercoaster and it’s about finding the right balance between affordability and quality of life. Definitely. It’s hard to find that balance. Parking in the city centre is also a constant nightmare. You mean the whole free-for-all parking outside Gateshead Metro?

Thank you so much for coming over today to help clean our house. It was so thoughtful of you to consider doing it at short notice and for such a good price! No problem at all, love. It's no trouble really. I'm just happy to help out whenever I can. Besides, I love questions and catches up with you and the others. It makes the day fly by, doesn't it? Absolutely! It's always lovely catching up with you. I was just talking to your mother about how much she enjoys your visits. You must get a lot out of seeing her too, right? Oh, absolutely! It means the world to me. These little visits, they're just what gets me going sometimes. Though, let me tell you, even with all the work, I still find time to watch my nature shows. I'm obsessed with the migrating geese this time of year. Oh, yes! I remember when we used to spot geese flying overhead in these autumn months. It was a regular sight, wasn't it? That's right! I'm always this time of year watching the news for stories about their migration patterns. Did you know the geese change their routes based on weather conditions? No, I had no idea! That's fascinating. It really shows the level of intelligence they have to manage their migrations so well. It does indeed. I remember one year, there was an unusually large group in Peterborough, because they'd been deterred from their usual route by a storm. And we were all over the place, donating food and whatnot because they were struggling. It was quite the event that year. Oh, dear, I don't think I was in town then, but I can imagine it would have been quite a sight. I just love the fact that they keep coming back to the same spots year after year. Seems like they have this internal GPS. That’s quite a leap, but I'll take it. Internal GPS for geese. Oh, I'm sure there's a scientific term for it but it sounds quite charming as you put it. Reminds me, have you two caught up on any of these celebrity trials that have been making the news? Or perhaps you're more interested in wildlife and nature? We're all over the place really. I work in sales

Ah, I'm so glad we could catch up, Sarah. It's been ages. How have you been? Oh, I've been alright, thanks for asking. Got married last year, but we're still waiting for that baby to arrive. That's great! Congratulations! I hope you don't mind me saying, but it must be a bit of a worry now that you're nearing the due date. Of course I mind!  laughs  But it's always that weird mix of emotions, isn't it? Excited and terrified. Absolutely. I remember when I had my first, just the uncertainty and all those bits of advice from everyone. Right? So, how’s your side of life? Keeping busy with language teaching? Yeah, it's always busy but rewarding. I actually just had a particularly stressful project with one of my international students. She's from the Middle East and struggled a lot with the different intonation patterns in English. It's funny because it made me realize how often English speakers use intonation as much as the words themselves. That is quite fascinating. I come across it with students from different parts of the world. You’re right, though, the intonation can really change the meaning of a statement. Exactly! It’s such a subtle but important part of communication. Speaking of communication, have you had any job interviews recently? Actually, yes. I've been trying really hard to move into a more senior role, but it’s been tough. I feel like I need more leadership training but doesn’t come in my current position. It’s also the elephant in the room - the Midlands accent. I hear it makes a difference, you know? Oh, absolutely. The Midlands accent can sometimes make people a bit wary, especially in formal settings. But it should never define your abilities, Sarah. Just be confident and remember, everyone’s voice is unique and valuable. True, but changing the way you naturally speak feels so fake, doesn’t it? No, it's not about changing who you are or how you speak in general. It's about adapting so that your message comes across clearly in a professional setting. And you’d want to do the same for any region. That makes sense. I just wish people understood that job skills are what should matter most. I recently read an article about how certain dialects can actually be beneficial in certain environments, like customer-facing roles.

Hey, I'm really enjoying this evening at ANON's house. It's been ages since we've all been together. Yeah, me too! It's so nice to catch up, especially since we've all been so busy. How have you been, Soph, since the company started? It's been a whirlwind, totally. As you know, taking on a production controller role was a big jump for me right after my postgrad. You're so capable, just like your mum. She would be proud of you too, in all her managerial glory. Thanks, that's very sweet of you! Yeah, I think she would be proud, though sometimes I also think she would want me to slow down a little and enjoy life more. I've found the admin and secretarial work kind of assumed I'd just 'manage' but it's quite a juggling act. Especially after we got to the core team, it's been a lot of high-pressure situations. Like, 'Oh, we need this proposal by tomorrow morning', or 'Can we squeeze in an extra shipment this week'? Yeah, I get it. That's been me too over the past two years. Sometimes doesn't feel much like work and more like just "manage" that stress. Right. I guess that's the future career world we're in, though - always being asked to just 'manage' more, do more. Do you ever feel like we've been chasing degrees and qualifications only to end up in roles that are less about what we loved learning, but more about managing a constant changing landscape? Oh, all the time. Sometimes I think about what people used to say: "Get a good degree and you'll have so much choice later..." but reality feels different now. Exactly! And it's not even just about the job itself... it's the cost of living, the constant job switching to find something 'better' or to keep up with living costs. It feels like everything costs more and pays less, especially if you're from outside the bigger cities.

Alright, so I've decided I need a social media detox. I'm just getting so annoyed every time I open up Instagram. Seeing all the holidays people are going on, new boyfriends, and well, just life in general, it's really getting to me. Especially now that the semester’s over and I have so much free time! Oh, I feel you 100%. I've been doing a little bit of the same thing, although I've actually taken a step further. I blocked all the local drama queens from Doncaster that I keeps coming across. But at the same time, seeing all those updates makes me wonder if I'm just being too jealous or if I actually have a right to be annoyed. You know, when your ex starts dating someone new a week after you two broke up... Exactly! It’s the timing and the blatant disregard that gets me. But, you know, maybe it’s better that we focus on ourselves instead of comparing our lives to others. Plus, it’s probably not as perfect as it looks. For me, it’s more about focusing on the present than getting caught up in what everyone else is doing. I’m currently working on some projects that I love, so that keeps my mind busy in a more productive way. Social media can sometimes make you feel like you’re missing out, but in reality, you’re probably just seeing a highlight reel. That’s really great to hear, Speaker_3! You’re right; social media often shows us the best version of people's lives, but we rarely see the bad bits. I need to remind myself of that more. Speaking of projects, how’s your research paper going? You were talking about that last time we caught up. It’s coming along, thanks for asking! I just submitted the first draft to my supervisor. She gave me some really constructive feedback, so I’m busy working on revisions. That sounds like a lot of hard work! But it’s great that you’re staying focused. I was just wondering, how do you deal with jealousy or annoyance in your personal life if it arises? For me, it usually helps to take a step back and assess the situation objectively. Ask myself if my reaction is justified or if it’s just a personal insecurity.

I hope you all enjoy this pasta dish. I made it myself from a recipe I found online and it turned out surprisingly well. It’s supposed to be inspired from a place in Italy. Want to hear the story while we eat? Sure! Tell us. Indeed, share your stories, Sarah. We never get to hear those when you're too busy working. So, this recipe was supposed to be from a small village in Tuscany. Apparently, the locals there have been making pasta this way for centuries. Sounds cool! Do you need to boil the pasta in the water with the sauce? That’s always confusing when I watch you guys cook. That’s how it’s traditionally done, yes. It infuses the pasta with all those flavors. It’s not so hard once you get the hang of it. For me, the hardest part is choosing the right noodles for pasta. There are so many different types! You'll learn. The key is good sauce, and the right balance of ingredients. Speaking of balancing, did anyone watch the hockey game today? I saw highlights online. Yes! John is playing in the school team and they won! And his team mates are his friends from school. That’s great! Did you see the goal? He nailed it! He did! The young man has a good eye. I tried to get tickets to a Wolves match but they were sold out. Hmm, maybe we should plan a family day out to see a Wolves game sometime. You guys like that idea? YES! I’ve never been but I want to go for sure. Me too, but I think we need to save up for that. It can get expensive. We could perhaps plan for next season and pool our resources. Make it a family outing. That sounds like a plan. We’ll make a note of it. And when we go to the game, can we also eat at that Italian place we never get to because we're always late to movies? That could be part of the fun. A full day out. How about that for next fall then? We’ll see if we can plan around youth hockey and school commitments, and maybe even save up for a nice family dinner after the match. I just saw they’ve got some travel deals for a city break. Maybe a mini holiday in addition?

Ah, I'm so glad we could take this trip together. The Redwoods are so beautiful, aren't they? It's my first time out here, and they're even more impressive than I had imagined. I know what you mean. Especially now, the light through the trees is breathtaking. I've been out here a few times before, but it never gets old. Absolutely. I've been working non-stop for the past three months. A trip to the States and especially to this part of California was really what I needed. I totally get it. I'm actually on a bit of a break myself. After finishing my master's degree, I thought it would be easier to find a good job as a translator/editor. But it turns out there's a lot of competition and not as many jobs as I thought. I know the feeling. I studied something pretty niche in university so jobs in that field are rare, and most are overly specialized. Nowadays, I find myself mostly taking anything that comes my way. It’s hard to turn down work, even if it’s just a temporary fix. [laughs] It can certainly be a bit of a rollercoaster, can’t it? Although I always find myself being grateful for the opportunities I do have in my field, even if they're not exactly what I always envisioned. We have to make the best of what we get, don’t we? 100%. And it’s funny how much this trip and this conversation has made me feel all those frustrations just lift a little. We’re lucky to have the flexibility, or opportunity, to take these breaks, aren’t we? Yes, definitely lucky. It’s also nice to have someone to talk to about all this, and not just technical work stuff. We don't get to catch up as often as we'd like, given how busy we both are. I know. Our lives have taken different turns and we just keep getting busier, but it’s always great to reconnect like this. Speaking of reconnecting and lives taking turns, you know my mum almost didn’t come on this trip.

Ah, I'm going to make Chicken Kievs for dinner. Dad always enjoyed those. You know, he was super into watching rugby and he used to mimic the commentators back in our living room, all the "and here comes O'Mahony, he’s almost at the line!" stuff. Ha! Yeah, I've heard about that. Backchat! Oh absolutely. He loved his language of rugby, as much as I love watching him get up and try to “score a try” with his backwards leap. I think it's about time we actually visit Granny. She's always asking about us and how the little ones are doing. Might have to upload some pics to Google Photos or something for Granny. You know, this actually reminds me, I read somewhere that hedgehogs can do better with our gardens than we can. Maybe we should just embrace the situation and leave some biscuits out for them? What? Ah, I'm so excited about tomorrow's work leaving do. We have to make sure we leave a decent note for Alex to cover my tasks. Oh, yes, of course. Are you finished making a handover guide for him? Hey, I'm so glad we could catch up without the kids this time. How's the business side of things going? You've always been such a natural with finding opportunities. You know I love a good conversation about work. It's been solid, thanks for asking. I've actually been looking into some new ventures outside of the UK because of the Brexit-related uncertainties.
