Ah, I'm so glad we could take a break from coordinating this research project. I'm nearly dizzy from all the linguistic data and documents. Oh, definitely needed! I've been swamped with editing and proofreading for our latest book series, and lunch was a welcome respite. So, do you manage to make time for research outside of your publishing work? You seem quite busy. Oh actually, I do occasionally. I found this fascinating book on how dialect shapes identity when I was shelving at the library last week. It was fascinating, I just devoured it in one evening. That's interesting! I've been thinking a lot about dialects from my London upbringing, and how different even slightly different accents can convey so much about a person without them realizing it. Exactly! Hence my job. I'm actually doing some fascinating research on how language changes over generations in different parts of London. Our department's thinking of applying for a grant to further that research, which is quite thrilling. That sounds really interesting! So, where were you born? I'm curious about how it affects your view of language and culture. Ah, I'm from Aylesbury, which is rather different from London. But growing up in the south-east definitely had its influences. Do you also speak with an accent like the southeast? [Joining in, slightly uncertainly] Ah, I’m from, ah, Sweden originally, but I’ve lived in the UK for a few years now, so I’d say my language is a bit of a mix. But I don’t really carry a strong accent anymore. Oh, that’s really interesting! How does that mix affect your understanding and use of language here? Well, it’s surprisingly seamless, I think. But I did find, for instance, that when I first moved here, people would often remark on my use of certain words—more formal or less common ones, I suppose. But you adapt, naturally. It's really interesting how our diverse backgrounds contribute to how we interact with language, isn't it? Especially for us in the publishing/paper industry, where language is our primary medium, it truly shapes our perspectives. For sure! And it makes our work so versatile too. This project I’m on, we’re looking at almost 50 dialects just in the UK... 50?! That’s incredible. How do you manage to keep track of all of them?

Right, so we need to figure out how we're going to get visas for Mongolia. Both of us are British, so I think we should be fine, but I talked to someone recently and they said we need to apply about six weeks in advance. That sounds about right, but have we started applying for donations yet? I was thinking we could set up an online fundraiser and maybe post about it on social media to get more eyes on it. Good call. I can set that up today and set a target. For donations, how about we get a local business to support us? You know any friends or family who work at companies that might be interested? Yeah, my mate's dad owns a shop in Warrington. He's always been down to support community stuff, so I can give him a shout. That's brilliant, mate. He might even be able to donate a bit of money or goods for a raffle or something. While we're at it, let's also make a list of all the things we need to bring. Passport photos, visas, any specific travel documents, visas... oh, and I need to sort out my passport renewal as mine expires soon. Ah, right. Let's do passport photos today, while the topic's still fresh. I can print them off at work if I need to, but there's also a photo booth near here. Yeah, or we can even take them at home if we've got good enough equipment. I've got a fairly good camera. I was thinking if we're going to print them, we should make sure they're good enough for visa applications. So maybe the photo booth is safest? Just to make sure they meet the requirements. Good decision. On that note, let's also try to post an ad on Gumtree for anyone who might be interested in donating equipment or supplies for the trip. Just couple of small things like water purifiers or first aid kits could be super useful for us. You've already got it all planned out. Good job, mate. Thanks for the support. It's actually starting to feel a bit more manageable when we break it down like this. Exactly. And remember, the sooner we start, the less stressful it will be. Absolutely. I've got a meeting with my boss tomorrow to formally ask for time off.

Hey, I'm so glad we could catch up first thing. I have to admit today's been a bit of a rollercoaster. Last night I was at the hospital with my arm. Got it dislocated at that party, you know? No, I wasn’t there! That party sounds crazy. A dislocated arm though? Are you okay now? Yeah, did you get that checked out? It’s not right to just be fracturing limbs at parties. Oh it’s fine, really. The medical staff seemed quite amused about the whole situation, just had to set it straight. They did warn me though about overdoing it. Sports is gonna be tricky for a while. That’s actually really concerning. You need to take it easy. And have you thought about seeing a uni wellbeing advisor? It’s not just about sports, looking after your health is important too. Absolutely, that’s a good idea. And maybe this semester you should lay off the late nights at parties. I’m speaking from experience here. Ha, well maybe you’re right about both points. Looking after myself might not be the easiest thing for me right now though, I’m so tired. Was up late in the kitchen studying and then the party thing happened. Ah, come on, we’ve all been there. But seriously, studies and parties aren’t a good mix. Speaking of which, how’s your exam prep going? It’s hectic. I swear all I achieve is getting more and more behind. First I had my arm, now it’s like I’m playing catch up the whole time. You should really start prioritizing time management. Maybe set specific study hours or join a study group? I’ve found that really helps focus me, and having people keep you on track. If you think about it, we all have similar struggles. All of us are dealing with the pressure of exams, partying, changing social circles. It’s scary but we’re doing okay. True. I guess what’s most daunting is this new feeling of tiredness. It’s not just physical from the arm, but mental too. It feels like I’m constantly figuring out who to be at university. That’s normal. We’re almost adults yet still students. It’s like being caught between two worlds. Yeah, plus there are always boys or girls to deal with too!

Ah, I'm so glad we could all come together for's Dad's 80th. It's been ages since we've all been together like this, hasn't it? Yeah! It was brilliant! I loved seeing all the family and hearing the old stories again. But, do you have any idea how many times Auntie Jean and Uncle Frank got into an argument this time round? Oh, actually, I've been thinking about that. It seems like it's their annual tradition during these gatherings. You know, it's always something silly. Yeah, but it makes for great entertainment. Remember when they disagreed about the best accompaniment to roast beef - Yorkshire pudding or bread sauce? Right, right. And then there was the discussion about the best football team. As if anyone cares about Uncle Tom's claims about Leeds United being the only proper team! But, seriously, I did learn a lot about the family history. You know, for example, that their first meeting was at a village fete in Malton? We really don't talk about these things often, do we? That's true. The stories get lost over time. But now that we're in this more relaxed atmosphere, it's nice to catch up on all the little details. It makes you appreciate the journey everyone's been on. Yeah, I noticed how much you all looked at old photos. I wish I could see all those photos from when we were younger, and all the ancestors. I know what you mean. There's something special about seeing those faces and how we're all connected through them. It's like we're retracing our steps and seeing how far we've come. Definitely. I just wish I could relate to some of those stories more personally since I'm getting old enough to be taking more interest in family history. You will, my dear. You'll start reading those old diaries and letters and suddenly you'll see yourself in the stories. It’s a journey, but a rewarding one. Mhm. I want to learn more about our family's roots too. Like, I want to know more about those ancestors who came from the Dales. Ah, yes! The Dales are steeped in history. I can look into that for you. Actually, I think I have an old book or two that might be helpful. Really?

Dad, I'm going to need another water bottle soon, I've already drank two today. Oh alright, sweetie. I'll check in the back. Got some pens as well, right? You're quite the fussy writer on the go, aren't you? Yeah, just trying to plan out a few stories. This journey's got me quite bored, but my imagination is healthy. Haha, well, creativity never goes out of style. By the way, when do we plan to stop for lunch? Think about something not too hot, right? We don’t want any heat-induced stomach upset. Yeah, definitely. I was thinking maybe we could go early so we can avoid the heat too. Maybe around Plymouth. Good call. Then we can hit a café or restaurant that has air conditioning. You're thinking ahead already. Speaking of which, are you alright on the tea or coffee? You didn’t order any in advance, did you? No, we didn’t. Do you think we should stop by that Holland and Barrett we passed? I saw they had some cute tea options. Now that's a thought. Might as well, they often have some fun drinks too. And while we're there, can we grab some supplies? You know, for if we get to the cottage and can't find anything immediately. Ah, right. I was meaning to look into some IBS-friendly things. It'd be a shame if we were really enjoying ourselves and then had to stop because of a stomach issue. Absolutely. I was thinking myself that we could reorganize the kitchen and the larder before we arrive, just to make sure you're comfortable. And maybe if we're planning to cook, consider some less spicy options for now. Thanks, Dad. That means a lot. On that note, did you sort out the coffee machine? Last time we went, it was a bit of a faff to get it set up. Yeah, I did. It’s all pre-loaded and packed. I was also thinking that maybe some chocolate would be in order for the journey. You like dark, right? Oh, definitely! And maybe we could take a small pot for the cottage too? Again, health considerations. Good call again. Dark chocolate and maybe some liquorice or honey as alternatives. I know you like that stuff. Yeah. Especially if we're thinking about something soothing.

Everybody, I hope you're all enjoying the evening so far. We have a beautiful spread prepared; Hopeie did an amazing job with the dinner. Oh, yes, indeed. The smell of that chicken is quite captivating. It brings back memories of our university days when we'd do something similar back in the days. I couldn't agree more. And while we're reminiscing, let's not forget our contributions to those meals. Now, with hindsight, it seems like it was much simpler times even with all the chaos of university life. That's true, aunty. Simple yet lazy, full of laughter and freedom from the pressures we feel now with our various responsibilities. Indeed. Speaking of responsibilities, we haven't really talked about what's been keeping us busy lately. What's new with each of you? Work, as usual, but also a fun project on the side. I’m thinking of starting a local educational initiative, focusing on history and heritage. It's been a passion of mine for years, but I've never had the courage to start it. Oh, that sounds quite fascinating. I'm sure it'll be beneficial for our community. I've been involved with local educational projects while I was headmistress. If you ever need guidance or resources, I'm more than happy to help. Well, I've decided to tackle some renovation projects for families in need, using my carpentry skills. It's been rewarding, really connects with the community in a meaningful way, and it’s fulfilling in a different kind of way than my usual work. That’s fantastic! Your work with wood has always been impressive, and finding ways to use it for good is admirable. That reminds me. Did I mention that I’ve been exploring different cooking methods again, perhaps inspired by my project. I found a way to reduce waste while making meals for larger groups. It's similar to what they do in some community kitchens but tailored to household needs. That sounds like something out of a textbook. Education for sustainable habits in everyday life. I often talk about similar concepts when discussing environmental issues in our local schools. It does seem like a worthwhile project. Speaking of everyday life, how have the kids been? I haven’t seen them in a while. They’re doing well. Tom and Emily are growing up so fast.

Hey everyone, gather round for a second will you? I’ve been thinking about our Mother’s Day plans and wanted to discuss them all together. Speaker_2 : Are we doing something special? Speaker_3 : Yeah, questions? Well, I was thinking, as it’s quite a special day, maybe we should have some pre-arranged plans right? Like what? We could go for a picnic at Forest School, if the weather is fine. That sounds fun! Can we bring our favorite toys? Well, yes, certainly, just like you to bring something you’d like to share. But let’s also make some little Mother’s Day cards. What’s that? You know cards? We make them for mothers on Mother’s Day, it’s a tradition. Oh, like presents but not really. Exactly! And then we could maybe have a little party this evening, just the four of us, with some of Mum’s favorite treats. Can we still go for a walk too? Absolutely, we can plan the day around the weather. If it rains, we could have a fun indoor day instead, maybe play some board games or watch a movie, all things Mother would enjoy isn’t it? Yeah, we could also make a wish tree. What’s a wish tree? It’s a small tree or even a big branch where we tie little notes on with our wishes or just kind words for Mum. That’s a great idea! I like that! I can write down things I think Mum does really well. That would be lovely, but remember it’s a day for Mum so let’s also make sure to tell her everything we appreciate her for, not just on paper. Can we also talk about idioms? Idioms? What has that got to do with Mother’s Day? Well, could you explain some more? Like what does "the apple doesn’t fall far from the tree" mean? That’s a good one. It means that children often have traits or skills similar to their parents. So like I get my love of reading from you? Exactly! And maybe you get your enthusiasm from Mum, who knows? How about “spill the beans”? What does that mean? That means to reveal a secret. But there’s also "piece of cake" which means something is really easy. Oh, I get it! Like when someone says, “Oh, this homework was a piece of cake.”

Hey, I'm so glad we could catch up without the kids this time. Yeah, it's about time! I've been meaning to ask you, how have you been handling everything with your mum's diagnosis? To be honest, it’s been tough. She’s really brave, but I don’t think she fully understands her condition and the treatments they're suggesting are quite aggressive. I can imagine. My uncle went through something similar. It's very difficult for us as family too, keeps coming back to consciousness when you least expect it. Exactly. Like when we're having a normal conversation at the dinner table, and suddenly her mention of something connected to it brings it all to the forefront again. Definitely. And from your perspective, what are the doctor's plans, and has she started any treatment? They're exploring surgeries and chemo, looking for a combination that reduces the size of the tumor. But the prognosis isn’t great, which is making it harder for me to support her through all these options. Sometimes I feel like I'm advocating for her treatments more so than anyone else. That must be extremely challenging. My uncle’s initial reaction to his diagnosis was denial, while the rest of us were trying to discuss realistic possibilities. It was a real balancing act to provide support while also being mindful of what we could and couldn't do. It's always a balancing act, isn’t it? Like when we talk about the really tough subjects with our kids too. My son’s a bit young but my daughter's been through a painful situation with a friend and I'm trying to find the right words and the right amount of information to share. Absolutely. I remember when my son was going through that phase of understanding death, it was hard to explain to him, especially when it comes to a family member. You just want to protect them from pain but also help them deal with reality. That’s so tough! I read somewhere that honesty and shared reading can help prepare them. Like books or even video content created for kids on these tough topics. I want to do it right but I’m not sure I can. That’s a great approach. Honesty helps a lot, even if it’s hard. It shows they can trust you.

Hey, good morning! How was your day? Hey! It was pretty chill aside from my study session. I was practising Korean again. You wouldn’t believe the number of food shows I watch. Want to grab breakfast at the new place on the corner? Sure, sounds good. I’ve been looking for a place to grab a decent vegetarian breakfast and I heard they have a good selection of plant-based items. Perfect! I was thinking of trying their vegan biryani. It’s supposed to be amazing. You know, alongside all the Korean stuff, I’m also really interested in seeing the Indian vegetarian scene when I travel there – it’s supposed to be just as diverse and interesting. That’s cool, have you learned to make anything from those culinary shows? Aside from the language of course. Yeah, I tried making bibimbap and it wasn’t bad for a first attempt, but oh my God, the process was so meticulous. Everything needs to be cut just right, it’s like an art form. And it makes you appreciate the dedication that goes into these preparations. Absolutely! Now that I'm teaching this semester, I have to prepare everything beforehand when planning my classes. It’s fascinating the diligence students show towards their subjects, right? Exactly! It’s the same with cooking and studying – the prep work, the attention to detail, and the passion for the subject matter – it’s all interconnected for me. Speaking of interconnected subjects, have you thought about incorporating any of this into your dissertation? Exploring the intersection of culture, language, and food from a sociolinguistic perspective could be quite unique. True, I hadn’t thought of it that way, but it could be intriguing. I’ve been considering something around cultural influences in the English language. But side-tracking, any preferences for ramen or just the fruit bowls they sell here? Both. Ramen is my comfort food and fruit bowls are quick and nutritious. Also, I must ask, what’s the deal with changing the lecture times in your department? You mentioned something earlier. Yeah, it’s because some of our lecturers are now teaching joint courses and there’s clash in timetables. I’m just trying to adjust everything to make sure I don’t miss any of my classes. Oh right. Timetabling can be such a nightmare sometimes, especially in the university setups. Did you consider looking at external resources if you need additional help with certain topics?

Who here has been to Sugarhouse? Thought it was an alright night, but nothing too wild. Yeah, I was there last weekend. Got a little wild, but had some fun times. Want to go again soon? Did anyone else hear about the flooding in Lancaster? I'm kind of freaking out about the possible flood warnings. Yeah, heard about it too. Hopefully, our house is high enough to be safe. I'd hate to deal with that. You know, alongside all this flooding talk, I'm thinking about planning a camp trip this summer. Like in the Lake District or somewhere. What do you think? Camping in England? Sounds lovely! I've been to Snowdonia for camping and loved it. Was nice being in nature and away from the city life. Definitely joining if you're going! Maybe we could even make it more interesting with a trip to Africa afterwards? Just a thought though, might be a little crazy. Uhm, Africa? That's quite the shift. I love the idea though! We could plan carefully. Maybe look into volunteer work there too, it could be a cool experience. Exactly! Volunteering would be amazing. I've been wanting to do something like that for ages. Okay, plausible, but let's not rush. First, we need to figure out our campsite. The details can take months to arrange. Good point. Planning is key, really. But have any of you started playing Articulate or Heads Up in our uni days? I saw those board games and thought it might be fun. Yeah, we should definitely have a game night sometime! I bought Articulate when I was at sixth form, and Heads Up is definitely more fun together. Perfect idea. I've been watching way too much TV lately, think this will be a nice break. Do you want to do it tonight and order some takeaway? You mean like now? Sure, we might as well plan for today. I'm in! But let's also talk about our timetables. I need to check if I have any free slots for zero-obligation activity today. Yeah, definitely double-check that. Also, let’s pick a themed night. Like maybe all the games are from British TV shows or we play with Twilight-themed questions. Twi-light themed is funny. We could use characters from the books or quotes. Might bring out some laughs. That’s a great idea!

Hey, I'm on my way home from work and I've been thinking about our trip to the Lake District next week. I've never been there during the autumn, but I've heard the foliage is gorgeous around this time of year. That sounds lovely! I've been there a few times, but always in the summer. You’re right though, the autumn colours must be breathtaking. It'll be a nice change from the usual hustle of London, I bet. Oh, it will be. I was just thinking about booking a place with a view over the lakes, if we can find one that isn't too expensive. Have you heard of any decent spots? Well, I stayed in a lovely little cottage near Windermere a few years ago, but that might be a bit pricey for a week. There are some good mid-range places that might fit the bill though. I can look into some options for you. That would be amazing, thanks! I’m sure it’ll be a lovely change of scenery. Did your job ever take you to the North East for work? Not recently, no. I've worked on some projects on the east coast before, but nothing up as far as Sunderland where you're from. You’re from Sunderland, right? Yeah, that’s where I'm from. I used to think the North East was a bit too far from the South for technology companies to consider, but I saw an article the other day about some tech startups setting up there. It seems like there’s more interest in the area now. That’s fantastic. It’s always been a shame that the North East doesn’t get the same attention as the South East and the Midlands when it comes to business development and investments. Hopefully, that’s all changing. That would be great. I hope it leads to more opportunities for people like me, who want to stay in our hometowns rather than having to move down to London or somewhere else for work. Same here. There’s a lot of talent outside of London, and it’s about time it’s unlocked. It’s all happening slowly, but I’m optimistic. Definitely. Imagine having all these opportunities without having to leave Sunderland, or Harpenden for that matter. Exactly! It would be a win for everyone, and it’s about time.

Ah, I'm feelin' right poorly today, innit? Took me ages to get out of bed and even now, my back's been playin' tricks on me. You poor thing. You've been mentionin' that back pain now for months. You really need to get yourself to see a doc, innit? You'd think the weather might have something to do with it, but honestly, I'm baffled by why the weather affects us so much, eh? All this rain and damp can't be good, can it? Speaking of the weather, it's supposed to clear up a bit next week, so that's something to look forward to, isn't it? Oh, let's hope it does. I've been stuck inside so much, it's getting on my nerves. Getting on your nerves? It's been gettin' on mine for ages! You two both seem a bit down, though. How about we move on to somethin' more uplifting? Say, that new watch I got or that football match on the telly last night? Oh, speaking of football, Norwich got beat again, didn't they? Yeah, it's been one disappointment after another. Well, at least Norwich's got their health club for us to moan about football in without gettin' damp! True that, really. But you know, we’re lucky, despite all the moans. Health's a big issue nowadays, especially for our age group. But it's good to keep the conversation positive, eh? Absolutely, and if one’s in a higher socio-economic group, there’s the flexibility to try those new health treatments and whatnot. Higher socio-economic group? That's a phrase I've never associated me with before! Well, you know, it's not just about money changing hands. It's about access to information, health services, recreation… Yes, you're right about that. Though, it can't always take away the underlying issues. Like, all this information about what we should and shouldn’t be doin’ for our health. Can't win, can we? No, but we can enjoy each other's company, share our grievances, and still find some joy in the simple things. Like that lovely cup of tea I made for you all. You always know how to make things better, don’t you? Indeed we do, and I'll make sure to share some of those health and well-being tips from my lectures with you, too.

Hey everyone, gather round for a bit of gossip first, alright? So Grace has got engaged; how are we all feeling about that? That’s awfully sweet of her fiancé, I suppose. Right? Though I must admit I've just heard the rumour about him being – well, let's just say 'notorious' around town. What's everyone’s vibe on that? Honestly, I've actually met him at a few events, and he seems very nice. Polite and genuinely nice to talk to. I get how it can be mixed feelings seeing someone you like get hitched, but you’ve got to be happy for your friends, right? Oh yes absolutely. Congratulations, Grace! Fingers crossed everything goes smoothly. You deserve the best, my love. Thanks, guys. It’s actually been a whirlwind, so it’s nice to hear positive things. But as much as I love this wedding announcement, have you heard about… well, similar news in the making? News in the making?! You’re not getting engaged? Not yet! But I did go on this super neat date the other day with someone. It was genuinely good; he made me laugh and we totally clicked, you know? Oh, how exciting! But hey, nice to see you focused on yourself as well, all things considered. Good for you! Now that we’re here, and all agog with wedding and potential wedding news, shall we plan a girls’ night in for next week? Grace’s fiancé’s family is kind of holding a stag do here, but I think we should keep it low-key and just the girls? That’s a great idea! I love having a girls’ night. But funnily enough, while we're on this subject, do any of you feel the pressure to settle down and kids, you know? Because I’ve been getting so much of that from my family lately. Like, why does everyone care so much? Oh, for sure. I know what you mean. Sometimes, it feels so much like an expectation rather than a choice. But real talk, has anyone else been feeling this pressure, and how are you guys coping? Honestly, I've just been trying to tune it out and focus on my career and enjoying life right now. Kids can wait; I’m not ready. But I’ve been reading up on so much stuff from influencers about staying child-free and finding that really empowering.

Ah, good day everyone. Lovely to see you all's here. I brought today's newspaper, if you'd like to have a look. Thought it'd be talked about at least the Brexit stuff. You two been following that at all? Actually, yes! It's a right mess, ain't it? Can't make head nor tail sometimes. What's got people talking now? Well, they're saying the talks might be right at the crunch point. Negotiations are going very slowly. It's always about goods and money, never considers us people really. Indeed, yes. 'S always seemed like a big game to me, with the little ones having to pick up the pieces later. Though, let's not go there too much. I prefer talking about less serious things, like my grandson's new passion - oh, he's taken to playing this horse racing game online. That's quite popular these days, isn't it? Our grandkids seem to love those games. Though, it's good for them to learn about things like financial management through them, innit? That's true. Education through games can be quite effective. But it's a strange thought, isn’t it? Thinking the next generation is learning about money and risks through games. Absolutely. Strikes a chord with the money problems we've been facing, us older folks. Still, it's technology doing its thing, giving the young minds some insight into real-world problems. Speaking of money, we should be really careful with that, considering we’re both, well, never really worked and now face long-term employment issues. But it's not just about the money now, is it? It's about keeping active and engaged. Speaking of which, did you two know the village is planning another horse show? Might be a good day out to see, relax. Oh, that sounds right up my alley. I used to love horses before health issues got in the way. Still, it'd be good to see a bit of the old routine again. We could sit together and watch. Yes, I'd like that. I used to go for rides with my children when they were little. A horse show would be such a nostalgic treat. It'll give us a chance to remember the good old days, and enjoy the sunshine perhaps. Yeah, plus it's local and might be socially beneficial for us all to get out, see some familiar faces.

Ah, good morning! It's lovely to see you, Mr. Johnson. How are you today? Good morning, young one. It's always a pleasure to see you. I'm doing all right, thanks for asking. Just trying to keep myself occupied with this crossword puzzle – it's given me some kind of brain workout since I retired. That sounds like a good healthy challenge. Language has always been of great interest to me, I teach English to foreign students and it’s so rewarding to see how they pick up new words and grammar. Oh, that's interesting. Tell me, do they ever get your accent from the southeast confused with the more southern accents they've heard of? Oh, quite the opposite! They often tell me that the South-East London accent is quite distinct and sometimes even harder to understand than the more neutral accents they're used to. But it's all part of the fun and challenge of learning a new language, right? Indeed, indeed. I remember when I worked in London, I used to struggle with the different dialects. But it was all quite fascinating. Nowadays, it seems everyone is learning to speak English, isn’t it? Quite true. English is widely used as a second language and as a lingua franca across the world. It’s wonderful to see how it bridges so many cultures and countries, isn’t it? Speaking of bridging cultures, have you ever thought of travelling more? You're still young; you’re probably well placed to explore the world. Oh, absolutely! I would love to travel more. Last year, I took a trip to Spain and it was an incredible experience to practice all the Spanish I teach in real life. Spain, you say? Lovely place! I was thinking of going there when I was younger but never managed. There's still time! It's never too late to travel. I heard of a group of older people who even decided to learn Spanish together and then they went on a trip to Barcelona. Inspiring, isn’t it? I suppose it never is too late. And it's always good for the mind too – keeps it sharp. Exactly. Did you have any hobbies when you were younger or during your career? Oh, when I managed, I played a lot of golf. It was a great stress reliever and something to look forward to on the weekends.

Hey, so did you manage to sort anything out for Valentine's Day? I was really hoping for a decent film and maybe some dinner at a nice place after? Hmm, not really. You know how it is when you're at uni. It feels like everyone is either too busy with deadlines or already paired up. I just ended up stuck at home watching movies and eating stale popcorn. Oh, I know, it can ruin the vibe when you’re expecting something and it just doesn’t happen. Exactly. Plus, nothing beats having a hot date right? But we’ll try and make the best of it next year, eh? Definitely, we’ll make sure next year’s planning starts early and is taken seriously. Speaking of food, have you tried that new Vietnamese place near the library? I heard it’s really good and cheap too. It might be worth a shot if we ever feel like a proper meal instead of usual canteen food. Oh, that sounds like a plan! I’ve been meaning to try it out since the opening. Maybe we can even go on a quieter weekday? I’m not sure it would be quite as buzzing on a Friday evening. Right, good idea. Less queue, more time to enjoy. Plus, they might have more English at that time rather than trying to pick out the right thing in the rush. Ah, the struggle of trying to order when you’re unsure, especially if it’s one of those places where they barely speak English. One time, I wanted a coffee and all I got was a 'cot'. Like a bed, not coffee... Oh no, I can just imagine! Did you get to say 'No, no, COFFEE'? Exactly! I had to repeat it a few times, and of course, by then it was funnier than problematic. Oh, that’s hilarious. My auntie always says that she got 'corn' when she asked for 'can't' at a restaurant once. It’s these sort of mix-ups that remind you how important accents are for basic communication. True, but it’s also kind of cute in a weird way. Reminds you how small the world is when you can share little miscommunications like that with someone. Exactly! It’s like our job as language enthusiasts to embrace the weirdness. For sure. I mean, it could be worse; I could be trying to explain what 'faff' means...

Hey, I'm so glad we could catch up without an agenda. To start, today's newspaper really got me thinking. The articles about racism and its effect on social mobility are eye-opening, aren't they? Are you still involved in the activism work you were doing last year? Yeah, I am, but it's harder now. You know, COVID and everything else, it's been tough to keep up momentum. But that's exactly what we need, right? More momentum, more voices. Have you heard about that new report from the London School of Economics about racial inequalities in housing? It's shocking. You'd think it's a thing of the past, but it's not. I hadn’t, but it sounds in line with what we talk about often. The housing market, especially in London, it’s becoming less of a place to live than a luxury commodity. I just got through a project in Westminster and the prices are ridiculous! It makes me feel bad for the younger generation. Exactly! I barely see my younger cousins dream of ever owning a home in their own city. And the shift in their political views because of this… it's worrisome. We're talking about capitalism, right? It's like it's been allowed to run unchecked, causing all this social and economic strife. Absolutely. It’s a vicious cycle, isn’t it? Capitalism can't fix the problems it causes, and yet, it's the dominant system. The jobs I take on as an architect, I try to advocate for more affordable and community-led projects, but it's an uphill battle. You working that through projects is admirable. I was thinking… would it be feasible for you to lead the design phase of a community project? There’s a local group in Kensal Rise looking for just that. It could really bring about some tangible change. I’d love to, but the time commitment. I’m already juggling several projects. However, if we could integrate it into some existing work or if there's funding available… That’s what usually holds me back - the lack of resources. I see. Well, maybe we can talk more about this over the weekend? I know some connections and might be able to set up a meeting so we can discuss this properly. And if you're free, maybe we can even grab some tea and discuss it.

Ah, I'm so glad we could catch up without the babe. I've got so much to share with you. Thanks, talked to her for the whole morning! Made lunch but I need a break! Did the morning go okay with baby starting nursery? Well, she was pretty surprised and didn't want to leave me at first, but the teachers were so lovely and settled her right in. Now she’s outgrowing her nappies too. That’s good, at least it wasn't a huge tantrum to start, those can be a bit upsetting. Yeah, I was expecting something big from her. But then again, I think she is actually excited to be learning and seeing new friends. That’s the best, hearing she’s enjoyed it. Sure, but its being left at a nursery for the first time, she’s only little. And now I suppose it's back to work for you? That can't be easy. For me, yes this is it. It's been a weird few years balance between uni and everything else. I'm looking forward to getting back to study but the pressure of balancing work and baby in nursery is making me anxious. It's a huge adjustment. But it’s important to remember that you can prioritize your study as well as your daughter. She’ll still be developing even when you're not right beside her all the time. That helps. But it's terrifying! I'm worried I might not be good enough at either. There’s no such thing as good enough, dear. You're doing everything one can in these circumstances. We all have different strengths and weaknesses, and together, we'll figure out the best way to keep everything moving smoothly. Thanks for saying that. It really does reassure me. That's what a family is for. Yeah, can we also maybe talk about a family holiday somewhere? A holiday is such a great idea. We need it too. I mean, having the baby going into nursery does give us a bit more freedom, doesn’t it? Definitely feels like we could finally plan something. Maybe Spain or Portugal? Ah, that sounds lovely. I always love the Spanish coast. Warm, beautiful beaches. And they’re family-friendly too. I’ve seen some amazing baby-friendly resorts. Right, and maybe you could even get back to reading a book yourself?

Right, so did you manage to sort out that awful phone bill from EE? Ah, yes. Took quite a bit of effort, but I managed to get them down on that charge. It was some ridiculous voice rate for a call that only lasted a few minutes. Must be such a hassle. Glad it’s sorted though, eh? Absolutely! It makes me so mad when companies just bill you for whatever without any warning. And how was your day otherwise? Anything out of the ordinary happen? Oh, just went to the police station. They wanted to get a statement from me since I was apparently a witness to something from a few weeks ago. Not like it was any big deal, but still, waiting around in the station can be a drag. Witness to what? An accident or something? Yeah, there was a small incident with a car and a cyclist near Hinckley. Nothing too serious, thankfully. But these things always take longer than they should. Been any calls from work recently? Now that you’re a manager, it must be quite demanding. Not anything major. Just usual store logistics and team updates. But the pressure is definitely on. Speaking of which, I’ve been getting quite a bit of pressure at work as well. Ah, as a fund raiser, I can imagine. It’s a constant battle, isn’t it? But you seem to manage quite well, don’t you? I don’t know how I do it sometimes, but the team helps a lot. And what kind of plans do you all have for the week? Any big events or meetings lined up? Well, just the usual for me: keep the store running smoothly and probably a review at the end of the week. Nothing too exciting but hopefully productive. And me, I’ve got a meeting with some potential donors on Friday. It’s always a bit nerve-wracking because you never know what’s going to happen. And I’ve got a fundraiser event at the local town hall on Saturday. It’s going to involve quite a bit of organisation, but it should be worth it. Good luck with the meeting and the event. As for me, just weekday work, then I’ll probably go to a friend’s birthday party on Saturday if I can make it. Sounds good to me. I might actually have the day off this Sunday, so maybe we can do something then if the weather's nice.

Ah, good to see you again James! How was your journey here? I hope you didn’t have any trouble with trains after all my warnings about late trains being more talked about than late trains being unrealistically on time, right? Still relatively on time, considering, but I did have to wait an extra 10 minutes at St Pancras. I knew what you meant, though. It’s like a rite of passage for train commuters, right? Exactly! By the way, I've got some keepsakes here from my last trip to Europe - Malarials tablets and a bottle of anti-sea lice spray. I thought about using them as conversation starters, but I wasn’t sure if that's your cup of tea. I’m intrigued. So, you’ve actually tried the "tourist’s vaccination kit?" Exactly! Got a bit overzealous prep for a family trip. It didn’t attract any sea lice, but my mom nearly fainted at the pharmacy. She couldn’t believe the amount of travel medication I’d packed. That’s pretty impressive. So, what about the Rome trip? Did you learn anything new about Roman history that’ll make me feel even more ancient coming from ancient Luton, while I’m gardening in modern Bedford? Oh, certainly. I mean, we can't compete with ancient history, can we? I’m expecting, maybe, something about Roman gardening in Britain or something really unusual. Well, there is something interesting and pretty unusual. Apparently, the Romans used a lot of spices that came from the eastern trade route, which we associate more with ancient China and the Silk Road. They would use these spices in their cooking, which the British then adopted into their own cuisine, particularly in breads and stews, much of which is still a staple in traditional British food today. Oh, that’s fascinating! So next time I’m making a bread, maybe I should add a dash of something from the Roman era. What was it they used a lot of? Noonie’s for sure - in fact, there’s a recipe I found from that era, it includes coriander, cumin, and even chickpeas! They’d grind them in a mortar and pestle. Did you know the ancient Romans loved spices so much that they'd overuse them sometimes? I swear, if they had 21st-century flat whites with hazelnut syrup back then, they’d have been all over that too.

Hey, I'm so stressed out about our English test tomorrow. We have to write an essay; it's been super hard to come up with a good topic. Yeah, I know what you mean. We’ve been doing really well in class so it just feels like this test is supposed to trip us up. What topic are you thinking of? Honestly, I’m still struggling. I was thinking maybe something about “A Christmas Carol” but I’m not sure I can come up with enough to write about. You could get creative with something else. We’ve discussed “To Kill a Mockingbird” a bit in our English lessons. Remember when we talked about the themes and characters? Maybe something about that could work? Yeah, you’re right. I remember we talked about racial injustice and racism in the novel. That’s definitely an important topic. Thanks for the idea. No problem. You’re going to do great. You also know your stuff. Plus, English lessons have been pretty fun this quarter. I barely ever thought I'd say that, but Mr. Smith really makes it interesting. For sure! We’ve also been working on quite a bit of poetry lately, right? That’s actually the bit I’m enjoying more. I found we can express so much in such few words in a poem compared to an essay. Absolutely! And the art lessons have been interesting too. We’re starting a new project focusing on symmetry and perspective. I feel like it’s good to mix things up in school sometimes, really helps with creativity. I completely agree. And our art teacher, Mrs. Davies, she’s so nice and really helps you understand the concepts. Makes the lesson enjoyable. You also helped me with French homework one day. I totally forgot about the conjugation of verbs and had no idea what to do. Thanks again, btw. Anytime. French lessons can be tough but Mrs. Thompson is awesome. She makes it fun. True. She always has fun ways to help us remember new vocab. Like when we play those games to learn new words. Right. Funny how a bit of competition can make learning easier. And have you heard about the school orchestra? Our principal was saying something about a big concert at the end of the term. Oh right! I had almost forgotten we’re working on that wind band piece.

Ah, good day! It feels great to finally sit down and talk. I've been meaning to catch up for ages. How are you, sweetie? Oh, hi Auntie Lucy! I'm doing good. Just finished my exams. Still waiting for the results though, a bit nervous. Oh, I remember those days. It gets easier once they’re over. And, by the way, where are you with your plans? Now that you’re nearing the end of secondary school. Well, I’m still deciding. Some of my friends are planning to go to college. Others are considering apprenticeships or taking a gap year. Ah, hello there! It’s nice to see you both again. How was the school year for you, boy? It was alright. Some teachers were great, while others... not so much. The exams were stressful but I hope I did okay. Stressed, you say? Off we go again. Now, onto something entirely different - how about that bank account or savings for you both? For me, it's always about planning and budgeting. Not really thought about it. I mean, I get pocket money but... beyond that. Ah, the reality of the world. I used to lecture on the importance of vocational training and saving, but current jobs aren’t that lucrative. Speaking of which, how is the economy in Darlington? Alright, I suppose. Small businesses are popping up but jobs are competitive. Plus, doesn’t help that the cost of living keeps rising. Is that why we've been hearing more about people struggling to pay bills and rents? Exactly. More so since the pandemic. Yes, yes. It's all about money these days, isn’t it? Always something wrong and it always seems to circle back to money changing hands. Like it matters if you make the wrong notes for your music theory exam. That’s so typical of you, always coming back to music. But, seriously, it's funny how little most people know about the value of money. I try teaching them in my class but... You’ve got to start somewhere, right? Even if it’s just explaining how those silly credit card traps work. I know that one! They make it sound so simple but... Son, if anyone here understands credit card traps, it’s your auntie here. I’ve become quite the aficionado over the years. Given my... let’s say, “financial endeavors”, I’m also becoming quite successful.

Speaker_1 :   "I was reading today that nearly 60% of the UK population is either overweight or obese. It's staggering. What are your thoughts on this?"   Speaker_2 :   "Well, I'd agree it's a big issue. But, from my experience, it's part life, part diet, and part genetics. I've seen tall, slim people with big, portly families; and short, stout people with very fit kids. It's not just about what you eat, I think it's about your genes as well."   Speaker_3 :   "Absolutely, I think genes play a big part. My sister used to be really slim, but now she's struggling with her weight. And us women, oh we always have a battle with the scales! Women, I mean."   Speaker_4 :   "Indeed. And it's often a vicious cycle: if you're overweight, it's harder or rarer to exercise, which makes it harder to lose weight. It's certainly complex, both genetically and behaviourally. I lecture on health studies, and this kind of topic is always on the news. But it's remarkable how little progress we seem to be making in addressing the core factors contributing to obesity."      "And while we're on the subject of health, did anyone hear about that new surgery for weight loss in Britain? It really is a double-edged sword, isn't it? On one hand, it's a needed treatment for some people, but on the other, it speaks volumes about our relationship with food and exercise as a society."      "Oh yeah, I've heard about it. My neighbor had the operation; she's lost loads of weight, but she always says it's a daily battle not to gain it all back. It's like her body's trying to find its set point again. That and she's always saying it's a very changing diet regime. It sure isn't a quick fix."      "I couldn't even begin to phantom going for an operation like that. It sounds scary! But I've seen how much it's helped some people, like my sister's friend.      "The biggest problem, I think, is how we've commercialized food. We've made 'unhealthy' options cheaper and more available, and 'healthy' options are seen as a luxury. It really is something we need to address from the top down. And while surgery can be a solution for some, it often doesn't tackle the underlying lifestyle issues...

Hey, I've been trying out Moodle recently and I have to say, I really like the intuitive interface. How about you, have you started exploring it? Yeah, I've been working with it for a bit now and I agree. It’s quite user-friendly considering it's a learning management system. Especially when it comes to setting up courses and managing materials. Absolutely, and the fact that it’s open source is a big plus right? Makes upgrading and customizing easier? Definitely. But even with how user-friendly it is, there are still some nuances to get used to, especially when you want to create complex structures within a course module. Exactly, that’s been my experience too. For instance, I spent a bit of time figuring out how to best organize the content without making it feel too cluttered. And the grading system isn’t perfect either, sometimes it can be a bit clunky, but overall it’s functional. True, the grading system could use some work. And I noticed that when I tried to set up a discussion forum, it took me a few tries to get the flow right. But once you get the hang of it, it works quite well. I found the Gradebook is the most useful part though, being able to track student progress and see the entire portfolio of work all in one place is great. Absolutely. And it’s relatively easy for students to engage with. The multimedia support is also pretty solid. I had to teach an online lecture and using Moodle’s built-in media player made life much easier. And the integration with other tools? I saw that it doesn’t come with everything out of the box, but the plugins are quite diverse. Have you installed any? Yes, I installed the Turnitin plugin for plagiarism checks and also the Kaltura plugin for video creation, they were both very useful. The only issue is whenever there's a new Moodle update, there can be some compatibility issues with third-party plugins, and it requires technical knowledge to resolve. Yeah, I ran into that. The tech support for plugins is not always as strong as you’d hope. But in general, it’s still so much better than when we were using WordPress as a makeshift learning platform. Agreed. However, it still has its limits. For example, for more advanced features like interactive simulations or virtual labs, you might need to look elsewhere or use Moodle in conjunction with other software.

Hey there, love! How did you sleep? I'd be lying if I said it was great. The jetlag is really kicking in. It's always tough adjusting to these time zones. I know what you mean. Especially now, after all this international travel. We do need to think about the kids and starting them on a routine soon though, right? Absolutely, we should. I've been thinking, maybe we can start implementing a bedtime routine tonight? Our little one will be 2 in a few months, it's a good time to get them used to it before we start looking at schools. True, and it's just as much for us to have a routine too. Definitely, but what about the performance we're going to tomorrow night? Is it still on? And do we have everything sorted out for the babysitter? Yes, it's on. I've confirmed with Ron again. He's looking forward to it. And yes, we've got the babysitter sorted. Sarah from next door is happy to help us out. I hope you don't mind relying on a neighbor. Not at all, it's great to support each other in the community. Plus, it'll give Sarah a great experience with kids. It will. I'm glad we can also be there for her. Now let's talk about the performance - 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'. Plus, it’s at the local theatre, which has a great reputation. And it’s not too late or too early for the kids. Right after dinner should be okay, they can have their bedtime routine, relax a bit, and then it should be fine. That does sound like a solid plan. So, to recap: We're changing the bedtime routine tonight, getting the kids used to it, and we're all out to see the performance tomorrow. Any concerns or changes for tomorrow? Nope, all good so far. I'm just looking forward to a relaxing evening and a good show. Speaking of relaxing, maybe after the show could we grab some dinner? I could do with a sit-down meal and maybe recover from all this jetlag. Noted. We can book a table after we're back.

Ah, I'm so glad we could catch up without any major passport restrictions these days. It’s been quite some time. How are your family and friends back in Iraq doing? You know, it's complicated. Some are OK, but it's tougher for others. My sister – she teaches English at the university – she had to close her house in Kurdistan and moved to the US with her husband and children. It's difficult to get settled, of course, but at least there are better opportunities. And how about rebuilding keeps coming backwards due to all the political tension? Yes, it's a cycle. They have oil, but it seems like the more they have, the more trouble they get into. You know, like the whole situation with Wahhabi influence... Yes, the Wahhabi movement has had an impact everywhere. Even here in the UK, we've seen some problems with the export of that ideology. Exactly. It's like the economy of war fuels itself, doesn't it? And now Libya... it's all connected in ways that are quite distressing, especially for the ordinary people who just want peace. Indeed, it's heartbreaking. As an academic, I often interact with foreign students who are looking for the 'western dream'. They're genuinely good kids, but the world seems to throw them into these conflicts without their consent. It makes you wonder about the future for young people in those areas. Absolutely, it affects everyone. I remember when I moved here, I had to learn everything from scratch – the culture, the language, even the 'informal rules' of interaction. Yet, despite everything, there's a resilience... and I think that's what keeps people holding on. I completely agree. People’s resilience is truly remarkable. On less serious side of things, any plans to move house? I've been thinking of a new place myself. Ah, actually, yes. There's a house we've been considering in a different part of town. The kids need a bigger garden, and my wife really likes the new community center nearby. That sounds great. I've had similar thoughts. The city's changed so much over the years. Sometimes, it feels so different from when I first moved here from Salzkotten. The community aspect really matters when you have children and education to think about. Yeah, definitely. It’s like... you can’t just throw them into any environment, you know?

Ah, I'm so full. That lamb was amazing, wasn't it? Yes, definitely one of the better home roasts I've had. Right! And don't forget the accompanying mint sauce. That was a nice touch. Going over to the TV now? Or do we need to move the meal into the dining room? I'm right behind you. Let’s just pick up our plates and glasses. Good idea. And while we do that, I suppose I could ask you two about your lazy Sunday TV habits. I usually stick to documentaries. Sports is my thing, especially when it's live. But we can always mix it up - maybe we could even find that cruise documentary you were talking about? The one that showed all the different routes and whatnot? Let's try to find something like that. And I heard there was some new show on BBC about the Mediterranean that looked interesting. Yeah, that might be a good option. I'm sure we can find something that pleases everyone. Speaking of trips, are either of you thinking about going on the Mediterranean cruise at some point? Honestly, I'd love to, but it's not in the budget at the moment... Alright, well, plans change. Maybe it's something we look into for the future. True. We can always start saving up for it or finding good deals. Right, right. Shall we get started with the TV? You know, speaking of saving money or budgeting... do either of you have any issues with our landlord lately? Yes, actually. He mentioned something about raising the rent next year. Oh, not another rent hike! That’s getting quite unfair isn't it? It does seem like a bit much. Our flat isn't falling apart. And it's not like the property has gotten any improvements. This is becoming a topic that comes up more frequently. We should probably discuss how we handle this as a group. Maybe there's something we're missing or another option. I've been looking into rent-a-Villas or something similar if we have to move. Yeah, worth considering. Another idea could be to see if there are better places available across the city. Absolutely. Let's all do some research on that over the next week or two. And maybe even get some advice from a financial advisor if that's a feasible option.

Alright, everyone, what did we all grab for brunch? I was so starving; grabbed a couple of pastries from the bakery down the street. Oh, that's right! You got pastries while I was stuck queuing for the café, but honestly, they do have the best scones. Going to grab some before I head out to my lecture. Yeah, I wish I could’ve joined, but I was still asleep. Just woke up, gonna grab some for my desk-bound day at uni. Are there still leftovers here? Yeah, dude. Plenty. But I’ve been meaning to ask—are there any big family plans coming up soon for you two from the Northeast, if you don’t mind me asking?

Alright, everyone, what did we decide we're making for Mum's baking lesson today? I thought we could try making some gingerbread men. Thought it'd be fun and simple enough for everyone to participate. You two excited to help out? Yeah! I love Gingerbread men! Can we do faces on them? Can I have a cat face and one for my doll, Lily?
