Mom, how would you name your bookstore if you were in France? Well, I had a few ideas. Maybe "Petit Plume" or "Livre Sentier." Do you think we can actually make a little village feel with a bookstore even if we are just in Comberton? Of course! It’s all about creating a warm, inviting atmosphere, right? You could have little reading nooks, maybe even a café area in the back. or even a kid's area with cute little chairs and plenty of stickers. I want the kid's area to have a big train set! Absolutely, we'd have the biggest, most intricate train set anyone has ever seen. And plenty of books about trains, of course! Speaking of dreams, have you guys considered what we could do if we won the lottery? Oh wow, that would be so cool! We could get a dog! But it has to be a cute one that loves adventures. Yeah! And maybe we could build a dog park in the backyard. Right, Dad? Well, that’s a bit of a stretch, isn’t it? If we won the lottery, we’d have to find something more feasible, like traveling and maybe helping out some great causes. Speaking of feasible dreams, we might actually be able to afford a dog soon anyway, right? Plus, I've been looking for a small cottage out in the countryside. We could take turns caring for it. Can we name the dog Buddy? Buddy sounds cool! Can Buddy go on adventures too? Absolutely! Buddy could join us on all our adventures. Even the bookstore could have a special dog-friendly area. So, just to recap, we’ve had dreams about a café, a bookstore in France, a dog park in the backyard, and a little cottage in the countryside. And if we won the lottery, we’d definitely bring all these dreams into reality, right?

Have you seen the news about A&E overcrowding? We've hit record numbers today. Yeah, I saw that. Unbelievable. Makes me worried for when I need to be there, you know? Exactly! Just this morning, I saw a man sitting on the bench outside with his head in his hands. Injured and couldn't get in straight away. And that was before 9 am! And the wait times are just getting worse too. I've heard some people even get turned away because it's just too full. I've noticed that. Like, medical emergencies can't wait. What's the point of going if you have to wait hours in pain? Completely agreed. This is a major issue. It puts pressure on staff too - they're already overworked. Exactly, and it's not just A&E. I've met a nurse recently, she's always talking about the stress of under-staffing and lack of resources. That can't be right. I mean, these are the people that are dealing with this crisis, on the front lines. We're lucky they even stay in this job given the conditions. Yeah, it's really concerning. Have you had any experience with this? Well, I've had to take a family member to A&E a couple of years back, tore his knee badly. Took hours to get seen. Luckily, it wasn’t life-threatening, but it could have been, couldn’t it? And that’s what keeps me up at night. Same here. I’ve had friends who’ve had to wait for hours after finding out serious news. It’s unacceptable. We should be able to rely on A&E. Definitely. I’ve been thinking of writing to my local MP about it. Maybe we can even do something as a community. Organizing some kind of campaign for better funding and staffing in our areas? That’s a great idea! You know they’re already struggling to meet demand. We need more voices. Plus, I think we can use our social media influence too – it can't hurt. Exactly! If we speak up loud enough, policy makers are more likely to listen. It might be one step in the right direction. Maybe meet up next weekend and see what we can do together. Do you think we could gather some examples or share some personal stories to add more weight to a petition or something?

Ah, good day, old chap. How have you been? Not bad, quite alright, thanks for asking. It's been a bit of a whirlwind week, really. Made some great progress on that new business idea I had. Still researching and refining the details, but I'm starting to get excited. Oh really? A new venture, eh? That's quite a challenge, especially at your age. I've heard you've got a fair amount of experience under your belt, though. That's very kind of you to say, thank you. Yes, I've been in various types of business over the years. It keeps things interesting, to say the least. It sure does. I've often considered something like that myself, but teaching was always the path for me. Well, from what little I know - though we do swap stories sometimes - this new project of yours seems like a rather daring one. It's looking that way, isn't it? But, you know, when you've got a dream, there's nothing wrong with trying to make it happen, even if you're not as young as you used to be. Plus, with this particular idea, I believe it could fill a niche that isn’t quite as busy in the current market. That's true. Niche markets can often be a lucrative place to be. It's just the risk and the time investment that can be daunting for some people. Absolutely. But I've learned to balance risk with caution through the years. And really, if you don't try, you'll never know. What do you think about that? Well, I think that's a fantastic attitude to have. I remember my late father used to tell me that, "If you don't take risks, you can’t reap the rewards." Seems fitting in your case. He was a wise man, your father. On that note, did you catch up on any recent news or international events? It's quite interesting to see what's happening around the world lately. Oh, sure. There was this big one about the climate summit, I believe? I'm not entirely sure I follow all these new terms and what they really mean, but it looks like they're trying to make some positive changes internationally. It's a bit of a mess, but it looks like they're making good efforts.

Ah, I'm so glad we could meet up here tonight. The Guardhouse has such great atmosphere, don't you think? The décor is quite reminiscent of the old English pubs back home, but with a slightly modern twist. Absolutely! I love this place. The kind of place where you can easily spend a whole evening just catching up and enjoying a good pint. Exactly! Speaking of pints, shall we actually decide on our order? I'm in the mood for a proper English bitter. I agree with you on that. But before we order, do you want to check on the Happy Valley TV marathon they're supposed to be running tonight? I've heard it's been really popular. Oh, is it still on? I wasn’t sure. Well, that’s a great idea - let’s quickly check and then decide what to have while watching. [They glance around the pub and notice a sign with the TV schedule.] Ah, there it is! Happy Valley marathon is running on the big screen in the corner. They’re between episodes 4 and 5 right now. What do you think? Shall we keep it on and watch some while we're here? That sounds like a plan! While you go get the drinks, maybe I can check what the food menu’s like over there? I’m feeling peckish, and I know they have some quite good pies here. Righto, I’ll grab the drinks then. Also, did you see that new study they did about university grants? It was quite interesting. No, I haven't had a chance to look at the news today. There was something about how some universities were overspending on administration while others were doing more with less. But the article I read did mention the lack of transparency in the grants process. Oh, that does sound concerning. As a transcriber, I often come across reports and studies that deal with governance and administration and it really makes me think about how things could be better. Speaking of governance, is this really comfortable seating or…? No, it's fine. But you're right, I suppose it’s not the most ergonomic. But we’re here to enjoy ourselves, not to work. True! And look, there’s the cat. How about we give it some of that cat food over there? [Chuckles] I don’t know if you should.

Ah, I'm losing count. You're at least your seventh passport stamp from your trip to Africa, aren't you? How was it, man? Was it what you expected? Ye know, I was a bit sceptical at first. A lot of people told me, “Aye, you'll see poverty, you'll see disease, but you’ll also see some of the most breathtaking landscapes and wildlife on earth.” And ye know, they weren't wrong. But it was way more than that. The people. The resilience. The joy in the simple things. It was something else altogether. Oh, that sounds like a real trip. I’ve always been fascinated by the Great Migration, but I’ve been too caught up in work to take a proper break. How was the preparation, though? I read that some of places can be quite... unpredictable. Ah, the preparation was thorough. I’ve done a bit of adventuring before, but this was a different beast. You need to be very flexible, plan for the unexpected. And you can't underestimate travel advice from locals. They know the ins and outs better than any guidebook or website. I’m sure. I remember last year when I went to the Highlands for that workshop training. One of the most difficult parts was predicting the weather. One moment it's sunny, next it’s pouring. It was chaos, to be honest. Aye, the weather in Scotland can be just as unpredictable, but for most of my trip, the weather was great. There were a few cloudy days, but really, the light is incredible in Africa. It’s all about timing and knowing when to take the picture. I wish I could've seen that light. I’ve always wondered how to capture such dramatic moments with my lens. I’ve been doing more and more photography since the workshop, but there’s just something about your pictures that’s a level above, man. Thanks! I’ve been getting into it more and more. There’s something therapeutic about capturing a moment, freezing it and taking it back home with you. And changing the world from that viewfinder... You start to see things differently. I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to capture more of the world around me. Even down here at Ryan’s Bar, I find myself looking at things from different angles, wondering how the light falls on the pint glass or the character of the bar itself...

Hey kiddo, how was your week at work? You’ve been looking a bit more tired than usual. To be honest, it’s been a bit chaotic! The kids are all going through different phases and one of the parents seems to think I have unlimited patience . But overall, it’s rewarding. Yeah, teaching is definitely a rewarding job. I sometimes miss my years at the university. I think I'm right about to be fractious myself if we don't pick up the pace with this nursery planning! Oh, the nursery? I’ve been meaning to show you the plans I’ve made. We can discuss it properly today if you’re free. Absolutely, that sounds just like the plan. So, what’s the plan? What’s the latest from your end? Well, we’ve got a few options. One is a nursery just up the road from here, and another one further out but with a creative curriculum we both like. The problem is, the one up the road is quite small and might not have space for Albert by the time you’re back to work, but he loves playing with the kids there already. Interesting, I liked the location of the first one for me, being close by. But if we can’t guarantee a spot for Albert, that’s not ideal. Exactly, and apparently the second one, even though it’s further away, has a nice structured day with focused activities mixed in. They also offer phonics classes which can only be a good thing for little ones, considering we’re trying to get him into that local private school. Hmm, I see. But it’s further out and the commute for you would be a bit longer, right? Yes, significantly longer. On the upside, the drive is pretty scenic and I could listen to audiobooks or podcasts. But I am worried about losing time in the morning or having to get up earlier for drop-offs and pickups. True, but changing the car routine might not be so bad. It’s all about finding routines that work for everyone, isn’t it? I remember when you used to get picked up from school, we’d always take a little detour for ice cream on Fridays. Maybe we can do something similar for the nursery. Ice cream as motivation is definitely a good idea! On a serious note though, I’ve been meaning to ask, have you got any free time this week to help finalise some of these plans or to maybe visit the nurseries together?

Right, so at my job, I'm pretty much running everything from initial planning to venue setup. It's been super stressful lately because we're trying to pull together this big conference at the end of the month. You two remember that one we did at the beginning of the year? This is going to be a similar size, but we're doing it outside now so the weather is a complete wildcard. Yeah, I remember that! It was huge, and you did an amazing job co-ordinating everything. Is it still at the botanical gardens this time? Yep, still at the botanical gardens. It's going to be a bit of a challenge getting everything set up in time with the weather and all, but I'm managing. You're doing great, Sam. I read that the speakers were from all over the world - do we know how many attendees we're expecting? On the updated estimate, we're looking at around 500 people. That's a big number, but the gardens have done larger events before, so we're in safe hands there. The bigger issue is probably the logistics - we'll have to make sure there are enough seating and this time it won't be as problematic as when we had to reorganize everything due to rain the last time. Yeah, that did happen. I was there setting up at the time and we were all scrambling around under umbrellas. But it ended up being okay in the end, didn’t it? Exactly! Despite the hiccup, everyone seemed to enjoy themselves. But this time, we’re trying to be a bit more prepared with the tent and stuff. That sounds like it'll be a great event. Thanks, guys! I do appreciate the support. Speaking of events, the one we went to last weekend for Natalie’s birthday was fantastic. We had so much fun, right? Yeah, definitely. And I loved your outfit, by the way. Oh, thanks! That dress was actually a bit of an impulse buy. I was running late after a long day of juggling conference prep and ended up popping into that boutique in town for something quick. But it paid off. I thought it suited you really well too. And the food was amazing, wasn’t it? I still can't stop thinking about that cake... Haha, yeah. Clearly Natalie has taken out a personal chef course!

Ah, good day everyone. Lovely to see you all's here. I brought today's tea, freshly made from that old tea set from my mum's side. It's proper tea, proper English tea. You two remember that one from the garden fete at the church last summer? Oh, yes, I do! It’s so comforting to have a nice cuppa and chat. I've been thinking about my grandmother's recipes. Do you think this tea of yours, would go with any of them? Perhaps a scone or a Victoria sponge? You're putting me in mind of those distant school days, seeing the pupils enjoying a brew. I remember serving tea to parents during the parents' evening. It's always been a staple of British social life, hasn't it? Indeed, it’s a nice little ritual. Reminds us of old times. I suppose it's a way of slowing down a bit, enjoy the simplicity of things. Absolutely, slowing down seems to be the key these days, doesn’t it? Off we go so quick these days. Someone should make a book about the art of making a good cup of tea. I'm sure someone has, actually. Now that's an idea for a project. You’re always full of ideas, aren’t you? Though, I might be more interested in reading about it than writing it, really [chuckles]. Indeed, slowing down allows one to appreciate the little details, perhaps even more than the process itself. There’s something soothing in watching the tea leaves unfurl in the hot water. That's so true. And the way it brings people together doesn’t hurt either. But it's not just about the tea itself, it's the act of making it, serving it. It’s time taken just to be together. That’s the whole point, isn’t it? It's not just about the drink but the company and the pause in the day. Just couple of years ago, we were all so busy, living separate lives. Now, we meet here often and it’s been a lifesaver. It's been a blessing, really. No one’s had to deal with these new technologies or whatnot. It’s just real, proper conversation. Though, I do miss seeing the children around... We can wish for those days again. But the children themselves, aren’t they gone and moved on to new things?

Who knew we'd all end up educating others in our careers? To think we met back in uni studying history together. That sounds familiar. It's funny, doesn't it? We're all here now, from different walks of life but now, all linked through our various educational roles. And isn't it lovely? But speaking of education, have you heard about the new regulations for CRB checks? It's causing quite a stir in our sector. Oh yes, I've heard about it. It's a bit contentious, isn't it? They say it's to protect the children but it feels a bit...overreaching sometimes. I hear ya. I've just been dealing with it in my role as well. Everyone's always saying we need less bureaucracy in our lives but then they create more complicated rules that just cloud the issue. Speaking of rules, I had an interesting incident with one of my trainees recently. They asked if they could take time off for a visit to the hospital for a circumcision procedure. A circumcision? That's not something that comes up often in our HR guidelines, is it? Not in the training manuals but it should be assumed under the umbrella of religious observance and/or medical grounds. It's surprising what can come up at work. But it must have been a bit of a shock to the trainee, I'd imagine. Exactly, they were really nervous about asking for time off for it, and they didn't want to 'inform' me of why. But it proves the point about the need for understanding and inclusivity, doesn't it? Definitely. But the really surprising thing is that the company's guidelines don't even touch on religious observation. Anyway, enough about work. How about another glass of wine? This Harvest is lovely. Please, but mind the driving afterwards. Indeed. It might be a good idea to consider staying over – there are plenty of nice hotels around. True, but what if we stuck closer to home? After all, we're here with family. You're right. Why not have a nice, quiet night in and perhaps head to our local pub tomorrow? I swear the food there is worth a little detour. A good plan. But what if we also invite some other friends over? I heard about some interesting art projects happening in London and maybe they could share some insights over dinner.

Hey, I'm so glad you're back! How was your holiday? I missed you so much these past two weeks. Thanks, it was great! I got some well-deserved rest. Want to grab breakfast in the kitchen? I've just made some toast, and I found this new avocado spread which I just have to try. Sounds amazing! Let’s get into the kitchen, I’m starving. So how was your time without me? Was it peaceful in our shared kingdom? Well, it was quiet at least. But I missed having you around. You're always making sure we eat something healthy. Speaking of, would you like to make some plans for the weekend? Perhaps a movie night or try out that new restaurant that just opened? Yeah, that sounds perfect. I'd love to go check out that new restaurant. What do you think about Sunday evening? That works for me. Shall we meet for dinner there or maybe watch a film or a sports match before heading out? I’m catching up on football and there’s a match on Sunday night. That could be fun too. I haven’t watched any football lately. If the weather’s good, we can even have a small picnic in the backyard before dinner. That’s a fab idea. The forecast says it’ll be sunny. Speaking of sunny, how was your therapy in practice during the holidays? Was it hectic? It was hectic but rewarding. I saw some really interesting cases during that time. That’s great to hear. You’re doing such important work. Did anything challenge or impress you during your sessions? More than usual, actually. I had a case of a young woman who’s really improving with our sessions. It’s so rewarding to see her confidence building. That’s beautiful to hear. While you were dealing with all that, I was dealing with my own stuff. I managed to meet up with a few old friends from uni but also had to deal with an ex calling out of the blue. That sounds tough. How did you handle it? It was a bit of a mixed bag to be honest. We’re just in different places now. I’m trying to move on. I did have a laugh with some of the friends though. We talked about wanting to start a book club. Maybe we can do that together?

Hey, I was thinking about Sarah again today. You know, things have been so tough for her these past months. Yes, it's been a real challenge for the whole family. I've spoken to John a few times and he sounded almost overwhelmed but managing, as best as he can. It's just so unfair isn't it? She's got young kids, her career blossoming, and then this blow. True. Life can be cruel at times. But it's amazing how she remains so upbeat and keeps supporting those around her, despite everything. That's her, she's always been such a strong and supportive person. I remember when she was going through her PhD, she did two years of study with a toddler in tow. I never knew how she did it. Yeah, she's got an incredible resilience. And the way she's handling everything now, advocating for herself, learning about treatment options—it's inspiring. It also shows how we need better health systems for these situations, you know? Absolutely. And it’s made me realize how unprepared we are as a society. But that aside, have you noticed there are more houses for sale in our village these days? Oh yes! I did see that. I think it’s because of the town planning proposal that’s been floating around. It seems to have really unsettled a few people, making them want to sell up. Really? I had no idea. What's all that about? I thought it was just a proposal about maybe extending the green area around the village, but not plans for anything drastic. It's been a bit more than that. Apparently, the council is considering a small development project to the north of the village, but some people are worried it'll impact property values or the village character. Oh no, that could be disruptive, especially for the local businesses. Do you think our friends John and Sarah would be affected? It's possible if they own property and it falls within the development area. But changing the character of the village could also affect Sarah’s sense of peace and healing, if that impacts on her current support network and surroundings. You make a good point. A quiet, soothing environment is crucial for someone going through medical treatment. Exactly. And it’s not just about Sarah. It’s about the community and maintaining a village-like atmosphere where everyone feels they belong and have space to heal or work through challenges.

Alright, Sarah, what’s on your mind first? We've got some time today so let's spill some truth. What are some things you really don't enjoy doing in our roles here? Oh, there are quite a few things. I guess now that the semester’s started, I've been dealing with students' complaints more and it can be a bit draining. Yep, that sounds like it. I'm pretty sure it's the same for security. Just last week, we had a bunch of students arguing about room keeps coming through. Nothing particularly violent, just exhausting. Yeah, I hear you. It feels like every student thinks they've been wronged by the world or something. And sometimes it’s just a misunderstanding that’s taken too far. But as much as we try to resolve it, sometimes it’s like talking to a brick wall, isn’t it? Exactly! My point exactly. It feels like some just want someone to listen, but others just want to vent and never really hear the rational side of things. And it's funny because it's not usually the major issues - it's often the little things. Like, last Tuesday I had this argument about a missing microwave from the common room. Turns out, someone borrowed it without permission. Ha! Borrowing without permission is classic. But the worst is when it's things we can't change, like the food choices in the canteen or the noise from the sports facilities. The food is... serviceable at best, and the noise is just a constant in our lives, really. But you can't really argue about that much, can you? Nope. Plus, doesn’t help that we have to deal with it too. I mean, sometimes I wish food and entertainment options were better here. It’s hard when you’re surrounded by the same choices day in and day out. Oh, I feel that. The choice of food can be quite limited. And when you think about it, we're tasked with making this place feel like home for students but sometimes it feels like we’re dealing with the same routine that doesn’t change much year to year. True. I guess what bothers me most in general though, is when it feels like our efforts don’t matter. Like we try to address issues or make recommendations but nothing ever changes.

Ah, I bumped into so many Brits last year's summer holidays in Rome. It was like everywhere you turn, someone was speaking clearly South East English! I talked to this charming couple from Herne Bay who were on a package tour. They said it was the best and easiest way to visit Italy because all the details were taken care of. Oh, I remember those group tours. I never took part but my sister used to. She loved the minimal language hassle and seeing the famous spots. But, isn’t it funny how much we always end up finding each other when we’re abroad? Very funny indeed! And, speaking of meeting fellow Brits abroad, did you hear about Christmas markets in Antwerp? It’s supposedly magical. Yes, I have! My husband was there last year. He loved the atmosphere, though he struggled a bit with the Dutch language, poor soul. Hence, we’re planning a language evening at home so he can learn more. Learning languages, eh? My grandson used to be fascinated by these things. But now, all he seems to care about are those new video games. Aww, that cute! We’re actually planning on taking the children to some Christmas markets this December if we can find good ones. There’s something so special about the festivities. Yeah, and the food! Especially if we manage to find one with traditional English fare. It can be quite hard to keep them away from the German bratwurst though. Oh, but the silly prices can ruin it sometimes, can’t they? I remember we used to go to a market in London that had some overpriced burgers. Indeed! Speaking of overprices, ever heard of the prices for parking in London now? It’s just ridiculous. But the traffic, oh god, the traffic! Makes you want to keep just walking, if you ask me. True. Parks and Gardens are still so underrated by us Brits. We should all just get bikes or walking boots instead of sitting in traffic for hours. I used to love walking on the Brighton seafront. There’s something so calming about it. Though when I was younger, I preferred getting lost in the Dorset countryside on a caravan holiday. Oh, Dorset caravanning, fantastic! I’ve been meaning to go. Maybe this summer. You should! It’s a great way to spend time with family or really just anyone close.

Hey Mum, did you hear about that equality vote last year? Yeah, I did. It's something that will clearly impact Ireland a lot, isn't it? I guess so. Is it like our equality laws but just for Ireland? In a way, yes. It was about making sure everyone has equal rights and protections. So does that mean same-sex marriage can actually happen in Northern Ireland now? It should! There was an amendment that needed to be passed in the House of Commons. So it's not there yet then? I believe it's been delayed a bit. There's still a bit to go, but hopefully it will happen soon. Oh, that's a shame. It's 2019 and we're still discussing this? Yeah, sometimes change takes a while, especially in politically tense areas like Northern Ireland. It feels weird. We're talking about something as basic as love or as simple as not being treated differently because of this. I completely agree but it's also different in each country. Ireland has been more progressive on this issue while the UK has had its ups and downs. Do you think there's anything we can do to speed things up? Well, people can always vote for parties that support equal rights. And as a family in Britain, we can maybe support charities or write to MPs, but it might not help that much. Hmm, I wish there was a better way. Just keep talking about it, supporting gay friends, and if you're in politics later on, or join clubs that push for equality. Yeah, maybe. School should teach more about LGBTQ+ stuff. Absolutely, schools play a big role in educating and promoting understanding and equality. Speaking of school, my History teacher mentioned something about equality votes in our Equality and Diversity class. That’s great! Schools should definitely cover real-world issues like that. Yeah, it actually surprised me a bit because it's such a real issue and it’s relevant even now. It's all part of growing up and learning about these big societal changes, isn’t it? True. It makes me think about all the different ways people are different but should be equal anyway. Exactly. And that's what equality is all about – treating everyone fairly despite any differences. So, when I go back to school next year, maybe I'll make sure to talk about it more in class.

Ah, I was going over some of Grandpa's old tools the other day. You know the lathe he had? It was a beauty. I've been meaning to get it fixed up, but I've no idea how to use it. Oh now, the old lathe! That was before my time, but I've seen pictures. I bet it was something else, eh? Lathe tools, you mean? I remember Dad once gave me a lecture about how he used it for woodwork during the war. It’s amazing what people would craft in those times. Yes! Even made some of our furniture with it, I believe. He was quite skilled. He would sometimes work on it for hours in the shed. The scent of wood and machinery... it’s quite nostalgic. It's amazing how much you can make out of a simple lathe. Nowadays, we just throw things away when they’re broken, don’t we? That’s a useful skill to have. Someone should make a video tutorial! Maybe one day. I'm more worried about figuring out how to fix it myself. I’ve tried looking up some guides online, but all the terminology! 'Rear center bearing'? What on earth does that mean? It’s like another language, innit? I'd be glad to help show you, if you'd like. I could try to explain it in simpler terms, or we could even go and look at it together. That’d be nice of you, thanks! I’ve always wondered what makes that thing tick. You should really do that. We can make it a project for next week. Seems like the weather's looking alright, so a few hours in the shed won’t be a bad thing. Absolutely. Plus, working on something like that can be quite therapeutic. True, very true. You know, it's things like this that remind me how much I miss my parents. I wish I’d paid more attention to these sorts of things when they were around. Oh, indeed, we should learn from them more often. This reminds me of the time Granny used to almost pop the hamster in the microwave thinking it was just a little bowl! Oh no, not again! That story makes our family gatherings. “And then Grandma went to grab a bowl for the hamster...!” I still can't believe she thought that was the right appliance.

Ah, I had a fascinating day today at work, Alan's passport was ready but today's task was transcribing some old letters. They were from Charles Dickens! I talked about it with the tea lady down in the canteen. That must have been a fun day! I had a meeting today with one of our customers and they were surprised to learn about the new rule on charging for plastic bags. It's funny how some things can ruin a lovely shopping experience. And here I am, coming from sorting out a whole different kind of routine at my school. But I must say, plastic bags are a real issue. Remember when we used just the old paper ones? But I do get it. Sentimentally, I think a bit of change was due. Exactly, but it's the unexpected changes that catch us off guard. Hence my fascination with those old letters. Speaking of which, I came across this archaic looking address and it read "27 Up-hill Dropofdogs, Woundsworth". I had to look it up because it sounded far too quirky! That would be this side of England, quite certainly. I remember when I was a kid, my mum would always paint this absurd picture for us about how things used to be: "We had to walk up to shops to buy things, and we used coins that were worth something!" A walk up to the shops sounded rather familiar growing up. But, regarding serious matters, did you guys see today's news about the banks? Another scandal with the mortgages? Yes! I actually had to transcribe that too. The figures are quite staggering, but then I remembered thinking if one’s house price falling the way some are, who would win or lose in the end? It’s a complex world now with all these mortgages and debt. But at least we don’t deal with that kind of problem personally, right? While I was dealing with the customer today, I had to explain the updated banking rules. Indeed, that’s some relief. Though in these times of economic uncertainty, it’s always something. But let’s move on to something light. Did anyone see last night’s episode of that cryptic crossword show? It was about those mirror-writers and almost sounded like folklore. Mirror-writing! Yes! Did you know, Charles Dickens was one of them? No, I didn’t.

Alright, have you two fellows thought about how playing with toys like Lego and Minecraft actually helps with your creativity and problem-solving skills? Yes, we've built some really cool things! Like, we created an entire city in Minecraft and had to make sure everyone had houses and food. And with Lego, we've made this big castle and figured out how to build it so it doesn't fall down. Yeah! And we've also been trying to learn how to write our own stories in Minecraft, like what's happening in our world. That's great! You're learning how to create your own narratives and bring those worlds to life through imagination. It's wonderful that you're enjoying it so much. But, um, when we play, it feels good because we get to control things. Minecraft and Lego let us build and change things whenever we want. That's true! Having control over your play can be really rewarding. However, I wonder if balancing playtime with reading can also help make our imaginations even more vivid, right? What do you think about that? Like, if we mixed building in Minecraft with reading about knights or castles, maybe we could get more ideas? Yeah, and when we read stories, doesn't it sometimes feel like it's like building things too? We have to build the world and the characters in our minds. Exactly! Reading does that same thing. It helps create worlds and characters in your mind. The fun thing is, each time you read or imagine something new, you're building that skill of creating worlds in your mind, which can actually help a lot when you're playing with these toys too. It might even inspire new things to build or create. So, like, if we spend a bit of our playtime reading, it doesn't mean we have to stop playing with Legos or Minecraft. We can do both. Absolutely. The idea is to balance. If we spend some time reading about different worlds and things, we might find ourselves wanting to build those worlds in Minecraft or with Legos. It could actually make your playtime even more exciting. So, maybe one day we could build something from a book we read? What a fantastic idea! You could build a model of Hogwarts from Harry Potter, or maybe a pirate ship if you read a book about that.

Ah, good morning everyone! Lovely to see you all. How have you been today? Oh, good morning! It's been a bit chaotic but manageable. How about you, Auntie? What have you been up to? Morning! I’ve been stuck on questions for this exam preparation so far . I hope my day gets better. Well, let's sit down and make sure it does, shall we? I’ve got plenty of coffee and some lovely cakes. You always spoil us, Auntie. Yes, thanks for setting this up again. Your cakes are delicious, by the way. Oh, that just makes my day. So, what shall we discuss first? You two were on that recent holiday together - tell me all about it. And Sarah, your exam sounds stressful. How's the revision going? Well, we had an amazing time in Cornwall, it was just what we needed. And it was funny seeing you all so relaxed and enjoying yourselves too. I hope you took plenty of time for a break. We certainly did, it was lovely to see everyone together. And I’m sure the fun stories will keep coming while the cakes keep going. Do tell, stories are always welcome. I could use a break from my exams for a few minutes. Oh, I remember, we all went to this beautiful beach in St Ives. And then John tried to make sandcastles and they all kept tumbling down. But it didn't stop him, did it? He just went at it again and again. Kids never give up. That's so great to hear. More stories, please! And of course, we had plenty of fun dinnertime arguments about football. Your cousin even had us play Scrabble for once. That was a surprise but we enjoyed it. You sure did. You both did great at Scrabble, though Sarah was more fierce than I expected. I always take Scrabble seriously. It’s one of the few times I get to use my Latin vocabulary. Did anyone have any mishaps or adventures on the trip? Well, Sarah almost got taken out by a wave at that one beach. She still has sand in her hair. But she was funny and didn’t let it ruin her day. I fell into a bog trying to take a shortcut through the hike trail but that ended well... when you took a photo to scare me into taking a better path.

Hey guys, did you hear about James getting voted first school's prefect? I never thought he'd make it. Yeah, I was pretty surprised too. But he's always been well-liked, right? Absolutely. I think his personality really won people over. Plus, his leadership skills have been on show this year. Like when he took part in the history project? I remember he pretty much led that team to victory at the regional competition. Oh, that was impressive! I thought it was a close call though when he was up against Oliver in the election, you know? True, Oliver's pretty popular too. He's just very different from James in approach. But let's not dig up past arguments. Who's up for planning our summer holiday destinations? Sure, but how about we grab some lunch first? Sure, I'd love to go to Subway. Ronan, your thoughts? Count me in! And let's grab a few sandwiches to go so we can play that new card game I brought later. Great idea! By the way, have you guys watched any good shows lately? I've been binge-watching 'The Boys'. It's really intense, but good. I saw the first couple of episodes. It's certainly violent, but the humor works really well with it. Yeah, I've been meaning to catch up. What about any good movies? Did you guys see 'Tenet'? Nah, but I heard it's mind-bending. Maybe we can watch it over the holidays. That sounds good. It'd be fun to do something as a group. Maybe even have a movie marathon day or something? That could be real fun. Let's keep it in mind. If we're going to marathon, can we include 'Money Heist'? That series is really addictive. You got that right. I was on edge after every episode. Speaking of tense topics, did you guys see the news about those military drone strikes? Yeah, it's really complicated. I had a teacher lecture about international politics and it definitely made me see the other side. Honestly, I'm just getting more confused. There's so much information and everyone seems to have a different view. Maybe we should talk to Ms. Lee? She's our history teacher and has a lot to say on the matter. Good idea. She always helps to clarify things. Okay, so let's catch up with her about that soon.

Hey, I just heard that Mr. Davies is teaching our physics class. I hope he's as cool as they say. Oh, talked to someone who had him last year. They said he’s really good at explaining things, but can be quite strict if you don’t pay attention. Strict is fine with me if it means I learn. But have you heard his accent? It sounds a bit like he has a bit of a Cambridge twang. I wonder how he'll fit in with us. Yeah, I’ve noticed. It’s pretty strong, right? But we’re all from around here, so probably won’t phase many of us. I just hope he doesn’t confuse any of us by using too much university-level language. I’d actually like that. Means he’s challenging us. True, true. Another thing I heard - Ms. Patel, our form tutor, said we’re going to have English reading lessons? That sounds good, doesn’t it? I’d say so. I love reading, especially old classics. Maybe she’ll bring some interesting books and we can discuss them. Exactly! I just hope she doesn’t bring the ones we already had in previous years. I think it would be interesting if we got to pick some books ourselves. That would be great. Maybe she can set up a reading list and we can vote for our favorites. Can you imagine? It’d make the lessons so much better. Totally. Plus, doesn’t Ms. Patel have a pretty good sense of humor? Yeah, she always makes jokes in class and makes everyone laugh. But the thing is, she’s surprisingly good at keeping us in line when we start to get too rowdy. I really respect her for that. Yeah, she’s one of those teachers who really understands us kids. Speaking of teachers, did you see that we might get a new teacher in our next year? I heard it’s for our History class. Yeah, word is it’s a new guy. Hopefully, he’s not like Mrs. Gaston who used to teach us. That class was so boring. Oh, that’s just too bad. I hope they put someone more engaging in. I heard our History class is going to focus more on modern events this year. That would be interesting. But it won’t help if the teacher makes it dry.

Right, so who's seen any of the latest travel vlogs online? I discovered this really cool one about Transylvania. It was fascinating how they portrayed the place, talked about old castles, and of course, the legends of Dracula. Actually, the weekend, I was kind of stuck on questions because some of my baking conversations were involved and one of them mentioned a rare, traditional type of "vampire" cake they saw while visiting there. But actually, I've always wanted to travel to Transylvania and set up my own bakery there. Oh, we could be opening up a theme bakery there – serving up "Dracula's delicious delights". It'd be a hit in London too. Might just need to learn a bit more about the local flavors and add some of our own twist. I've got to say, while living in Australia, you guys have a plethora of unique expressions and sayings that sometimes confuse us. Do you have any in English that are particularly Australian that you could share? It'd be funny to hear. Yeah, there are a few. Like, it's pretty common to hear people use "g'day" as a greeting, and "mate" as a term of friendly endearment. Also, they might say "fair dinkum" to indicate something is really true, or "no worries" to mean "it's okay" or "don't worry". Oh, and don't forget "thongs" – they mean flip flops or sandals here, but they might not mean that in some places! But it's not just about the slang. Their phrasing can be quite different, too. I've heard them use "have a listen" when we'd say "listen to this" or "see a show" instead of "watch a show." Right! And then there's the way they sometimes confront something insincere or overly enthusiastic with a simple "Aw, come on." Haha, exactly. I was told once that when Australians are surprised or in disbelief, they might say "Well, I'll be..." Oh, and Australian food influences are quite versatile too! Again, coming from the baking side, there are almost as many cultural influences in Australian desserts as there are ciders or beers. I recently tried making a lamington. It's amazing how different each one can be! I've made lamingtons before and they were delicious. But I suppose we could really dive deep into Australian culture and food any time. Absolutely!

Hey everyone, did you hear about that new song by Florence + The Machine? It's so catchy and it really speaks to me about how music can transport you to another world. Is that like in Alice in Wonderland? Yeah, kind of! Going down the rabbit hole and then finding yourself in a totally different place! Exactly! And speaking of Wonderland, have we settled on a theme for Emma's party? Can it be Alice in Wonderland? I want to wear a costume and have a tea party! And we should definitely have music that goes with it. Maybe some of those classical pieces too. That sounds like a great idea. How about we have a playlist going on in the background? And we could even include a few of those songs from the movie. Yeah! And also, can we have music playing during the photos? Maybe we can have a little photo booth with funny props. And not just any music or photos, we should really capture the moment with this aerial hoop and maybe some muddy obstacle course shots. The photographs alone would be the best family album. Who knows, maybe we could make a little photo book or picture frame montage for the party. And can we swear , just a tiny bit? I love how Alice can always get herself silly and talk in riddles. Well, we should probably keep it "PG" for now but certainly we can have fun with language. Speaking of language, how about this food and drink menu? Should we do all English classics or mix it up with some other stuff too? As much as I love fish and chips, I think a little variety keeps things interesting. How about we do a couple of traditional English dishes but also include some family favorites? Can we have a cake too? With icing and everything? And party hats of course! I'm sure we can arrange all of that and make today’s plans for the party. But let’s make sure we capture everything we talked about so we don’t forget anything. And can we turn it into a family project? We can all help with music, food, and pictures. Absolutely! That way everything feels cooperative and everyone can be proud of the party. I think that will be great. It's not just a party; it’s a family event.

Right lads and lasses, I'm pretty happy with's pizza. Lookin' like we've got enough for everyone too. It's always a mission to find a place that does a good pizza. I really like this place though. Yeah, I heard rumors there was a tiny place downtown near the school that does them even better. Maybe we can get Speaker_5 to take us there sometime? Oh, I'd love to. They said it uses all local ingredients too! That's brilliant. You kids need to get some experience with good food before you lazy lot have to cook yourselves! Haha, you're getting ahead of yourself there, mate. Speaking of food, have you seen the new spot that opened near the railways? They've got all sorts of interesting sandwiches. I'd like to check it out. Maybe we could even do a little food review? What do you guys think? Now there's an idea! We could even tweet some photos or even do a little video. I don't know, granddad, do you think we can do that? It's worth trying. Good PR for the place and it's a bit of fun for us, right? Well, technology's for all ages, innit? I'd take some advice from one of you young 'uns before we embarrass ourselves. They say the key to good content is relatability. So, maybe highlight how it's like your community and things that people here would find interesting. Just like finding good deals at shops? I saw a tweet about half-price hair things the other day. Seems like the young people are always spotting a good deal, isn't it? Yeah, and it's fun sharing it online. It feels like you're part of something bigger and it's always good to see a favorite spot get some love. It’s all about the pressure points, innit? No one’s going to want to listen to a foodie trying to promote something if it’s not truly special. True, but with real passion and authenticity, it can show through. And it’s good for those kids to learn about storytelling and marketing at young age. Storytelling and marketing? You lot talk like you're running the BBC! Haha, funny thinking back, but that's just part of being in school and stuff now. You're right, grandpa.

Ah, I'm losing to Dad again at this Chinese chess. Dad, why do you always know these strategies so well? You've never told me about most of these moves before. I'm sure you've just understood something new or it just comes naturally to you now, Dad – you always have a way of finding new angles in games and life. But, actually, I have some access to materials that might help us get some of these strategies better, especially the more complex ones. Oh, that sounds like a plan. Are you talking about something online or in print? I used to think about getting into more strategy games when I was younger, but never quite got the hang of it beyond some basic notions. Might just be down to experience, but I bet having someone read up on strategies while we play could actually make us better. Speaking of, morning has been a bit of a struggle here. I had forgotten how the weather affects your daily routine when you spend time in the countryside. And you're always on about this. You know, for all the talk about relying on tech or planning, sometimes the weather still dictates a lot of it. It's certainly been affecting my morning routine – if it’s too sunny or too cold, it affects when and how I can shower and get dressed. Speaking of which, I saw there's an interesting weather pattern predicted for the South of England later this week. Maybe the nice weather will even take us back into the garden more often. Speaking of which, in my garden, I've got some berries ready for the picking and they might go well with any breakfast we can come up with. You and the berries. That reminds me, we could use some berries on our toast if it’s sunny during breakfast the next few days. Though the garden's looking a bit ragged since we've not had much time to tend it lately. You were saying something about skills or strategies, though? Right, back to Chinese chess. From what I know, a key is not just memorizing moves but understanding the strategy behind common patterns or setups. I can try to find some bookmarks or guides in my laptop. That would be great. I mean, I've always found games like this are as much about understanding the culture and history behind them as the moves.

Ah, I'm so glad we could meet up here in Tarnów. I've been meaning to catch up for ages. How are things going with you being a full-time teacher now? It’s good! I really enjoy it. Still getting used to the system, though. The students here are very dedicated. Yeah, I'd imagine. I've taught a few students privately, just part-time. Not as settled, of course, as you with your full-time job. Speaking of teaching, have you heard about the new regulations in education? I think it's supposed to affect student loans and such. Honestly, I haven’t really been following it. Is it any good news? Honestly, no. They’re planning to raise the interest rate on student loans again. Terrible timing, right? Definitely not. Makes me grateful for my graduate status, yet very concerned for the younger generations. And considering I’m pretty much on a fixed income now... it’s worrying for the future. Yeah. Now that I'm teaching this side of the pond, it’s weird to think about how students over here don't have to deal with that kind of financial burden while studying. It’s a substantial difference, certainly. I also really worry about the pension situation. Have you seen the estimates? It’s like they keep pushing the retirement age further and further back. Oh, I know. My grandmother was telling me that she had to work until 70 to achieve full pension and that was just a few years ago. How they expect people to live on the pension they do get until 80 or 90 is beyond me. Exactly! And consider career changes or side hustles, which are pushed so much these days, they often don’t come with the pension scheme benefits. It’s quite unnerving, to be honest. Makes you question everything about planning for the future. Indeed. It’s one reason I thought of potentially working abroad – more opportunities, some places with better benefits... though of course, it's not without its challenges, as I’m sure you know better than me. Definitely. I’ve been thinking about it too. Did you have a look at any countries in particular? Spain caught my eye – relatively straightforward to get settled if you know the language. Also, the lifestyle suits me. But I’d love your insights, you’ve been doing this more recently.

Hey mate, great to see you again! How was your year? I heard you got into the accelerated GCSE maths program. It was alright, thanks for asking! Yeah, maths is actually getting quite challenging, but I'm managing now. What about you? How's human sciences going? It's really interesting! I love how it combines social science and humanities topics. It links pretty well with what we've been learning about race relations, and I'm really enjoying it. That's cool! You know, alongside this, I've been thinking about my future university options. I'm pretty sure I want to study human sciences as well, but I need to make sure I have a back-up in case anything goes wrong. Yeah, that’s smart planning. You might also want to look at the modules they offer. Some universities might have stronger programs in individual components of human sciences you’re interested in, like sociology or anthropology. That makes sense! Do you have any advice on how to prepare? Like, what are they looking for in applicants? Well, from what I’ve gathered, they really value a broad interest in the social sciences and humanities. So showing that through your A-levels is good, but extra-curricular activities that demonstrate your passion can give you an edge. Like if you’re really into history, perhaps doing work experience or volunteer work related to that could help. That’s really helpful. I’ve been thinking of doing some volunteer work at a local museum or something. Exactly! That'd be perfect. Shows initiative and interest. Also, don’t underestimate the importance of writing a good personal statement. Yeah, my tutor mentioned that. It's kind of daunting, thinking about how to express everything in the right way. No worries, just start by thinking of the projects or subjects you’ve enjoyed most and why. If you think about it, we can even meet up and brainstorm some ideas together. That would be great! Thanks. Speaking of brainstorming, did you ever plan on playing rugby at a higher level after university? I’ve been thinking about joining a team at uni if there’s one. Oh definitely! I've played all my life and would love to continue. Some universities have great clubs and even compete in national leagues. I've almost gone over the course list for all the uni's I’m considering to see if they’ve got good rugby programs.

Ah, I've been reading about this new policy the government's trying to push through. It's all quite complex, but essentially it will increase taxes for people like me who have a certain level of income. Is that the policy that the opposition and some grassroots organizations are heavily criticizing? I heard there were large protests against it last month and that it could disproportionately hit those in the lower-middle class. That's the one, actually. Now, you graduated in politics and languages, so how do you think this policy will affect people like me? Well, it's a bit concerning. The rhetoric from the supporters of the policy is that it's necessary to fund various social services and infrastructure projects. However, critics argue that those funds could be raised more sustainably through other means, like closing tax loopholes or increasing corporate taxes. That's interesting. I never realized that there were various ways to do this. But looking at my own situation, how would an increase in tax affect me? It would depend on the specifics of the policy, but typically, any increase or new bracket added to the tax system would reduce your disposable income. It might not seem like much at first, but over time it could limit your ability to save or invest. And while the government says benefits will offset the impact, that’s often not the case for people who, like you, already have modest savings and a manageable yet respectable income. I see. A bit like how, when I was an accountant, we'd sometimes see clients who were suddenly hit with unexpected tax liabilities and they'd have to adjust their budgeting significantly. Exactly. It's the same principle. The government often talks about adjusting tax brackets or rates to make the system more "fair" or to "reduce the gap between rich and poor". More often than not, it's just added complexity. Do you think our current tax system is fair? It’s complicated. Some argue that our progressive system—where you pay more tax as your income increases—is fairer than regressive systems where everyone pays the same proportion of their income. However, there’s a lot of unease about how multi-national corporations or those with certain income sources can so easily avoid paying their fair share through various legal loopholes and offshore accounts. I could never understand that.

Hey, I'm so stressed out with work at the moment. We have a big project coming up and I'm having to juggle a lot of different tasks at once. Oh, that sounds tough. What kind of project are you on? It’s kind of a rebranding project for one of our clients. We’re doing everything from creating new branding materials to redesigning their website and overseeing the launch of a new campaign. And to be honest, I’m really unsure if everything is set for success. Wow, that does sound like a lot. I once managed a large-scale exam day at school. It was always chaotic, but we just had to make sure everything was perfect. Seems similar to what you’re dealing with. How is your team handling it? So far, okay I guess. They’re all working well together, but I have to ensure they all understand the bigger picture and the project's timeline. We’re looking for a launch within the next 6 weeks, so time is of the essence. And honestly, I’m worried about the possible financial constraints for the client. That adds an extra layer of complexity doesn’t it? I remember having to deal with budget constraints when I worked at school - always trying to make do with what we had while still delivering everything needed. Exactly! It feels like the perfect storm sometimes. On top of all that, we’ve had some disagreements over design decisions. The client is very particular about the aesthetics, and it seems like my team can’t quite understand what they want. I can sympathize. When you deal with clients, it’s like you’re constantly trying to read between the lines and see things the way they do. Sometimes it feels like they’re speaking a whole different language! It definitely does! How did you handle these kinds of situations at the school? I feel like I could learn from your experience. For me, it was about making sure I had clarity on the technical aspects - so I knew exactly what we could and couldn’t do. Then, I’d do my best to translate that into terms that were easy for the rest of the team to understand. If there were issues that couldn’t be solved immediately, I’d always try to find a compromise or work around. It’s all about problem-solving and being flexible.

Ah, I'm losing my touch with modern tech, innit? I was trying to learn how to use this new iPhone, but it feels like it's speaking a completely different language. Can you teach me some basic stuff? Of course! I'll show you. Which specific features do you want to learn? Or maybe I could help, as I have some knowledge about them. Although, I have to admit, I'm more of a Google Fi and MacBook person. Yeah, well, most people from down here prefer their iPhones, don't you find? Indeed, dear. I used to be quite the tech geek back in the day. But now, with my work as a biomedical scientist in retirement, my main digital involvement is probably just making sure the recycling goes in the correct bin and that kind of thing. Well, you're creative with how you use technology then. Recycling and bin sorting is good for the planet. How about showing us some old photos on that new device? That sounds like a great idea! Yeah, let's see if we can get some good ol' photos on there. I'm sure we have some hilarious ones from when you all tried that new recipe that totally failed, right? Ah, That was a disaster. The whole kitchen seemed to hate the concept of vegan meatballs. Alright, I'm all for showing embarrassing family photos. That should be good for a laugh. Or a few. Here we go, let's see. Oh, I found some! These are from your 50th! You, blurred out, trying to blow the candles out while the kids are all chasing confetti everywhere. Oh, god, and there you are, Chief! Strapped in a party hat that's about to sit on your head at any moment. I've seen that photo before! It’s legendary! Here’s one of all of us at the beach, 2015. Again, me with the party hat. And Speak, you're wearing the silliest sunglasses I’ve ever seen. Ah, those things were the in-vogue item at the time, I suppose. Sure, they were, but this one time...I...we all wore... ...banana costumes at the beach. Oh, for the love of... We did actually do that, didn't we? Yes! That was for charity, wasn’t it? But damn, what were we thinking? Hey, it raised lots of money! Plus, it’s memories we’ll cherish forever, won’t we?

Hey, I'm so glad we could catch up without the kids this time. How's the new school year been treating you so far? Oh, it's been really well. The children are all enjoying their new classes and teachers. Still, now and then, you get those kind of days where questions are flying left and right and you need a coffee before the end of the morning. I know that feeling. Just had a particularly grueling lesson with some of my oldest students who wanted to discuss verbs. You'd think they'd get it by now, but, you know, there's always a question they haven't thought of before. Absolutely. And let’s not even start on trying to get them to participate in speaking exercises. Some of them need a bit of coaxing. On that note, did either of you go to the TEFL conference last month? I was thinking of going but my work schedule ended up being pretty chaotic. Actually, yeah, I went. It was really helpful, especially the session on progressive teaching methods. Oh, that sounds interesting. I’m always looking for new techniques to keep my classes fresh. I especially struggle with balancing teaching grammar with the need to make classes more interactive and engaging. Do you have any tips? One thing that really stood out for me was integrating more game-like activities into the lesson plans. There’s this really good workshop on Kahoot! for language learning that they offered. It’s amazing how much it can help in terms of participation and retention. Plus, doesn’t feel as stuffy as the usual grammar exercises. Oh, that sounds intriguing. I’ve heard of Kahoot! but never thought of using it in teaching contexts. I’ve been trying to use more real-life scenarios for my adults, but it can be tough sometimes. Exactly! Real-life scenarios are great, but sometimes you need a break from the usual routine to keep everyone engaged. With adults, especially, it’s harder because they often don’t want to feel like they’re back in school. But these new technologies can often bridge that gap. And it doesn’t overwhelm if you’re not too tech-savvy? No, actually. Kahoot! is pretty user-friendly. It’s like any other quiz tool, but with the fun game aspect included. They even offer templates for language learning questions, so it cuts down on your prep time a bit.

Ah, I'm so glad we could take this trip together. It's been ages. You know, I've been feeling so stagnant after leaving my job, and this little adventure has really lifted my spirits. You're right though, fitness is really important for our health. I must admit, after a couple of weeks of driving and exploring, I've started missing the gym and my daily routines. I completely understand. It's healthy to keep active, especially with our age. Now, you never told me what happened with your job. Was it difficult adjusting to not working? It was. You know, it's funny, people assume being unemployed means lazy or not doing much. But for me, it's been a very emotionally draining time. I've struggled to find new purpose and even activities to keep me busy. It's not the same as working, even part-time. And the transition from full-time to part-time and then semi-retired... it's a bit hard to adjust. I didn't know you were in such a tough spot. That must be really challenging. You're so strong to admit it, though. Thanks. I guess it's part of me learning to be more open. It's not something people usually talk about openly, especially in our society with the bias against unemployment. Well, it takes courage to talk about it. Especially if we consider the stigma around mental health and unemployment. It can lead to depression and anxiety for many people. Exactly! But I'm trying to turn it into a new chapter, you know? I started doing some freelance TEFL, and it’s been rewarding. I feel like I'm still using my skills and talents. That’s great to hear! I'm really proud of you for that. And you're still doing what you're passionate about, which is important. Yeah, I just wish I could do it full-time. The pay is unpredictable and it's hard to find regular clients. But at least it gives me something to look forward to and it keeps me interacting with people, which is also important. It might be worth looking into some online platforms that match teachers with students. I've used a few for my own teaching and it’s worked out quite well. That’s a great idea! Maybe I'll look into that.

Ah, good morning! I was thinking we could possibly move on from the history discussions today. I found an interesting piece about gerontology which struck me as insightful. What are your thoughts on the current trends in life expectancy? Good morning! I’m all ears. I’ve been reading up on some aspects of gerontology myself because my aunt was diagnosed with a rare age-related condition a while ago. It really made me think about our own ageing process. Life expectancy has increased significantly over the past century, and it’s mind-boggling how medical advances have contributed to this. That’s fascinating, yes. I was reading about telomeres the other day, how they’re linked to cell ageing. It’s a field of study that’s trying to understand why some people live longer than others. But in the broader context, advances in medicine, better nutrition, lifestyle changes... all these have contributed to extending human lifespan. I didn’t know about telomeres. It’s remarkable how cells work. But then, when you think about anti-ageing products and potential myths surrounding them, it’s quite concerning what people might expose themselves to or hope for. Oh, absolutely. There’s so much pseudoscience out there promising miracle cures or youth. It’s kind of like looking for the 'Fountain of Youth' in a bottle. While there are genuinely helpful things to stay physically and mentally fit, the key seems to be a holistic approach: good diet, exercise, mental stimulation, perhaps avoiding certain pollutants. True, and even as someone who’s not professionally working, I’ve noticed a focus on Omega 3 and some other nutrients when caring for my toddler. Healthy habits seem important from the start, I think. Absolutely. And while we’re on the topic of health and aging, have you considered or ever done any of those anti-ageing treatments? I just find the whole industry a bit... contested. No, to be honest, I personally think they are more for the well-to-do who perhaps feel pressured by societal expectations of aging. But in my situation, my focus is on nurturing a healthy, happy child – I suppose that’s the best form of 'anti-aging' for me right now. I agree, indeed, focusing on the current and future wellbeing is probably the most sensible approach. It’s good to have you around, by the way. Even though you’re not working right now, you’re contributing so much.

Everybody, I'm so glad we could all meet up like this. It feels like ages since we've done anything together. How are you all doing? Right, really well, thanks for asking. I’ve been, shall we say, adjusting to life back in the UK now that the pandemic has finally started to calm down. But honestly, it feels great to see everyone again. Yeah, me too. It’s been ages since we’ve all sat down together with nothing else to focus on but each other. Speaking of, has anyone seen the new Sainsbury’s voucher book that just came in today's post? Oh, let me show you then. Yeah, it has some great deals in here. Like a 30% off everything in the garden section. Ooh, that would be useful! I’ve been meaning to look at some new plant pots for the garden. I spotted a really nice fruit tree deal too. Anyone fancy a new apple tree? Speaking of the garden, how about we get the new baby’s chair over there? It hasn’t been put out on the patio yet. Ah, the baby . How is she or he settling in? I heard it’s been quite an adjustment for all of you. Oh, it’s all a bit chaotic at the moment, but we’re managing. It’s actually been kind of lovely. The little one loves the garden, less so the new chickens, though. They’re a bit too noisy. Chooks, eh? Yeah, they’ve had us up at 4 am with their insistent early morning cock-a-doodle-do. You know, after all the… …difficulties we’ve had for the past few years, just hearing about all these little everyday joys feels really nice. 100% with you there. Did anyone else catch that referendum debate on the news last night? No. I was out running errands plus had to get the new sofa cushions covered. For when the chooks get too close to the patio. You know, I was really worried about the outcome. But honestly? It just brought everything into perspective for me. I’d rather focus on the little things, like these restaurant vouchers, how’s everyone with that? We can at least go out for a meal together, grab some coffee. Enjoy ourselves, without thinking about politics too much. We can use the vouchers at that new Italian place in town, right?

Ah, I'm so glad we could take a break from everything this afternoon. Got a bit of a stressful week at work, what about you? Yeah, it's been crazy! Made my first big client pitch at the agency yesterday and I'm still just trying to process it all. But hey, on the bright side, it’s starting to feel a bit more like my Christmas vibes are getting closer, don’t you think? Oh, absolutely! Now that we’re getting into December, everything is buzzing with festive energy. I even heard our neighbours are putting up their Christmas tree this weekend. Do we know when you’ll be meeting up with your boyfriend’s family for Christmas? We have plans for the 24th, just like last year. His parents are hosting the dinner, and we’re probably going to a movie earlier in the day. What are your plans? You’ll be joining us again? I hope so! Last year was so much fun, and your mum made such a fantastic dinner. Anyway, shall we actually start on our own preparations? It’s not so far off anymore. Yeah! But first, I’m really hoping I can get my nails done beforehand. Have you ever tried those new gel manicures? I read they last ages, while the traditional ones seem to chip so easily. Oh, gel nails, right? I’ve had them a couple of times, they’re quite good, really. But for Christmas, perhaps classic red nails would be more festive? I’m a bit old-fashioned, really. But they never go out of style, and they’re so easy to do yourself if needed. True that, it’s the thought and the style that counts more than the longevity for this season, I suppose. Speaking of doing things ourselves, do you remember when we were younger and we’d help your mum make those little handmade decorations for the tree? Yes! And remember when we tried to make paper snowflakes that inevitably ended up as triangles and squares? Silly times! We actually still make some decorations ourselves now. There’s something really personal about having homemade ornaments on the tree. Definitely. It makes the tree feel more, I don’t know, ‘ours’ or something. It’s like telling a story of all the years leading up to this. Did you hear from your best friend in Leeds this year?

Hey, I'm so glad we could finally move in today. It feels great to finally unpack. Totally! I've been super excited about this move. Got all of our boxes unloaded though? Yeah, most of them, but there's still a bit of chaos. I just unpacked the kitchen and bathroom boxes. That must've been fun! I remember when we moved into your old place in Kent. I had to assemble the entire flat pack furniture for your kitchen... Haha, yeah. Well, this time we've got professionals to help with the assemble. Good thinking! I've been wanting to check in on the internet connection though, it's pretty slow. Do we have to sort that out ourselves or is there a service that the building provides? Ah, right. Yes, actually, the building should be providing its own service. But looking at the terms, it seems we need to get the connection sorted out through a provider ourselves. I've got some numbers to call. Great, or maybe I should just check the documents again. I don’t want to waste time calling if it's already sorted. You’re right, no point doing the legwork if it’s taken care of. Also, food. What's the plan for getting groceries? Ah, we need to sort that out, yes. There's Tesco and Sainsbury’s nearby but also some independent shops around the corner that I'm excited about. I'd prefer to check out the local ones. I've heard great things about that veg market just across the street. Right, I've seen it. We should grab some fresh veg for tonight’s dinner. Perfect idea. I noticed there's also a chicken shop nearby. Yes, that's Mrs. Higgins' and it's supposed to be the best in town. Can't wait to try her chicken. Also, we need to sort out rubbish collection. I’ve got the schedule stuck on the fridge door but I might want to double-check if the bins are already registered. Oh right. Let me check that while you're calling about the internet. Go ahead. Yeah. It's fine. We're registered under the building's account. But we need to get a small bin for inside the flat since this place doesn't come with one. True. We'll get that sorted out tomorrow. Also, have you seen the nursery next door?

Hey, long time no see. I'm so happy we could finally meet up after university. How have you been? You've been doing your thing out in the Midlands, right? Oh absolutely! It's been really great to get back into the swing of things after graduation. But yeah, I moved back to the Midlands for the placement. It's been a bit of an adjustment but I've been enjoying it. That's great to hear. I've been doing alright myself. Been stuck in Peterborough for work but it's keeps me busy. You know how it is - routine can get pretty interesting if you let it. Haha, I totally get that. I used to commute from here to Coventry for a while and it was ... an adventure. Right, but anyway, tell me more about your placement. What's been keeping you so busy? It's project coordination - mainly organizing case studies for a healthcare research program. So it's a lot of overseeing trials, similar to what I imagine your projects involve. Exactly! I'm a project co-ordinator for a different company now. I'm actually quite enjoying it though. Managing teams and making sure everything is running smoothly. There's a certain sense of achievement every time a project closes. That sounds great to hear. It really suits your organizational skills, doesn't it? Ah, thanks. I'm really focused on building my skills, especially after uni. I feel like in my field, having good organizational and interpersonal skills is essential. Agreed! So what's new on the socio-economic front? But it's probably rude to ask how that's doing? No, don't worry about it. Honestly, career-wise things are looking up, which in turn helps a bit with the socio-economic status. It’s not ideal yet, but it's definitely better than before. That's great to hear and honestly, it's great you're focusing on the upward trajectory. As for me, I'm still in the graduate ranger of unknown lands – I'm trying not to stress too much about it. Well, take your time. And remember, it's okay if it takes a bit of time to figure things out. That's comforting. I suppose almost all of us are just trying to figure out this whole adult life thing. Absolutely! Speaking of which, what are your future plans?

Ah, I'm so glad we could find a spot here. It's been ages. You know how busy Cambridge is around this time of year. Definitely, and I've missed these chats. There's something about discussing our work or the latest bands without distractions. Exactly. Going over the project notes or reviewing the last research findings, but without the academic pressure of a meeting. And the North East... I had a lecture on local dialects last semester for my PhD. It fascinated me how distinct they still are despite societal changes. Oh, absolutely. Like when someone says 'canny' or 'divvent' - I used to use those a lot when I lived near Sunderland, but my colleagues here sometimes get confused! LOL, same with 'bairn' instead of 'child'. I have to ensure I switch out those words when I write project reports or during lectures. True. But it's lovely to hear when someone understands those nuances. Did your lecture cover local music scenes from the North East as well? Yes, we touched upon that a bit. I was surprised to learn about the popularity of bands like The Futureheads and Maximo Park even outside the region. The Mod scene still seems to have an influence in some of the music. That's great, really. I've always been impressed by how local bands can keep distinct regional sounds while still reaching larger audiences. Like, I love how Arctic Monkeys kept their Sheffield accents and in-your-face style. For sure. It’s all about authenticity. I know what you mean. Now that's a topic... Fashion is the other thing I kind of miss about the North East - the whole 'Geordie shore' effect can be quite different from the Cambridge side of things, where it’s more a focus on mod. Haha, I'm sure there's a whole other story about that. Of course, fashion's also about cultural ins and outs everywhere but it's interesting to notice changing trends across different regions. Like, I was just looking through a new shopping store here in Cambridge - they've got loads of brands I've never seen before. In the North East, we tended to have more local designers or maybe a greater influence of vintage or retro. True, the thrift shopping scene is almost gone here. There's just not the same selection. Yeah, and that came with certain styles.

Hey Grandma, I've been thinking a lot about politics lately. Our teacher brought it up in class and it was really interesting. Oh, talked about politics in class, have you? Politics has been all over the news these days isn't it? Yeah, kind of overwhelming. Especially because some of my friends don’t really get it. But one thing I didn't understand was "Prorogation" and why everyone seemed so upset about it. Prorogation, yes.
