True – it’s a very changing of the seasons in more ways than one! I’ll be out of the country but hopefully I’ll still catch some of the festive atmosphere wherever I end up. Hopefully, all of you have a real break and not an e-break [chuckles]. Speaking of which, anyone managed to avoid all the holiday job postings or course applications we deal with, or is that just me? Well, I’ve been “making the most of it” by just reading all the Christmas-themed academic papers... that is, until I hear the word “paper” and reach for any type of paper I can find.

Ah, I'm losing my voice from screaming at the TV. We have to win today. The Northern lads never lose to the team from the Midlands when it comes to this competition. You're right though, you've got a strong team. Especially now that the new tactic seems to be paying off. Exactly! I'm expecting them to dominate today. But have you heard about the new fast food restaurant they just opened in Sunderland? It's all the rage with the youngsters. Foot-longs and proper Northern chicken parma! Can you imagine it? I'd be all over that, especially if it means lazy Sunday afternoons with good food and the match on TV. But fast food from a place with your roots must be quite different than anything available here. Do you ever miss the Northern places when you're in Cambridge? All the time! Even though Cambridge is lovely, sometimes I want a proper Greggs or a decent chippy. You know, food you can actually get excited about, not just things that are good for you. I can't say I blame you. I remember when I was in Birmingham, there were plenty of places that only had the Midlands specials, like balti or anything from the Balti Triangle. The food culture is so different up North. It is! I used to think the food up North was all about pies and fish and chips, but it's so much more diverse than people give it credit for. You've got all sorts of international influences too in cities like Newcastle because of the docks. Shows how little I knew, I guess! But speaking of food, doesn't your family still have a spot for Coronation Street? Absolutely, we've been watching that since I was a kid. My mom still gets into it the most, though. Every time a character from the North gets a storyline, she's like "That's right, lass!" My family was always more into EastEnders, and honestly, it's great to see more changing demographics on screen. But I think football brings out a universal sort of northern pride, doesn't it? Definitely. I mean, just look at the stadium today - so much support for the North! And if we win today, it'll be all the sweeter knowing we're strengthening the regional rivalry. There's something deeply satisfying about having a local team to cheer for.

Ah, good morning everyone. Lovely to see you both. How have you been today? Mum, are you feeling okay after all this rain? Morning dear! Yes, I'm doing well. Just a bit cold. Still, now, the rain, it’s kind of nice to have some rain after days and days of nothing. Reminds me of when you were younger, out playing in the puddles. Oh I know! You always used to set up a dam in the front garden and watch it overflow when it rained heavily. You were always so excited about that, Mum. True! I was quite the pint-sized project manager back then. Sent your Dad to run down to the shop for more plastic bags to build a better dam! Ah, bless his heart. Little mastermind already back then! So, what have you been getting up to lately? Work been good? Yeah, it's been busy as usual. Just managed a major project handover last week so a bit of a breather this week before the next one comes along. How about you, Mum? You've been keeping busy with your own things? Stitching and knitting mostly. Can't really go out as much now, so I manage to keep myself busy with that. Can't wait for summer though, always love the garden. I know, the garden really needs some sunshine, doesn’t it? Although I do have my own bit of "proper" gardening to do doesn’t come close to what you two have achieved over the years. Well, if one’s to do things properly, it’s done by the measured hand of a grandmother, I’m sure! You always matched Dad’s efforts with a tray of freshly baked scones when we were up here. Oh, but of course! Can’t let the boys go out working on things without some proper sustenance to keep them going. I still remember the endless cups of tea, scones, and fruit cake when I came over as a teenager. Those were the days! Yeah, definitely great times. Speaking of which, I was thinking of getting my old bike out. I started to clear out my garage and got a bit nostalgic. How is your “treasure trove” doing? Are you still restoring that vintage car? Oh, it’s still sitting there waiting to be finished. Truth be told, it’s taken a bit longer than I expected.

Alright, who's excited about Pancake Day today? It's been ages since we've had such a proper feast together. Pancake Day! I can't wait to make my own pancake. How many do we get, Mummy? Pancake Day! Pancake Day! Pancakes, right? Yes, pancakes. But before we get stuck into them, shall we discuss what we would like to do this weekend? We were thinking of going to the Science Museum. Yay, Science Museum! I really want to see the London bus that's just like the one in our city. And can we go to the beach too? I want to build sandcastles. Well, you guys want a lot! Perhaps we can plan a fun-filled weekend with a visit to the Science Museum, then maybe a little beach visit if the weather holds up. And this afternoon, we will try and help out those children in class or even reach out to any that might need a helping hand. You both know that some children don't always have the chance to eat properly or enjoy extra special fun days like today, while others may have too many choices. It's important to make sure everyone has a chance to enjoy simple pleasures like Pancake Day. Ah, right. The kids who might be hungry or feel left out. We should bring some extra in class, maybe? That's a very thoughtful idea. What do you both think? We could ask the class helpers to see who would like to share their treats with others. Yeah! And while we're on the topic of helping others, do you remember when we read those Green Knowe stories? How the children weren't just about their own fun, but also about looking out for others. Exactly! Now, while we're figuring out what and how to help, let's make sure we also set an example by finishing our food. It’s a good practice to clean up after ourselves and to appreciate what we're given. Oh, and wait! Did we finally decide on going to see the light show in the Festival Hall? That's almost as much as pancakes in the list of things to do! We can pencil that in if the time works out. Let's just get through the pancakes first. But yes, to sum up: Science Museum, beach, maybe Festival Hall, and helping... helping lots of people feels good, doesn’t it?

Who knew I'd spend my Monday evening discussing Bob the Builder's film career over Chinese? [The group laughs] Well, let's say this choice of film beat arguing over who's turn it is to do the dishes. [Laughter again] Did anyone else find the portrayals of Bob's questions quite... humorous? Yeah, I'd totally forgotten how those little songs "Can we fix it? Hey everyone, gather round for a little Chinese New Year celebration. We have Grace and Mia here; these are two lucky dragon boys who will help us welcome the Year of the Rabbit. Speaker_2 : Is this like the one from our class? Speaker_3 : Yeah! Why are there so many ginger jars? That’s a great question, Mia! Ginger jars are used in Chinese culture to welcome good luck, especially during Chinese New Year. They contain all sorts of good things for us. Did either of you know, there are myths and legends about how these animal signs came about? Can dragons be one of those signs too? Good question again! Dragons are actually really special. They are included in the zodiac signs, but only once every 12 years. So, it doesn’t come around that often. But it’s fun to think about, even if we aren’t born in those years. So, next up, let’s get the papers and crayons out and start drawing. You can draw your favorite things about dragons or rabbits. Can we make the dragons really big? Bigger and bolder, that’s the spirit! And as you draw, I might tell you a bit more about why these Chinese New Year traditions are so important and how they are similar and different from our own traditions. Maybe I’ll draw a rabbit with a big dragon next to it.

Right, so everyone's seen Rome properly today? Yeah, today's been a whirlwind. I've never seen such noise and chaos. It's kind of overwhelming but really exciting. You two been doing much exploring? I managed to visit the Trevi Fountain this afternoon. There were loads of people, but it was fun watching everyone. You should really go before it gets dark. Who else is joining and do we need to make a reservation? I’ll check the availability and book the table, if it’s decent. We won’t want to miss it. I noticed a lot of places get really busy without reservations. Count me in. And I’ll also check the menu to see if they have some lighter options. Accentuating on Accents - did anyone else catch on to our friend's Aussie accent? Haha, yeah. It’s always a bit of a laugh when Speaker_4 starts speaking. Though, honestly, it’s such an interesting blend of Aussie and British. You could easily pick up on the Aussie tones if you listened closely. Yeah, I love hearing the different accents around here. It’s like a world tour just in one group of friends. So, what about travel plans after Rome?

Hey everyone, welcome to Rosie and Ali Bonds! I can't believe we've finally managed to all come together for this girly coffee date. Oh, I know right? True, but they'll be joining us at the hen do soon, I suppose? Yes, planning that is proving to be quite the task. It just seems like there is an endless number of activities to choose from. And then we can either do it together or at the party itself for everyone to participate. And... should we invite any of the other girls already? Good thought. I'll make a quick guest list of everyone we're considering. Maybe we can also make it a weekend thing if it works better for some of them.

Alright, so I've decided I need a holiday. We've been cooped up in the house for months and I need some fresh air. Thought maybe somewhere warm, like Spain or the Canary Islands. You've been there, right? What did you think? Yeah, I spent a weekend on Tenerife a couple of years ago. It was lovely, but make sure you book ahead if you're thinking of going in winter. It's their off-season, right? Might be able to get a good deal. And how was the food? Are there good local places to eat? Oh, the food's incredible! Even the hotel food was pretty decent. Try some delicious local seafood, or traditional Canarian dishes like Papas Arrugadas. And don't forget to try the local wine, it’s very good. Yeah, sounds right up my street. What about the locals? Are they friendly? Very friendly! Especially if you make an effort to speak some Spanish. They appreciate when you try, even if you’re not fluent. But English is also widely spoken, especially in the tourist areas. Worth a try then. I don’t mind practicing Spanish. I've been listening to some podcasts before bed, so I reckon I'll know enough to get by. That’s great! It’s always nice to learn a bit of the local language. It makes a big difference when travelling. I agree. A couple of years ago, I went to Italy and embarrassingly, I didn’t even know how to say "hello" in Italian. I relied too much on "Do you speak English?" But it's never too late to learn! And it really does enrich the experience of travelling. Plus, now with all these language learning apps, it's easier than ever to pick up a bit of conversational language. True. I've been playing around with Duolingo, actually. It's pretty addictive but effective. Good for you! You know, it's funny. My last trip abroad was to Berlin, and that was more of a city break. But now, for this holiday, I feel like I want something more relaxing. Beach, maybe some hiking, or just general chilling. Tenerife is perfect for that. It’s got those beautiful black sand beaches and breathtaking landscapes. And the Teide National Park is stunning if you're into hiking. That sounds amazing. And the hotels? How is the standard?

Ah, I'm going to make a shopping list first, I've been meaning to today. Need to pick up some vegetables and bread and perhaps some cheese for our cheese and crackers later. What are you going to do about birthday cards? We really need to get Aunty Jean's this week. Oh, yes, birthday cards. I was wondering if those numerical birthday card companies have changed at all. It used to be so easy, you just had to pick the right number. Now, they have so many designs for every decade! True. It seems like they have more options than before, but sometimes it takes a while to find the right one. I remember when I was younger, you'd only get the numerical cards with just the age and maybe a line or two. And the places you'd get them from - oh, the dusty little card shops on the high street. They seem to have disappeared now, mostly online or at the supermarket. Exactly. But I prefer going to those independent shops if I can. There's something about holding the cards and looking through their collection. I hope they still make the ones that are so plain and simple, just the number and maybe a flower or something. I'm sure they do. I found a great one last year. Was it for mum? No, it was for Uncle David. It was just his age and a simple print behind it, nice and uncluttered. I think we all still appreciate that sometimes. Speaking of simplicity, we’re always talking about getting some calendar fobs and clips over the years. I wonder if they’ve come back into fashion. I kind of hope so. There's something very comforting about knowing what day it is by looking at the fridge or the bulletin board, you know? No endless checking of phones, just a quick look. I used to love making those calendar fobs when I was teaching. The children really enjoyed making them for projects, especially in art and craft class. Art and crafts in school. I was just thinking back to how much I loved those classes. I spent hours making these intricate pieces in primary school. I remember specifically a collage I made, it was so abstract but it won a local art competition. That's brilliant! I recall when I could have kids paint, draw almost anything

Ah, I'm really enjoying the view from here, but I've been worried about our new neighbours. What have you found out about them, Speak_2? Well, we've had a few conversations here and there at the new place. From what I gather, they seem friendly enough – a couple, two young children. It's always nice to have friendly people around. You know, when we first moved to this area, I was a bit nervous too. It takes a while to get used to the new surroundings and the people. Still adjusting, of course. It's been a bit of a culture shock from management to the actual work on the floor, but I'm learning. Gardening is a great hobby! Have you seen the garden across the street from ours? It's wonderful. Maybe you can swap some ideas with them? Also, there’s a local gardening club that meets regularly at the community hall. Would you be interested? That sounds interesting and useful. I’d love to join. How about we check that out together sometime? That sounds like a good idea. And you know, there’s also a local walking group that starts at the community center just around the corner. They’re a friendly bunch, and it’s a great way to get to know more people in the area. Yes, they are. Last time I walked with them, we had a great conversation about the best places to go on a walk around here. It's lovely to explore a new area that way. I like that. Exploring on foot, it truly gives you a different perspective on the place. It also reminds me of that book I read last week, something about walking and the importance of it.

Hey mate, did you seen any of those latest gaming monitors on online? I'm really into that stuff and was thinking about getting one but clearly can't afford it right now. Oh absolutely, the ease of buying online has almost gone too far, right? It's led to a lot of impulse buying and unnecessary spending, especially around holidays and sales.

Right, so we've got a lovely day ahead of us. ANON was saying today would be a good day for that coastal walk and perhaps even stop by the new furniture store that opened up in town. Right, so I'm reading this study on the impact of job stress on cognitive health. It's really quite concerning, especially when you consider how common it is for people in professional fields to experience high levels of stress. Is that right? I can definitely relate, the pressure to perform is quite high in my field as well. Absolutely, and it's not just about "being stressed". It has real health implications, you know, actually damaging your brain and affecting memory, attention, and so on. That's depressing. It makes me wonder if my job is literally wearing me down. But it's interesting because the study also found that despite this, many of these professionals just accept it as part of the job. They don't really question whether there needs to be such a high level of stress required to do well. I think you're right. It's almost like stress has become a badge of honour - if you're stressed, it means you're working hard, right? Exactly, and I think that's really unhealthy both for individuals and for the workplaces themselves. We really need to start challenging this idea that more stress = more value. You’re right about that, but the pressure doesn't just come from the workplace; it often comes from within as well. We're always striving for more, better, or different. True, but perhaps that's where we, as individuals, need to pull back and assess: what really needs to be done? What is the minimum required to achieve what we want and still maintain our health? I mean, doesn't it seem counterproductive to work ourselves into the ground for something that might not even bring the satisfaction we expect? Definitely. That's something that needs to be measured, you know? More research and real, honest conversations about workloads are really needed. I'm also getting tired of seeing companies value "work-life balance" as just a buzzword in job ads but then expect overtime like it's nothing. You hit the nail on the head. It's a bit like they're saying, 'We value you for what you produce and if you're not pushing yourself past your limits, you're not contributing enough’. This attitude is toxic and completely neglects the long-term benefits of being well-rested and balanced. It's like the entire system needs a rethink.

Ah, I'm so glad we could all make it tonight. It's been ages. How have you all been? Stressed to the max, to be honest. No one, but I sure hope people start having more meaningful conversations over their toast. Quite right. So, speaking of toast, did anyone have a chance to try the new sourdough recipe I almost but didn’t quite attempt over the weekend? I did. Hey everyone, gather round for a second will you? I’ve got something I want to share. Sure thing, what’s up? What is it then? Are we still here to talk about food? Ah, yes, questions for food will be answered today! Specifically, I’ve been thinking about the topic of regional foods in England and how they differ. Oh, that’s interesting. I’ve noticed differences when I traveled north for my work. Exactly, and as someone from Sunderland, I’ve always wondered about the cuisine from different parts of the north – compared to where Grandad [Speaker_2] is from. Well, you’re among family here. You can ask me anything from Timperley. Great. So, for instance, how is the traditional food from up there different from where you’re from? Our traditional food is often quite plain but hearty. We had a good amount of meat stews served with potatoes and vegetables. Sounds much like the northern food I encountered. I loved it. It’s certainly very different from what we typically see down here in the south. Exactly! And then when you compare it to where I'm from, even within the north, there are differences. For example, people from Sunderland love their fish and chips, while in Timperley, perhaps it's more about traditional meat dishes. Yeah, fish and chips are legendary in Sunderland, innit? But all parts of England have their own unique culinary specialties. It's fascinating. It plays into the travel aspect too. The regions have such distinct identities, and understanding the local food can give you a real insight. Totally, and it’s not just about the food itself but the community and culture it brings along with it. Speaking of culture and community, next time you’re traveling and try some local food, you’ll notice people are generally very proud of their local produce and dishes. Definitely. I recall this time when I visited Liverpool. I tried the scouse, and it was unlike anything I had before. The story behind it was fascinating too. Right! And in Sunderland, even the way certain dishes are prepared has almost become an art form. It’s like a technique passed down through generations. That’s true. Our meat stews used to be cooked for hours in a slow cooker, so the flavors just seeped in beautifully. I suppose that’s a common trait across much of traditional English cuisine – the love for slow-cooked meals.

So, I was thinking that for next semester, we could move away from the more traditional lectures and try these more interactive group discussions instead. I've seen they've been quite popular in other faculties. What are your thoughts? I really like that idea. Especially now that the students are getting a bit older and more questions are coming up regarding real-world applications of what they're learning. Interactive discussions could help them get into more nuanced discussions that they might not have otherwise, right? Absolutely. And as lecturers, it would also provide us an opportunity to get a better sense of how our students are thinking and understanding the material, rather than just seeing how well they can recall certain facts or theories. And maybe we could incorporate some multimedia resources into these discussions as well. Videos, podcasts - any sort of media that can provide real-world examples or illustrate the point we're discussing. That's a great idea! It would make the sessions more engaging, especially if we also set up some kind of online discussion forum or group where students can continue these conversations outside of class time. I've been thinking about this too. It could actually help us get more feedback from students and maybe see issues beforehand that might arise during the discussion. We could even use some online tools to moderate these discussions while they're happening. It all sounds so exciting. I also really want to consider varying the types of questions we ask them. Perhaps some are open-ended to foster debate, while others could be more focused, summarizing-type questions to reinforce the main points of the topic. I'm all for that. I think that can also help with the students' critical thinking skills - encouraging them not just to learn the content but to think about it critically and apply it to their understanding of the world. That's the goal. I just hope the students are as enthusiastic as we are, and that the format doesn't intimidate them too much. There's definitely some risk of that, but if we're guiding the discussions well, I think they'll find it engaging and rewarding. And perhaps we could do a sort of trial run next week – a mock session before the semester begins. That’s a brilliant idea. We could even involve some student volunteers or maybe even have a small preview of what to expect at the end of the previous semester.

Ah, I'm losing patience with this coffee machine! It's costing more time today to make a decent cup than teaching algebra all day. You sound like my boss. He hates the one at our office too. But isn’t that just the point of politics and leadership? To try and change those systems. I mean, I’m not a Labour supporter or anything, but isn't wanting better something worth still thinking about?

Right, so here's what I've been thinking… Instead of making pasta from scratch today, how about we just use that instant packet stuff from the store? Are you kidding me? We’re in Italy.
